7. All fields: The custom fields configured for the Space, with a count of how many there are. Fields with no value show a dash.
8. Associated objects: CRM records linked to the task, with a count.
9. Subtasks: Tasks nested under this one, with a count and a control to add another.
10. Comments: A composer at the foot of the panel, prompting "Write a comment...".

Task detail page opened through the sidebar 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461360/original/xNTlhxHLXwloE5mJmoRkoYBmiCLthBAa9A.png?1786717975)

**Check the status**

Confirm the status reflects where the work actually is.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461352/original/yKUQI7Rhv5R4dbChAR0LGS8t1irZ6ee_HA.png?1786717975)

**Add assignee(s) to the task**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461357/original/RcxOlHkbnTVepgwqQi_O5HCR1-OUa_GsAw.png?1786717975)

**Set the priority of the task**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461358/original/7kFYzSLjMJ8zcdbxwY4vC6YJMOIWV16AXw.png?1786717975)

**Set the dates**

Choose a single date, or a range if the work spans a period. The timezone the dates are shown in appears beside them.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461355/original/ZSdcYDGRfAnx3_dPBevar1yfuDr3fSHwYQ.png?1786717975)

**Write the description**

Click into the description area and describe the work. Use the formatting toolbar for structure such as lists and emphasis. A useful habit is to state what "done" looks like, so whoever picks the task up knows when to stop. You can also add images under description.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461366/original/fILoCEgyR8cGImQ5J00aV91z3RV0xCCWuA.png?1786717976)

**Fill in the custom fields**

Open the "All fields" section and complete the fields your Space uses. Empty fields display a dash.

**Link any related CRM records**

Use the "Associated objects" section to connect the task to the records the work relates to.

**Save your changes**

Use the "Save" control on the panel to commit your edits, or "Cancel" to discard them.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461364/original/goaUBWl6SPTAdJEND9loWHGZ8RvvhwtCUQ.png?1786717976)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078887395/original/ygTcGwLyL-TQMl_qjRoxcXim6knM8IumbQ.gif?1787222608)

---

## Steps for creating a task quickly

**Open the List you want the task in**

Click the List in the left panel.

**Start a new task**

Click "Add task" in the toolbar, or "+ Add Task" at the foot of the status column you want the task to start in.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078830206/original/MRzxnbRCYyWkB7HoL-Eztvu4Y3tl51X_tg.gif?1787155013)

**Enter the task name**

Type a name that says what needs to happen. A name that describes an outcome is easier to work with than one that describes a topic.

**Set the assignee, date, and priority**

The composer offers "Add assignee", "Select date", and "Priority". Setting an assignee is worth doing straight away, because an unassigned task has no owner and is easy to lose.

**Save**

Click "Save". The task appears as a card in the column.

---

## Steps for adding a subtask

Subtasks are useful when one task has several distinct steps, especially when different people own different steps. Because a task takes only one assignee, subtasks are also how you split a piece of work across more than one person.

**Open the parent task**

Click the task card to open its detail panel.

**Find the Subtasks section**

Scroll to the "Subtasks" section near the foot of the panel. Its heading shows how many subtasks the task currently has.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461361/original/dEltK1UZRc7HA63D_159u0X8vlUF5w2_lg.png?1786717975)

**Click "Add Task"**

Enter the subtask name and save it. It appears in the list under the parent.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461351/original/3LdQMzzPLHyMjKa5-2IZoGw63NQVbaf6Dg.png?1786717975)

**Repeat for each step**

Add one subtask per step. Once a task has subtasks, its card on the board shows a subtask count, so you can see at a glance which tasks are broken down.

A Kanban card displaying its subtask count

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461353/original/TPcptAu7axjbD_hQ7z2wI0bawkwrafClmA.png?1786717975)

---

## Commenting on a task

Each task has a comment composer at the foot of its detail panel, prompting "Write a comment...". Use it to keep discussion about the work attached to the work itself rather than scattered across chat and email. 

Comment composer at the foot of a task detail panel

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078461359/original/Nx6bgSlF34g2f9wEQw1LjV-eK_6-tfMRZA.png?1786717975)

Comments support mentions, replies, image attachments, and editing after posting and deleting. 

**Linking to a Specific Task**

When you open a task, your browser address gains a task identifier. Copy that address and anyone with access to the Space will land directly on that task when they open the link. This is quicker than describing where a task lives.

---

## Moving a task to a different list

A task lives in one List, but it does not have to stay there. You can move a task to any other List, whether that List sits in the same Space or a different one.

Moving is a relocation, not a copy. Once the move completes, the task no longer appears in the List it came from - it has one home, and that home has changed.

Open the task you want to move

Choose the move option and pick the destination List

You can select a List anywhere in the workspace, including one inside a different Space.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078941651/original/ph79P9IpWuv39ATYel6hIpX9DHlcWz8exg.png?1787247504)

Confirm the status mapping if you are asked to

Statuses are configured per Space, so moving a task into a Space with a different status set means the task's current status may not exist at the destination. When that happens, you are asked to confirm which status the task should take once it arrives. Review this rather than accepting the default, because it decides which column the task lands in.

The status remapping confirmation shown when moving a task between Spaces with different status sets

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078940995/original/381mSQSTo96TFGpT6BPiqyWvpic0OddLvQ.png?1787246771)

Confirm the move

The task appears in the destination List and disappears from the original.

```
Moving between two Lists in the same Space is straightforward, because both share the same statuses and nothing needs remapping. The confirmation step only appears when the destination Space defines its statuses differently.
```

---

## Adding a task to multiple lists

Sometimes a single piece of work genuinely belongs in more than one place - a task that a delivery team and a client-facing team both need to see, for example. Rather than duplicating it and keeping two copies in sync, you can add one task to several Lists at once, within the same Space or across different ones.

This is different from moving. The task keeps its original home List and simply becomes visible in the others as well. There is still only one task, so an update made anywhere is the same update everywhere.

---

## How statuses behave

This is the part worth understanding before you start.

A task added to a second List keeps the status workflow of its home List. It does not adopt the statuses of the List it has been added to, even when that List sits in a Space with a completely different set. The home Space's workflow governs the task wherever it appears.

To make that possible, the Space containing the secondary List has the task's status added to its own status workflow. So adding a task across Spaces can introduce a new status into the destination Space's configuration.

---

## What this means for someone working in the secondary list

The consequence occurs when a colleague tries to change the task’s status to one of the statuses available in a secondary List. While the status can be selected, attempting to save the task will return an error. The task can only be moved between the statuses defined in its home List.

This is deliberate. A task has one workflow, and it is the workflow of the place it lives. Allowing it to be dragged into a status from a different Space would leave it in a stage its home team does not recognize.

The practical implication is worth telling your team in advance. If someone is working out of a List that a task was added to rather than one it lives in, they are seeing the task through a window, not holding it. They can update it, comment on it, and move it through its own stages, but the stages themselves are set elsewhere.

The error shown when attempting to set a secondary List's status on a task added from another Space

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078940987/original/eNjSuwmTt1c_5gOzjIjWew9TtiDsgyvwoA.png?1787246747)

---

## Steps for adding a task to another list

Open the task

Choose the option to add it to another List, and pick the destination

Repeat for any further Lists the task should appear in

The task now shows in every List it has been added to, while continuing to follow its home List's statuses.

```
If you want the task to genuinely leave where it started, move it instead. Adding to another List keeps the original.
```

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is the minimum I need, to create a task?**

A name and due date. Assignee and priority can all be added later, though setting an assignee early is a good habit.

**Q: Can I set a start date as well as a due date?**

Yes. The Dates control accepts either a single date or a range.

**Q: Why do some of my task fields show a dash?**

A dash means the custom field has no value yet. The fields available come from the Space the task belongs to.

**Q: What is the difference between moving a task and adding it to another list?**

Moving relocates the task, so it leaves the original List entirely. Adding to another List keeps the original home and makes the same task visible in more than one place.

**Q: Why am I being asked to confirm a status when I move a task?**

Statuses are configured per Space. If you move a task into a Space with a different status set, its current status may not exist there, so you are asked which status it should take on arrival.

**Q: If I add a task to a list in another space, which statuses does it use?**

Its home List's status workflows. The task ignores the secondary List's status set and continues to follow the workflow it started in.

**Q: Why can I not change this task's status to one of my list's statuses?**

The task lives in another List and follows that List's workflow. You can move it between its home statuses, but not into statuses belonging to the List you are viewing it from. If the task should genuinely adopt your workflow, it needs moving rather than adding.

**Q: Why has a new status appeared in my space?**

A task from another Space has been added to one of your Lists. Because the task keeps its home statuses, that status is added to your Space's workflow so it can be displayed correctly.

**Q: If I update a task in one list, does it update in the others?**

Yes. There is only one task, however many Lists it appears in.

---

## Next: [Board (Kanban) and list views](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008446-board-kanban-and-list-views)

title_en: Workflow Action - Invoke Agent Studio Agent
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/-9IEemrWoBM?&wmode=opaque)

Invoke Agent Studio Agent connects HighLevel Workflows with Agent Studio so your automation can send context to an AI agent, receive a response, and continue to the next step without custom code. This setup is useful for summaries, lead qualification, content generation, structured outputs, and workflow branching based on agent results.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Invoke Agent Studio Agent?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-Invoke-Agent-Studio-Agent?)
- [Key Benefits of Invoke Agent Studio Agent](#Key-Benefits-of-Invoke-Agent-Studio-Agent)
- [Prerequisites & Permissions](#Prerequisites-&-Permissions)
- [Workflow Action Settings](#Workflow-Action-Settings)
- [Using Agent Output Downstream](#Using-Agent-Output-Downstream)
- [Best Practices & Use Cases](#Best-Practices-&-Use-Cases)
- [How To Set Up Invoke Agent Studio Agent](#How-To-Set-Up-Invoke-Agent-Studio-Agent)
- [Add the Workflow Action](#Add-the-Workflow-Action)
- [Configure the Workflow Action](#Configure-the-Workflow-Action)
- [Select Agent (Required)](#Select-Agent-(Required))
- [Message Field (Optional but Recommended)](#Message-Field-(Optional-but-Recommended))
- [Important Configuration Notes](#Important-Configuration-Notes)
- [Configure Inputs and Save](#Configure-Inputs-and-Save)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Invoke Agent Studio Agent?**

Invoke Agent Studio Agent is a workflow action that runs a selected Agent Studio agent from inside a workflow. When the workflow reaches this step, the agent executes in the background, returns its response, and makes that output available for later workflow steps. This allows you to combine workflow logic with agent reasoning, generated content, and structured data in one connected process.  

---

## **Key Benefits of Invoke Agent Studio Agent**

Using an agent inside a workflow helps you move from simple automation to decision-based automation. It is especially helpful when a workflow needs to analyze context, create a response, classify information, or return structured output that later steps can use.

- **AI-powered workflow execution**: Run an Agent Studio agent at a specific point in your workflow and continue the automation with the returned result.

- **Flexible data handling**: Send instructions through the Message field, map workflow data into input variables, and reuse the response in later actions.

- **Better downstream automation**: Use agent output in emails, internal notifications, field updates, If/Else branches, and webhooks.

- **Structured decision-making**: Return machine-readable JSON from the agent to support cleaner branching and more dependable automation logic.

- **Scalable operational workflows**: Apply the same workflow pattern to lead enrichment, summaries, routing, follow-up preparation, and record updates across sub-accounts.

---

## **Prerequisites & Permissions**

A smooth setup depends on having the right access and building the agent for the correct entry point before adding it to a workflow. Verifying these requirements early helps prevent confusion when the agent does not appear in the workflow action.

Before using this action, confirm the following:

- You have an active AI Employee add-on with access to Agent Studio.
- The agent is published to Production. Draft or Staging versions do not appear in the workflow action selector.
- You have permission to edit workflows and AI agents in the location.

```
Important: 

Build the agent with the Workflows trigger when the goal is to run that agent from the Invoke Agent Studio Agent workflow action. This trigger is designed for agents that need to be launched directly by a workflow, making it easier to pass inputs correctly, receive the agent’s response, and use that output in later steps.
```

---

## **Workflow Action Settings**

Each setting in the action panel controls what the agent receives and how the workflow can use the result afterward. Understanding these fields helps you build actions that are easier to test, easier to troubleshoot, and more useful in downstream automation.

The action includes these core settings:

- **Agent**: Select the Production agent you want the workflow to run.

- **Message**: Add free-text instructions for the run. You can use merge fields to send contact-specific or workflow-specific context.

- **Input Variables**: Map workflow values or static text to the agent’s named inputs. Missing required inputs can stop the action from completing successfully.

- **Store Output As**: Save the full agent response as a custom value for later workflow steps.

---

## **Using Agent Output Downstream**

The value of this action comes from what happens after the agent responds. Saving and reusing the output lets the workflow make smarter decisions, personalize communications, and send richer data to later actions or outside systems.

Common downstream uses include:

- Save the summary or result to a custom field or note.

- Branch with If/Else logic using values returned by the agent.

- Insert the response into Email, SMS, WhatsApp, or internal notifications.

- Send the full response object to a webhook or external service.

- Reference the response in later workflow steps using the agent response variable documented in the action article.

---

## **Best Practices & Use Cases**

Well-structured agent actions are easier to maintain and produce more consistent results. Clear prompts, mapped variables, and structured outputs help reduce errors while making the workflow easier for teams to understand and improve over time.

Best practices:

- Keep prompts concise and provide detailed context through mapped variables when possible.

- Ask the agent to return structured JSON when the result will be used for branching or field updates.

- Rename each action clearly if the workflow uses more than one agent.

- Test the agent’s expected output format before using it in important downstream actions. Agent Studio supports testing and debugging so you can review agent behavior before broader use.

- Publish agent changes to Production before expecting them to appear in the workflow action.

Example use cases:

- Lead enrichment after a form submission

- Conversation summaries after a chat is closed

- Sales triage based on the latest inquiry

- Internal handoff notes for service teams

- Structured output sent to webhooks or external tools

---

## **How To Set Up Invoke Agent Studio Agent**

Proper setup starts in Agent Studio and finishes in the workflow builder. Building the agent for workflow invocation first helps ensure the action can locate the correct agent and return a response that later steps can use reliably.

Build the Agent in Agent Studio

The trigger you choose determines how the agent starts. For this use case, the agent should be built for workflow invocation so the workflow can intentionally launch it, pass input data, and receive a response back for later actions. HighLevel’s trigger guide explains that trigger types define how agents start in response to specific events or entry points.

### **Navigate to **Agent Studio**.**

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068814869/original/7fVjMJU6TsdbZ_dPLMIFndbQ00Ljgm5r5w.png?1775748679)**

Click **Create Agent**, or open an existing agent you want to use. 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068815539/original/w-XD_ReNCv9eboynIXAS5tXH4IEZe6LgcQ.png?1775748983)

In the trigger selection panel, choose **Workflows**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068815348/original/n92qFgRgadhcircZnVRDPnSuD7TH-Xo9Zg.png?1775748910)

Configure the agent’s instructions, tools, and input variables based on the data you want to pass from the workflow. HighLevel’s Agent Studio documentation explains that variables can be used to personalize inputs and build reusable agents.

Test the agent and confirm the output format matches your workflow needs. HighLevel’s Agent Studio documentation and overview emphasize testing and iteration as part of agent setup.  

Click **Publish to Production**. Only Production-published agents are available in the workflow action selector.  

---

## **Add the Workflow Action**

Adding the action places the agent directly into your automation path. This makes it possible to combine normal workflow logic with an agent’s response in the same sequence of actions.

Navigate to **Automation > Workflows**. HighLevel’s workflow documentation explains that workflows are built from triggers and actions.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068816667/original/XyaIrDMqV3s1wRBAeV9fP5lPUFHiEsnS9Q.jpeg?1775749571)**

Open an existing workflow or create a new one.

Click **+ Add Action**.

Under **Agent Studio**, select **Invoke Agent Studio Agent**. The current HighLevel article confirms that this action appears in the workflow action selector.  

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068817052/original/egUNVtG2pvIlxYIUGmrCV7Es8heQcea4rw.png?1775749746)**

---

## **Configure the Workflow Action**

The configuration panel controls which agent runs, what the workflow sends to it, and how the returned data is stored. Careful setup here helps the workflow behave consistently and keeps later actions easier to manage.

### **Action Name**

A clear action name makes the workflow easier to read, especially when several AI steps appear in the same automation. This field does not change agent behavior, but it improves organization and troubleshooting.

Examples:

- Lead Message Analyzer
- AI Summary Step
- Sales Insight Generator

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068817183/original/hIYXvDxK3eupJ2T-VACkUMh-gIeSB9aNXQ.png?1775749793)**

---

## **Select Agent (Required)**

The Select Agent dropdown is where you choose the agent the workflow should run. Production status matters here because only Production-published agents are available in the selector.  

Choose the agent you want to run in this workflow.

If the correct agent does not appear:

- Confirm it is published to **Production**.

- Confirm it was built with the **Workflows** trigger for this use case.

- Refresh the builder and reopen the action if needed.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068817296/original/0MfHPCtRgx-zmQkcGH8Gy7wr1rD8eO5lDw.png?1775749841)**

---

## **Message Field (Optional but Recommended)**

The Message field helps define what the agent should do when the workflow reaches this step. This is useful when you want the same agent to handle different instructions depending on where it is used. The action article confirms that this field accepts free text and can use merge fields for dynamic values.  

Example:

Analyze the contact’s last inbound message and provide a short summary along with recommended next actions for the sales team.

Example with personalization:

Analyze the most recent message from {{contact.name}} and provide a short summary along with recommended next actions for the sales team.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068817956/original/pi65Rj8u1xAPFjWnyIGApsv0b9jwzIWOAg.png?1775750162)**

---

## **Important Configuration Notes**

Reliable setup depends on accurate mapping and clear expectations for what the agent returns. Paying attention to required variables and stored output helps prevent failed runs and makes the response easier to use later.

- Required input variables defined in the agent must be mapped correctly.

- Missing required inputs can cause the action to fail.

- The agent runs when the workflow reaches this step.

- The response is available for downstream use through the documented agent response object.

- Use **Store Output As** when you want to save the full response for later workflow steps.

---

## **Configure Inputs and Save**

Mapping inputs correctly ensures the workflow sends the right context every time the action runs. Saving the full output can also make later actions easier to configure.

1. Map each required input variable.
2. Add optional instructions in the Message field.
3. Choose **Store Output As** if you want to save the full response.
4. Click **Save Action**.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why doesn’t my agent appear in the dropdown?**

Only eligible agents appear in the selector. Confirm the agent is published to Production, belongs to the current sub-account, and is built for workflow invocation. HighLevel’s current action article confirms the Production requirement.  

**Q: Can one workflow call multiple agents?**

Yes. You can add multiple Invoke Agent Studio Agent actions in the same workflow and place them sequentially or in separate branches.  

**Q: What happens if the agent errors out?**

The action fails and the error appears in the workflow log. HighLevel’s current article recommends handling failures through workflow logic when needed.  

**Q: Are additional AI credits consumed?**

HighLevel’s current action article states that agent runs use the same metering as when the agent is run from Agent Studio, with no separate workflow surcharge.  

**Q: Is there a timeout?**

Yes. HighLevel’s current action article states that agents must respond within 60 seconds.  

**Q: Can I test this in a Draft workflow?**

Yes. HighLevel’s current article states that the action can be tested in Draft mode, and contacts process once the workflow is published.  

**Q: How do I troubleshoot variable mapping issues?**

Review the workflow’s execution log and compare it with the inputs and outputs shown in Agent Studio testing or logs. HighLevel’s Agent Studio documentation includes testing and debugging guidance.  

**Q: What type of output should the agent return?**

Return plain text when the result will be inserted into a message or note. Return structured JSON when the result will be used in branching, updates, or downstream integrations. This aligns with the downstream usage patterns described in HighLevel’s current action article.  

---

### **Related Articles**

- **[How to Use the AI Agent Studio in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000006058?portalId=48000045315)**
- **[Ask AI + Agent Studio Integration](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000006677?portalId=48000045315)**
- **[How to Set Up Agent Studio Triggers for Real-Time Starts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000007310?portalId=48000045315)**

title_en: Funnel & Website AI
source_md:
Funnel & Website AI is HighLevel’s AI-powered page creation and editing experience for funnel and website pages. It can generate pages from prompts, guided inputs, URLs, and images, then help you continue refining the page through conversational requests.

You can revise existing content and design, add new sections, or regenerate selected parts of the page while keeping standard builder controls available for manual refinement. This gives both beginners and experienced builders a faster way to create and iteratively improve pages without starting from scratch.

---

[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/t5Y3tJZcZ64?&wmode=opaque)

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Funnel & Website AI?](#What-is-Funnel-&-Website-AI?)
- [Key Benefits of Funnel & Website AI](#Key-Benefits-of-Funnel-&-Website-AI)
- [Choose Your AI Creation Path: Assist or Build](#Choose-Your-AI-Creation-Path%3A-Assist-or-Build)
  - [1. Assist](#1.-Assist)
  - [2. Build](#2.-Build)
- [Chat Mode and Side-by-Side Editing](#Chat-Mode-and-Side-by-Side-Editing)
- [Import from a Link or Image](#Import-from-a-Link-or-Image)
- [AI-Powered SEO Suggestions](#AI-Powered-SEO-Suggestions)
- [How To Use Funnel & Website AI](#How-To-Use-Funnel-&-Website-AI)
- [Important Notes](#Important-Notes)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What is Funnel & Website AI?**

Funnel & Website AI is HighLevel’s AI-powered page creation experience for building funnel and website pages from prompts, guided inputs, URLs, and images. It helps users generate layouts, copy, visuals, and page structure more quickly while still keeping builder controls available for manual refinement. This matters because it gives both beginners and experienced builders a faster way to launch polished pages without starting from scratch.

**Available Funnel & Website AI Tools:**

| Path/Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Assist | Helps users generate pages with guided presets and structured inputs such as business niche, goal, audience, tone, and layout preferences. |
| Build | Gives users more creative freedom by letting them describe exactly what they want the AI to create. |
| Chat-based editing | Makes it easier to update copy, sections, layout ideas, and design direction in real time while working inside the page builder. |
| Ask AI + Settings Side-by-Side | Keeps AI assistance and builder controls close together so users can refine content and styling without constantly switching views. |
| Import from a Link or Image | Helps users create pages inspired by a public URL or image reference. |
| SEO Support | Helps generate page titles, descriptions, and content suggestions that support stronger page optimization. |

---

## **Key Benefits of Funnel & Website AI**

Funnel & Website AI helps users move from an initial idea to a refined page faster. Its conversational editing tools also make it easier to improve specific parts of a page without rebuilding unaffected content.

- **Faster page creation:** Generate page structure, copy, visuals, and layout direction without starting from scratch.
- **Guided or flexible creation:** Choose structured Assist inputs or describe exactly what you want with Build.
- **Granular AI revisions:** Revise copy, theme, or design at the section or page level, or regenerate content when a broader change is needed.
- **Add new sections:** Insert new sections, such as pricing, testimonials, or FAQs, without regenerating the rest of the page.
- **Builder-native editing:** Continue adjusting AI-applied styling, including colors and typography, with standard builder controls.
- **Background generation:** Page generation can continue even after you close the browser or temporarily lose your connection.
- **Reference-based generation:** Use links or images to provide visual or structural direction.
- **SEO assistance:** Generate SEO suggestions that you can review and refine before publishing.

---

## **Choose Your AI Creation Path: Assist or Build**

Funnel & Website AI gives users two primary ways to create a funnel page, depending on how much guidance or control they want. Choosing the right path at the start helps generate more relevant results and makes the building process smoother from the beginning. The current HighLevel experience presents these two paths directly inside the Ask AI panel.

| Mode | Best For |
| --- | --- |
| **Assist** | Users who want guided inputs and help shaping the page |
| **Build** | Users who know what they want and prefer direct prompting |

### **1. Assist**

Assist is the guided path for users who want HighLevel to help shape the page before generation. It uses structured inputs like the funnel page name, business niche, page goal, target audience, and offer details to create a more tailored starting point. This option is especially helpful when you want direction, want to move quickly, or are not sure how to phrase a detailed prompt yourself.

Users can fill in fields such as:

- Name of the funnel page
- Business niche
- Goal of the funnel page
- Target audience
- What is being offered

Once those details are entered, users can generate the page directly or continue customizing before generation.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068214474/original/H2zQrvTrNAOPKiZBSWSvYiyHCbuh51Arbw.png?1775029087)

### **2. Build**

Build is the flexible path for users who already have a clear vision for the funnel. Instead of following guided fields, users can type a direct request and ask the AI to plan, build, or modify the page based on their instructions. This is ideal for users who want more creative freedom, have a specific campaign structure in mind, or want to describe copy and design direction in their own words.

Build also includes suggested prompt starters to help users move faster, such as creating a high-converting funnel or improving copy for impact.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068214751/original/jl4JD-3FexCFb8BEUXvgZhLzO2XYSRZ37g.png?1775029135)

---

## **Chat Mode and Side-by-Side Editing**

Chat-based editing helps you refine an existing page without manually rebuilding each element. Use conversational requests to target the type of change you want while keeping the standard builder controls available alongside the AI experience.

You can ask Funnel & Website AI to make several types of changes:

- **Revise copy:** Update messaging in a section or across the page while keeping the broader design intact.
- **Revise the theme:**Adjust the visual theme while preserving the existing content.
- **Redesign:**Change the design of a specific section or the full page when you want a different visual direction.
- **Regenerate:** Create a new version of a section or page when broader changes are needed.
- **Add a new section:** Insert new content, such as a pricing table, testimonial section, or FAQ section, without regenerating the rest of the page.

AI-applied colors and typography remain editable through the standard builder controls. You can continue using those controls alongside chat-based changes to fine-tune the final result.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068221672/original/auRTH86u5knB0UoTFhkf82rty5m0t-figQ.png?1775032416)  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068221733/original/BtriuDeUWtECYgb4ExwFDGy__x0SBhHEKA.png?1775032439)

---

## **Import from a Link or Image**

Import from a link or image helps users create pages inspired by an existing visual reference. This can be useful when you want to capture a style, structure, or creative direction without starting from zero.

Users can use this workflow to:

- Take inspiration from a public webpage
- Recreate the feel of a design direction
- Build around a brand style shown in an image
- Speed up ideation when they already know the look they want

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068222195/original/6AiqWx9_gqqzwDhVDqAhG_IvvOJ44BTKRw.png?1775032573)

```
Important: Importing from a link or image provides the AI with a reference for generating the page. It does not create an exact clone of the original page or guarantee that every design element, layout, interaction, or piece of content will be reproduced.
```

---

## **AI-Powered SEO Suggestions**

Funnel & Website AI can help users move faster on SEO by generating suggested titles, descriptions, and content direction during page creation. That gives users a stronger starting point when preparing a page for search visibility.

AI-generated SEO suggestions should still be reviewed before publishing. This matters because page goals, brand language, and search intent may require manual refinement.

Helpful follow-up tasks after AI generation:

- Review the page title for clarity and relevance
- Refine the meta description for search intent
- Confirm headings match the page purpose
- Update page copy to reflect your brand voice
- Add any custom metadata needed before publishing

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068222370/original/_tnew_AwdU0o81teGxdeHVlhVlDqf4lZLA.png?1775032685)

```
Note: AI-generated SEO content is a starting point. Review page titles, descriptions, headings, keywords, and page copy for accuracy, search intent, and brand relevance before publishing.
```

---

## **How To Use Funnel & Website AI**

A strong setup process helps users get better first-generation results and reduces the need for excessive edits later. Starting with the right mode, inputs, and expectations makes the AI output more relevant and easier to refine.

1. Navigate to **Sites**→ **Funnels**or**Websites** in your HighLevel sub-account. Click **Build with AI** to create a new funnel or website asset OR Open an existing Website or Funnel.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068222784/original/Ghr7x1RQlfjTMyo0XjXQlLH38rZirK3d_g.png?1775032966)
2. Choose your AI creation path:  
     
   After opening the AI experience, use **Assist** or **Build** to create the initial page. Once inside the builder, use the available AI chat alongside standard builder controls to refine the generated page.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068224821/original/_-cLLM6lPyMDjQlFeK_9x2Ar53bWzNxZrg.png?1775033924)
3. If you choose **Assist**, enter your funnel page name, business niche, page goal, target audience, and offer details.  
     
   If you choose **Build**, enter a detailed prompt that explains the page purpose, audience, messaging, and desired style.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068224868/original/T2HaGKnHAzr1IPmm2Fpa9JXKx9xH8Pctew.png?1775033947)
4. Use **Ask AI**chat and the builder settings to refine the page. You can request changes to copy, theme, or design, regenerate a section or page, or ask AI to add a new section without rebuilding the rest of the page.

   Continue using the standard builder controls when you want to manually adjust content, colors, typography, images, spacing, or other supported page settings.

   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068224485/original/KXmqtrhEJnhchaQ_btT5-K9uM783fi700Q.png?1775033755)
5. Review the page’s SEO fields, then complete any final edits before publishing.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068224668/original/AFeRYbwBJ0RYL9Q8jwJJn_hpDVECAQemmw.gif?1775033842)
6. Publish the page once your content, layout, and settings are ready.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068225013/original/5wDENthA4zejrgj3bHeb2I1Ci5HeOLyRmg.png?1775034037)

---

## **Important Notes**

- **Review AI-generated content before publishing:** Verify generated copy, claims, contact information, offers, links, images, and other business-specific information for accuracy.
- **Reference-based generation is not exact cloning:** A link or image provides creative and structural direction but does not guarantee an identical reproduction.
- **SEO suggestions require review:** AI-generated titles, descriptions, and content suggestions should be refined for your target audience, search intent, and brand.
- **You can continue editing manually:** AI-generated pages remain editable using the standard Funnel and Website Builder controls.
- **Check current AI usage limits:** Funnel & Website AI is currently available without additional AI usage charges, subject to usage limits. Refer to the[AI Product Pricing article](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006652-ai-product-pricing) for current details.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: When should I use Assist instead of Build?**  
Use Assist when you want a guided starting point and would benefit from presets or structured inputs. Use Build when you already have a clear page concept and want to describe it directly.

**Q. Can Funnel & Website AI edit an existing page?**

Yes. The current article explicitly allows users to open an existing Funnel or Website and use AI tools to refine it.

**Q: Does importing from a link or image work the same way as cloning a funnel or website?**  
No. AI reference-based creation is best treated as inspiration-driven generation.

**Q: Can I still manually edit the page after AI generates it?**  
Yes. The AI experience is meant to speed up creation, but users can continue refining the page using chat-based edits and standard builder settings.

**Q: Will the AI-generated SEO content be enough on its own?**  
It is a strong starting point, but it should still be reviewed for accuracy, search intent, and brand voice before publishing. HighLevel also supports manual metadata updates.

**Q: Do I need design experience to use Funnel & Website AI?**  
No. One of the main benefits of the tool is that it reduces design complexity by generating layouts, copy, and page structure for you.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [AI Product Pricing Update](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006652-ai-product-pricing-update)
- [Websites Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001633-websites-overview)
- [AI Employee Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003906)

title_en: Add Custom Templates to Template Library
source_md:
Template Library • Agency Admin • Reusable Assets

Add Custom Templates to the HighLevel Template Library

HighLevel's Template Library lets agencies turn reusable assets into templates that can be shared across supported sub-accounts and product areas. Agency Admins can create templates centrally from Agency View or upload supported assets directly from individual HighLevel products. Templates can include categories, tags, descriptions, previews, cover images, and prerequisites to make reusable assets easier to discover and understand. This guide explains how to create, upload, configure, save, publish, and control access to custom templates.

What You'll Learn

Learn the requirements for creating custom templates, how to create templates centrally from Agency View, how supported products upload reusable assets, how to configure template information, how Draft and Published templates behave, and how to control Template Library visibility for sub-accounts.

Important

Creating new custom templates requires an **Agency Admin** on the **$497/month Pro plan**. Agency Admins on the $97 Starter and $297 Unlimited plans can browse the Agency Template Library and use supported visibility-management features, but they cannot create new custom templates.

# What Is a Custom Template in the Template Library?

A custom template is a reusable asset an agency adds to its HighLevel Template Library. Published templates can be made available to sub-accounts so users can start with agency-approved content or configurations instead of rebuilding the same asset from scratch.

The Template Library supports multiple HighLevel product areas. Available template types and creation options vary by product, so use the product choices and upload actions displayed in your account to confirm whether a specific asset type is supported.

## Key Benefits of Custom Templates

Custom templates help agencies standardize reusable assets, reduce repetitive setup, and make proven content easier for sub-account users to discover and reuse.

- **Reuse Proven Assets:** Turn existing agency content into reusable templates across supported product areas.
- **Create Centrally:** Build Template Library entries directly from Agency View without repeatedly switching between sub-accounts.
- **Maintain Consistency:** Give sub-accounts access to agency-approved designs, content, and configurations.
- **Improve Discoverability:** Add categories, tags, descriptions, previews, cover images, and prerequisites to make templates easier to understand and find.
- **Control Publication:** Keep templates in Draft while preparing them, then publish them when they are ready for use.
- **Manage Visibility:** Control which templates and categories appear for sub-accounts.

## Prerequisites and Limitations

Confirming your agency plan, permissions, Template Library visibility, and source asset before creating a template helps prevent missing controls or inaccessible templates later.

Before creating a custom template, confirm:

- Your agency is on the **$497/month Pro plan** to create new custom templates.
- You are signed in with an **Agency Admin** role.
- Template Library access is enabled when sub-account users need to browse published templates.
- The source asset already exists when you want to create a template from an existing sub-account asset.

### Enable the Template Library for Clients

The agency-level Template Library setting controls whether clients can access the library. Enable it before expecting published templates to appear in supported sub-account experiences.

1. From **Agency View**, open **Settings**.
2. Select **Company**.
3. Scroll to **Template Library for Clients**.
4. Turn on the toggle when sub-account users should have access to templates.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081372038/original/xyhUsYPGBBAbYNmeZ6GMDskbtMSs1uU5qA.png?1789851933)

**$97 and $297 plans:** Agency Admins on these plans can browse the Agency Template Library and use supported visibility controls such as hiding templates or categories. Creating new custom templates still requires the $497 Pro plan.

### Understand Source Template Updates

Changes made to the original source asset do not automatically update an already published Template Library template. Treat the published template as its own reusable asset and review it separately when the original content changes.

## How To Create a Custom Template from Agency View

Creating a template centrally from Agency View lets an Agency Admin select an existing sub-account asset, preview it, rename it, and create a reusable Template Library entry without navigating through the source product first.

### Step 1: Start the Template

Start from the agency Template Library so the source sub-account and product can be selected from one centralized creation flow.

1. From **Agency View**, open **Template Library**.
2. Click **+ Create template**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081372045/original/SnWRzTygzTJ-3XFH4sxBu5q2-gfQhv-cOA.png?1789851971)

### Step 2: Select the Source Asset

Selecting the source sub-account and product type tells HighLevel which existing assets should be available for the new template.

1. Select the **sub-account** containing the source asset.
2. Select the applicable **product**.
3. Choose the template or source asset.
4. Click **Continue**.

### Step 3: Preview, Rename, and Create

Previewing the source asset gives you a final opportunity to confirm that the correct template was selected before creating the reusable Template Library entry.

1. Review the template preview.
2. Open the preview if you need to inspect the asset more closely.
3. Rename the template if needed.
4. Click **Create**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081372051/original/HO0Mjh0rkhg5xoA_d3Kh5Y5XjzmTbSCL-g.png?1789852010)

After the template is created, HighLevel opens the Template Library management experience so you can update template details, save it as a Draft, or publish it for reuse.

## How To Upload a Template from a Product

Supported HighLevel products can send an existing asset directly to the Template Library. The exact upload action varies by product, but the workflow generally starts from the asset's three-dot menu and continues in Template Library admin mode.

| Product | Starting Area | Upload Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Email Templates** | Marketing → Emails → Templates | **Upload to email templates** |
| **Social Planner** | Marketing → Social Planner → Content → CSV | **Upload to social templates** |
| **Workflows** | Automation → Workflows | **Upload to Template Library** |
| **Supported Sites Assets** | Sites → Select supported product | **Upload to [product] templates** |
| **Ad Manager** | Marketing → Ad Manager | **Upload to Template Library** |
| **Custom Reports** | Reporting → Custom Reports | **Upload Report Template** |

### Upload an Email Template

Email templates can be uploaded directly from the Email Marketing template list, allowing established designs to become reusable Template Library assets.

1. From the sub-account, go to **Marketing → Emails → Templates**.
2. Locate the email template you want to reuse.
3. Open the template's **three-dot action menu**.
4. Select **Upload to email templates**.
5. Enter a display name.
6. Select a category.
7. Click **Upload**.

### Upload Social Planner Content

Social Planner lets Agency Admins upload supported reusable content to the Template Library directly from the Content area.

1. From the sub-account, go to **Marketing → Social Planner**.
2. Open **Content**.
3. Open the **CSV** tab or another supported Template Library content area.
4. Locate the content you want to reuse.
5. Open its **three-dot action menu**.
6. Select **Upload to social templates**.
7. Enter the template name and select a category.
8. Continue to Template Library admin mode to complete the template information.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081372055/original/3GVRwpcSvBc8D8Wj1bgRXVxz5G0gCf83og.png?1789852060)

### Upload an Ad Manager Campaign

Supported Ad Manager campaigns can be saved as reusable templates. After upload, the campaign is created as a Draft template so its information can be reviewed before publication.

1. From the sub-account, go to **Marketing → Ad Manager**.
2. Open the campaign list.
3. Locate the supported campaign you want to reuse.
4. Open the campaign's **ellipsis (⋮)** menu.
5. Select **Upload to Template Library**.
6. Enter the template name.
7. Select a category.
8. Click **Upload**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081372106/original/hec53v-VpSfuCv2wWD8tQZqhSUZuDLp7yA.png?1789852526)

**Ad Manager Drafts:** Uploaded supported campaigns are saved as Draft templates. You can edit the template, keep it as a Draft, or publish it for reuse.

### Upload a Custom Report

Custom Reports require an additional permissions and cleanup step before upload so the reusable report works across sub-accounts without exposing client-specific information.

1. From the sub-account, go to **Reporting → Custom Reports**.
2. Locate the completed report on **Reports Overview**.
3. Open the report's **three-dot menu**.
4. Select **Manage permissions**.
5. Grant at least Read access to **Agency User**, **Account Admin**, and **Account User**.
6. Finalize the reusable layout, branding, page order, date ranges, and widget settings.
7. Replace client-specific text, screenshots, or other information with reusable content.
8. Return to the report's **three-dot menu**.
9. Select **Upload Report Template**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081372104/original/kSGhT6HNq5U1tqq-dQ3UH0ozuluIWbu77A.png?1789852505)

### Other Supported Product Uploads

Additional supported product areas can also upload reusable assets to the Template Library. The exact menu label varies based on the product.

- **Workflows:** Go to Automation → Workflows, open the workflow's three-dot menu, and select **Upload to Template Library**.
- **Sites Products:** For supported funnels, websites, stores, blogs, emails, forms, surveys, and quizzes, open the asset's three-dot menu and use the available **Upload to [product] templates** action.

## How To Configure and Publish a Template

Template information helps sub-account users understand what an asset contains, what is required before using it, and when it is appropriate for their use case. Complete the available metadata before publishing.

### Complete the Template Information

The available fields can vary by product, but Template Library admin mode can include the following information.

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Name** | The display name shown in the Template Library. |
| **Category** | Groups the template with related content. |
| **Preview** | Helps users inspect the template before using it. |
| **Cover Image** | Provides a thumbnail or visual representation of the template. |
| **Tags** | Adds searchable terms that improve template discovery. |
| **Prerequisites** | Identifies setup requirements needed before users apply the template. |
| **Short Description** | Provides a brief summary displayed with the template. |
| **Long About** | Provides detailed use cases, setup guidance, content tips, feature information, or other helpful context. |

### Save the Template as a Draft

Draft status keeps the template available for administrative editing without making it available for normal sub-account use.

1. Review the template information.
2. Complete the metadata you want included.
3. Save your changes.
4. Keep the template in **Draft** until it is ready for users.

### Publish the Template

Publishing makes the finished template available through the applicable Template Library experience for sub-account users who have access.

1. Review the template name, category, preview, prerequisites, descriptions, and other available information.
2. Save any outstanding changes.
3. Click **Publish Template**.
4. Confirm publication when prompted.

### Control Template Library Visibility by Sub-Account

Agency Admins can customize which templates and categories appear for individual sub-accounts. This helps agencies show only the assets that are relevant to a client's needs, niche, or plan.

1. From **Agency View**, open **Template Library**.
2. Open **Settings**.
3. Select **Customize for Subaccounts**.
4. Locate the sub-account you want to manage and click **Edit**.
5. Hide or show templates and categories as needed.
6. Click **Save**.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who can create custom templates?

Custom template creation requires the **Agency Admin** role and an agency on the **$497/month Pro plan**.

Q: Can Agency Admins on the $97 or $297 plans create custom templates?

No. Agency Admins on those plans can browse the Template Library and use supported visibility-management features, but creating new custom templates requires the $497 Pro plan.

Q: Can I create a template without opening the source product first?

Yes. Go to **Agency View → Template Library → + Create template**, then choose the source sub-account, product, and source template.

Q: Do I have to publish a template immediately?

No. Supported templates can remain in **Draft** while you review and complete their information before making them available to sub-account users.

Q: Do changes to the original source asset automatically update a published template?

No. Changes made to the original source asset do not automatically flow through to the corresponding published Template Library template.

Q: Can I control which sub-accounts see templates?

Yes. Agency Admins can customize Template Library access by sub-account and hide or show templates and categories as needed.

Q: Are all HighLevel products available for custom template creation?

No. Template availability and upload options vary by product. Use the current product choices and upload actions displayed in your account to confirm whether an asset type is supported.

Q: Can I sell a custom template?

Eligible templates can be submitted through the connected Template Library Marketplace workflow. From the template preview, use **Sell Template On The Marketplace**, continue to the Seller Portal, complete the required listing, support, and pricing information, and submit the template for review.

title_en: Dog Groomer - Service Calendar Setup Guide
source_md:
Recognizing the significance of ***Service Calendars*** becomes imperative when dealing with a range of services that necessitate diverse availabilities and resources. For Dog Groomers offering different services, creating Service Calendars ensures effective scheduling and resource allocation. 

[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/nOivRBmilXE?&wmode=opaque)

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is a Service Calendar?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/#What-is-a-Service-Calendar?)
- [Key Benefits of Service Calendars](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/#Key-Benefits-of-Service-Calendars)
- [Adding Staff Members and Availability](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/#Adding-Staff-Members-and-Availability)
- [Creating Groups for MedSpa Services](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/#Creating-Groups-for-%E2%80%8BPhotography-Services)
- [Creating Service Calendar](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/#Creating-Service-Calendar)
- [Edit Existing Service Calendars](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/#Edit-Existing-Service-Calendars)
- [Creating Service Menu](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/#Creating-Service-Menu)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/#Frequently-Asked-Questions)

---

# **What is a Service Calendar?**

Service Calendars are scheduling tools that let you define specific services, assign staff, and allocate resources like rooms and equipment. For a dog grooming business, this means you can create calendars for services such as full grooms, bath & brush, and nail trims—each linked to the right groomer, grooming station/tub, and tools. This ensures customers can book easily while your team avoids scheduling conflicts.

---

## **Key Benefits of Service Calendars**

Service Calendars help dog groomers streamline scheduling, improve efficiency, and enhance customer experience.

- **Automated Scheduling**: Customers book appointments without calling the salon.

- **Resource Management**: Assign grooming stations/tubs and tools (clippers, shears, dryers) to prevent double bookings.
- **Staff Scheduling**: Define groomers’ working hours for accurate availability.

- **Service Grouping**: Organize offerings into groups like “Bath & Brush” or “Full Grooming.”

- **Flexible Menus**: Offer multiple services in one booking (e.g., bath + nail trim).

- **Professional Branding**: Add images and custom colors for a polished booking page.

---

## **Adding Staff Members and Availability**

Adding staff is the foundation of service calendars since no service can be assigned without groomers set up.

### **1. Click Add User**

From your subaccount dashboard, Navigate to **Settings → My Staff → Add User.**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326915/original/4jcwkbkWzlWSn67YSV2EV3xSMnCCLjmZUQ.jpeg?1769164835)

### **2. User Info and Permissions**

Enter the groomer’s **name, email, extension**. Set **user permissions** (limit access if needed). Define **availability** (e.g., Mark works Mon, Wed, Fri, 9am–5pm; Henry works Tue–Sat, 11am–7pm). Click **Save**.

to learn more about user access you can click [here](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/48000982600?portalId=48000045315)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326412/original/fKndCR716FOeoVEpDD9XjWFxBls_FWmsnA.png?1769164551)

---

## **Creating Groups for Dog Grooming Services**

Groups act as categories to organize services. Each group has its own booking link.

### **1. Open Calendar Settings**

From the **Calendars** menu, click on **Calendar Settings** at the top-right corner. This is where you access all configuration options for groups, services, and preferences.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326429/original/Ae7yHbVYmJNGpPBbiXNsO4MRaR6uL7mbJw.png?1769164552)

### **2. Enable Service Menu**

Go to **Preferences → Account Preference** and toggle the **Service Menu** option on. This activates the service-based booking system so you can create service calendars and menus.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326410/original/-q6hq06KbNF7inZBnfIR2QZKnnEm4Gd6Kg.png?1769164551)

### **3. Start Group Creation**

In the **Calendars tab**, click **+ New Group** on the left sidebar. Groups help you organize related services such as full grooms, bath & brush, or nail trims.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326411/original/UUteO1TO6WGpRWj72J6rtpW5BoYgfNe4Xw.jpeg?1769164551)

### **4. Add Group Details**

Enter the **Group Name, Description, and URL (slug)** in the pop-up form. Select a template type (Classic or Neo) and click **Create** to save the group.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326416/original/93CcZZ5YbnjbEvZiYI_Ygh2ACDjdK5TqLw.png?1769164552)

---

## **Creating Service Calendar**

### **1. Create Service Calendar**

Select a group from the left sidebar and click **Create Calendar**. This begins the setup of a new service calendar for a specific dog grooming service like a full groom or bath & brush.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326414/original/BwQttZRhzO0Mk6PXTFWaxGq6mJJDQV5xvA.jpeg?1769164552)

### **2. Select Service Booking**

Navigate to **Calendars → Service Menu → Create Service Menu**. From the list of calendar types, click **Service Booking**. This option is designed for service-based businesses like dog groomers, allowing clients to book specific services such as full grooms or nail trims.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326752/original/-4ja56b5jNrkuQM26XLTa2utx4DvFF_jlA.jpeg?1769164726)

### **3. Enter Service Basics**

Fill out the service details including **Service Name, Assigned Staff, Custom URL, Service Duration, and Availability**. This step ensures the calendar is tailored to the specific dog grooming service being offered. Click **Advanced Settings** for further customization.

Clicking **Advanced Settings** expands additional configuration panels like **Service Details, Availability, Forms & Payment, Notifications, Customizations, and Rooms & Equipment**. These options let you fine-tune the booking flow, add branding, manage payments, and assign resources such as grooming stations/tubs or equipment.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326742/original/N-UicuXdMES_wSTRwv8dC_Hcpj4dzJg85Q.jpeg?1769164719)

### **4. Service Details Setup**

In the **Service Details tab**, you define the information that customers will see when booking this service. Start by uploading a **Service Logo** to give the booking page a professional look. Enter a clear **Service Name** (e.g., Full Groom, Bath & Brush, Nail Trim) and add a **Description** that explains what the service includes, such as “60-minute full groom including bath, haircut, and blow-dry.”

Next, assign the service to the right **Group** (e.g., Full Grooming) so it stays organized with related services. Finally, create a **Custom URL** — this becomes part of the booking link you’ll share with customers, making it easier to recognize and share (e.g., /full-groom-booking).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326417/original/8xoQBfY8AXdQijJghjMgYORQiXTR24EPqg.jpeg?1769164552)

### **5. Appointment & Staff Setup**

In this section, you configure how the booking will appear to customers and staff. Set the **Appointment Invite Title**, which will show up on both customer and staff calendar invites (you can use placeholders like {{contact.name}} to personalize it). Under **Team Members**, assign one or more groomers who are qualified to perform this service - customers will only see time slots for those staff members.  
Then, define a **Meeting Location**: this could be the grooming salon itself, a specific grooming station or even a custom video link if needed. Lastly, choose a **Meeting Color** to visually distinguish this service on the internal calendar view, making it easier for staff to quickly identify the type of appointment.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326423/original/bH5EHFNS-BBRdW0mJoDZ3z0KQRXtVTqbFg.jpeg?1769164552)

### **6. Assign Room**

In the **Rooms**tab, you connect a physical space in your **dog grooming** salon to the service. A room can represent a grooming station, bathing area, or drying station where the service is performed. For example, you might assign “Grooming Station 1” for full grooms and “Bathing Tub” for bath & brush services. Assigning a room ensures that once a customer books the service, that specific space is reserved and cannot be double-booked.This is especially useful for clinics with limited shoot spaces, as it prevents multiple appointments from being scheduled in the same spot at the same time.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326422/original/Rx-UKhx4_choUAzYPV7ZUqbwir7QZusQuA.png?1769164552)

### **7. Assign Equipment**

In the **Equipment tab**, you link the tools or resources needed to complete the service. Equipment can represent items like clippers, high-velocity dryers, or grooming tool kits, and you can specify the available quantity. For example, you may assign “High-Velocity Dryer” to a bath & brush service or “Clipper Kit” to a full groom. When a customer books the service, the system automatically reserves the necessary equipment, making sure it isn’t overbooked across multiple appointments. This helps maintain smooth operations by guaranteeing that all required tools are available for every appointment.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326419/original/aYQ3cRmvaCpIzP88d6na5APdZCWfdQkBBA.png?1769164552)

---

## **Edit Existing Service Calendars**

To update an existing service calendar, go to **Service Calendars (v1)** under the **Meetings** tab. Find the calendar you want to edit from the list and click the **pencil icon** under the **Actions** column. This will reopen the calendar settings, allowing you to adjust details such as service name, assigned staff, availability, notifications, or resources without having to recreate the calendar.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063856592/original/qFwNpTXLimbaA0ASVfzCna5DA2Fk-jL-Fw.png?1769776399)

---

## **Creating Service Menu**

The Service Menu lets you display multiple services or groups in a single booking page.

### **1. Open Service Menu**

Go to **Meetings** ➜ **Service Calendars (v1)** ➜ **Service Menu**. This brings you to the Service Menu area where customer-facing menus are created and managed.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326413/original/G3QXmqAh5VV1c1-pCcPn35U-Zoo8GhN5OA.png?1769164552)

### **2. Create Service Menu**

Click **+ Create Service Menu** in the top-right. This starts a new, customer-facing menu that will display your dog grooming services.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326418/original/siBhbm-77ZjE_LDY1wDd4GOdl0I62glZ3g.png?1769164552)

### 

### **3. Menu Details**

Complete **Service Menu name**, **Description**, and the **Service URL** slug; choose the **Form** and toggle the **Consent checkbox** if needed. These settings define what customers see at the top of the menu and the link you’ll share.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326427/original/cnV82-nZPs2BTFGTt6PPjfNHVnJBhH-oYg.png?1769164552)

### **4. Enable Options**

Under **Additional Options**, toggle **Enable Add Guests**, **Enable Multiple Service Selection**, and **Enable Staff Selection**. These controls let customers book for guests, select multiple services (e.g., bath + nail trim), and pick a preferred groomer.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326425/original/KNUAoO-vOZHLAIe9qW-hN4_YToDz1ckvAQ.png?1769164552)

### **5. Select Services**

Click **Select Services** and choose the **groups/calendars** to include in this menu. Only services you’ve already created and assigned to groups will appear; expand a group to check specific services.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326420/original/GNMLnph_V7R2xPWZwgoRKE8minDz0ohnRg.png?1769164552)

### 

### **6. Arrange Order**

Open **Arrange your services**, then drag the handles to reorder how groups/services appear. Place your most popular items (e.g., Full Groom, Bath & Brush) at the top to improve conversions.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063326415/original/uoYvLa1zk06Nspsi8aRBEEtCFoA1tC9shA.png?1769164552)

---

Now, when you give your customers the link to your Service Menu, it should look like this.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063564801/original/oJkNhAW206VOIA3HlXNIv4yRSI9E5zKPUw.png?1769512426)

Mastery of service calendars within High Level is crucial for businesses offering a diverse range of services. This detailed guide ensures that users can adeptly create, customize, and present their **Service Calendars**, providing a streamlined experience for both businesses and clients. Armed with this knowledge, businesses can optimize their scheduling processes and elevate customer satisfaction.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why can’t I save a service calendar?**

You must assign at least one staff member before saving.

**Q: Why are no time slots showing for a service?**

Check staff availability, assigned rooms, and equipment.

**Q: Can clients book multiple services at once?**

Yes, enable multiple services in the Service Menu settings.

**Q: Can I take deposits for services?**

Yes, connect Stripe or PayPal under Forms & Payment.

**Q: How do I prevent double-booking****grooming station/tub or equipment?**Assign rooms and equipment to each service.

**Q: Can clients pick their preferred****groomer****?**

Yes, enable Staff Selection in the Service Menu.

**Q: How do I list all services on one page?**

Use the Service Menu to combine multiple calendars.

title_en: How to Send Purchase and Order Confirmations in HighLevel
source_md:
HighLevel provides multiple ways to confirm a customer's purchase, depending on where the transaction occurs and how much customization you need. You can send built-in Sales Receipts for supported successful payments, use Store Order Confirmation Emails for e-commerce Store purchases, or create a custom post-purchase experience with the **Order Submitted** workflow trigger.

Choosing the correct method helps customers receive the appropriate transaction details while avoiding unnecessary or duplicate confirmation messages.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Key Benefits of Purchase and Order Confirmations](#Key-Benefits-of-Purchase-and-Order-Confirmations)
- [Choose the Right Confirmation Method](#Choose-the-Right-Confirmation-Method)
- [Send an Automatic Sales Receipt](#Send-an-Automatic-Sales-Receipt)
- [Send a Store Order Confirmation Email](#Send-a-Store-Order-Confirmation-Email)
- [Send a Custom Confirmation with the Order Submitted Trigger](#Send-a-Custom-Confirmation-with-the-Order-Submitted-Trigger)
- [Add Post-Purchase Automation](#Add-Post-Purchase-Automation)
- [Avoid Duplicate Confirmation Messages](#Avoid-Duplicate-Confirmation-Messages)
- [Test Your Purchase Confirmation](#Test-Your-Purchase-Confirmation)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)
- [Automated Sales Receipts](#Automated-Sales-Receipts)
- [Order Submitted Trigger for Custom Automations](#Order-Submitted-Trigger-for-Custom-Automations)
- [Additional Resources](#Additional-Resources)

---

## **Key Benefits of Purchase and Order Confirmations**

Purchase confirmations give customers immediate visibility into completed transactions while allowing businesses to automate the next steps after an order. HighLevel's different confirmation methods let you choose between standard transaction documentation and customized post-purchase communication.

- **Immediate Confirmation:** Let customers know their supported purchase or order was received successfully.
- **Transaction Visibility:** Provide applicable order, payment, and purchased-product information.
- **Custom Follow-Up:** Send product-specific instructions, onboarding information, or other post-purchase content.
- **Post-Purchase Automation:** Trigger internal actions, customer follow-up, or external integrations after an order.
- **Flexible Confirmation Methods:** Choose built-in receipts, Store confirmations, or workflow emails based on the purchase source.

---

## **Choose the Right Confirmation Method**

The appropriate confirmation method depends on where the purchase occurs and whether you need a standard transaction receipt or customized post-purchase communication.

  

| Method | Best For | Key Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Automatic Sales Receipt** | Supported order form, subscription, calendar, and invoice payments | Automatically sends standard transaction details after a supported successful payment |
| **Store Order Confirmation Email** | E-commerce Store orders | Sends a Store-specific confirmation and supports applicable order-access and digital-delivery experiences |
| **Order Submitted Workflow** | Customized post-purchase communication | Supports custom emails, order data, conditional logic, onboarding, internal actions, and external automation |

  
> **Tip:** You can intentionally use more than one method—for example, a Sales Receipt for payment documentation and a workflow email for onboarding instructions. Review all active notifications to avoid sending customers unnecessary duplicate messages.

---

## **Send an Automatic Sales Receipt**

Automatic Sales Receipts provide a straightforward way to send payment documentation without building a workflow. They are best when customers need a standard receipt containing the applicable transaction information after a successful payment.

HighLevel supports Automatic Sales Receipts for applicable:

- 1-step and 2-step order form purchases.
- Bump purchases and upsells.
- Subscriptions.
- Calendar appointment payments.
- Invoice payments.

When enabled, the receipt is automatically sent after a supported successful payment and can be delivered to the contact by email with the receipt attached as a PDF.

Sales Receipt settings also provide applicable customization for receipt information and email presentation.

> **Important:** Automatic Sales Receipts apply globally to their supported payment types. If you need different post-purchase communication for particular products, order sources, or purchase conditions, use an Order Submitted workflow.

For detailed configuration, see [How to Manage Sales Receipts for Order Form, Calendar and Invoice Payments](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000261).

## **Send a Store Order Confirmation Email**

E-commerce Store orders have a dedicated Order Confirmation Email rather than relying solely on the general Sales Receipt configuration. This confirmation can provide customers with Store-specific order information and access to the applicable post-purchase experience.

To review this configuration:

1. Go to **Payments > Settings**.
2. Open **Notifications**.
3. Locate the **Order Confirmation Email for Stores** setting.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081291225/original/-5IMIzezaYPZNunSAmA8ASTnZfyBnDGR1w.png?1789733656)
4. Configure the applicable Store order-confirmation experience.

Depending on the Store configuration, the confirmation can include a **View Order** option that takes the customer to their order information.

For applicable digital Store products, the Store order-confirmation experience can also provide access to downloadable purchases when digital delivery is configured.

> **Important:** If you sell downloadable products, do not rely on a generic workflow confirmation as the only delivery mechanism. Configure the applicable Store digital-product delivery experience.

---

## **Send a Custom Confirmation with the Order Submitted Trigger**

The **Order Submitted** workflow trigger gives you more control over what happens after an order. Use it when you need customized confirmation content, product-specific instructions, onboarding, conditional follow-up, internal actions, or external automation.

### **1. Create the Workflow**

1. Go to **Automation > Workflows**.
2. Create a new workflow or open the workflow you want to use.
3. Add **Order Submitted** as the workflow trigger.

> **Important:** **Order Submitted** and **Order Form Submitted** are different triggers. Order Submitted is tied to the order/purchase event, while Order Form Submitted is based on the form submission and does not necessarily establish a completed purchase.

### **2. Add Order Filters**

Filters let you control which purchases enter the workflow. This is useful when different products or purchase sources require different confirmation messages.

Depending on the order context, available filters can include criteria such as:

- Product.
- Order Source.
- Sub-Source.
- Funnel or Website.
- Page.
- Submission Type.
- Product Price.

For example, if the workflow should send onboarding instructions only after a specific product is purchased, filter the trigger for that product.

### **3. Review Allow Multiple**

A customer may generate more than one eligible order event, particularly when bump purchases or upsells are part of the checkout experience. Workflow enrollment settings determine whether the same contact can enter the workflow again.

If the confirmation workflow should run for subsequent eligible purchases by the same customer, review **Allow Multiple** in the workflow settings and configure it for the intended checkout behavior.

### 

### **4. Add the Confirmation Email**

Add a **Send Email** action after the trigger and create the confirmation message the customer should receive.

Your custom confirmation might include:

- Thank-you messaging.
- Order information.
- Customer information.
- Product-specific instructions.
- Appointment or onboarding steps.
- Support information.
- Relevant next actions.

### **5. Add Order Details with Custom Values**

When Order Submitted is used as a workflow trigger, applicable order-related custom values become available for use in downstream workflow actions.

Depending on the order data, these can include information such as:

- Order ID.
- Order total.
- Cart total.
- Currency.
- Coupon or discount information.
- Order date/time.
- Payment gateway.
- Customer name.
- Customer email.
- Customer phone.

Use only the information that makes the confirmation useful to the customer.

### **6. Show Purchased Products with the Shopping Cart Element**

If the email should dynamically display the products included in the order, use the **Shopping Cart** element in the email template used by the Order Submitted workflow.

The Shopping Cart element can populate applicable information such as:
