title_en: Error 135000 — Generic User Error
source_md:
|  |
| --- |
| Troubleshooting Guide  Error 135000 — Generic User Error  Understand why WhatsApp template messages fail with error code 135000, what causes it, and the known workarounds to get your messages sending again. |

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| What you'll learn   |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | +  What error 135000 means | +  Known causes | +  Step-by-step workarounds | +  How to prevent it | |

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Error 135000?](#overview)
- [Known Causes](#causes)
- [How to Resolve It](#resolve)
- [How to Prevent It](#prevent)
- [Related Error Codes](#related)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#faq)

---

|  |
| --- |
| What is Error 135000?  Generic User Error — a template message failed due to an unknown issue with the request parameters or a Meta-side restriction |

Error **135000** is a WhatsApp Cloud API error officially titled **"Generic User Error"**. It occurs when a template message fails to send due to an unknown error with the request parameters, or when Meta's internal systems flag the message due to security or policy restrictions.

What makes this error particularly frustrating is that **Meta does not disclose the specific reason** behind it. According to Meta's own documentation, the error is related to template restrictions put in place for security reasons, but the exact details are intentionally withheld.

```
Important: According to Meta Support, error 135000 is sometimes caused by false positives in Meta's spam and scam detection system. Legitimate templates can be incorrectly flagged, which means the issue may not always be caused by something you did wrong.
```

---

|  |
| --- |
| Known Causes  Confirmed and commonly reported reasons for this error |

The following causes have been confirmed by Meta's documentation, official support channels, and the developer community:

|  |
| --- |
| 1. Unsupported variable values in template parameters  This is the most common confirmed cause. When the values passed into template variables `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, etc. contain content that WhatsApp does not support — such as emojis, WhatsApp links, special characters, or excessively long strings — the message will fail with error 135000. |

|  |
| --- |
| 2. Template flagged by Meta's spam or scam detection system  Meta runs automated security scans on outgoing template messages. Templates that resemble spam, phishing, or scam patterns — even legitimate ones — can be incorrectly flagged as false positives. This is a known issue confirmed by Meta Support and can affect templates that were previously working without any changes on your end. |

|  |
| --- |
| 3. Template violates a WhatsApp policy  The template content or its variable values may violate WhatsApp's Business Policy or Commerce Policy — such as promoting prohibited products, including sensitive information, or using threatening language. Meta applies these checks at the time of sending, not just at approval. |

|  |
| --- |
| 4. Incorrect request parameters or formatting errors  Errors in the API request itself — such as mismatched parameter counts, incorrect component types, or malformed JSON — can trigger error 135000. This is more common when templates have recently been edited or when the number of variable parameters in the request does not match the approved template. |

|  |
| --- |
| 5. Template corruption or internal Meta sync issue  In some cases, previously approved templates that were working correctly suddenly start returning error 135000 with no changes made. This is caused by an internal Meta-side issue where the template becomes corrupted or desynced in Meta's systems. Deleting and recreating the template typically resolves this. |

---

|  |
| --- |
| How to Resolve It  Try these steps in order — start with the simplest fix first |

```
Note: There is no single guaranteed fix for error 135000. The steps below are the known workarounds confirmed by Meta Support and the developer community. Work through them in order until the issue is resolved.
```

Step 1 **Check the variable values you are passing into the template**

Review every value being injected into template variables and confirm none of them contain:

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  | | --- | | Do not include in variable values: - Emojis - WhatsApp links (wa.me/...) - Special characters such as # $ % & - Excessively long strings - HTML or markdown formatting - Empty or null values | | |  | | --- | | Safe variable values include: - Plain text only - Numbers and dates - Names and short phrases - Standard alphanumeric content - URLs only if the template was approved with a URL variable | |

Step 2 **Verify the request format matches the approved template exactly**

Open the template in your CRM or in Meta Business Manager and confirm:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| |  | | --- | | The number of variable parameters in your API request matches the number of variables in the approved template | |
| |  | | --- | | The component types (header, body, buttons) in the request match the template structure | |
| |  | | --- | | The template name and language code in the request exactly match what is in Meta Business Manager | |

Step 3 **Delete and recreate the affected templates**

If the above checks do not reveal a problem, the template may have become corrupted or incorrectly flagged in Meta's system. The most effective known workaround is to delete and recreate the template:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| |  | | --- | | 1 Take a copy of each affected template — screenshot or paste the content somewhere safe | |
| |  | | --- | | 2 Go to **WhatsApp Settings** in your CRM and delete the affected template(s) | |
| |  | | --- | | 3 Create a new template with the same or similar content — use a **new name** for the template | |
| |  | | --- | | 4 Submit the new template for approval and wait for Meta to approve it (up to 24 hours) | |
| |  | | --- | | 5 Test the new template once approved | |

```
This workaround — deleting and recreating templates — has been confirmed by multiple businesses and documented on the Meta Developer Community Forum as the most consistently effective fix for error 135000.
```

Step 4 **Delete and re-add the phone number (if error persists)**

If recreating the templates does not resolve the issue, try removing and re-adding the phone number linked to your WhatsApp Business Account:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| |  | | --- | | 1 Go to your WhatsApp Business Account in Meta Business Manager | |
| |  | | --- | | 2 Go to **Phone Numbers**, select the affected number, and click **Delete** | |
| |  | | --- | | 3 Click **Add Phone Number** and follow the setup and verification steps | |
| |  | | --- | | 4 Complete the OTP verification process and then test your templates again | |

```
Warning: Deleting a phone number will remove it from your WhatsApp Business Account. Make sure you have access to the number to complete re-verification via OTP before proceeding with this step.
```

Step 5 **Contact support if the issue persists**

If none of the above steps resolve the error, it is likely a Meta-side issue that requires escalation. Contact our support team and provide the following details:

|  |
| --- |
| - The name of the affected template(s) - The phone number ID associated with the WABA - The full API error response including the `fbtrace_id` value - When the error started and whether the template was working before - Any recent changes made to the template or account |

---

|  |
| --- |
| How to Prevent It  Best practices to reduce the likelihood of triggering error 135000 |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| |  | | --- | | **Keep variable values simple and plain** — avoid emojis, special characters, WhatsApp links, HTML, and overly long strings in template variable values | |
| |  | | --- | | **Follow Meta's template creation guidelines** — review WhatsApp's guidelines before creating templates, especially around content restrictions and variable formatting rules | |
| |  | | --- | | **Test templates with sample values before sending at scale** — validate that the exact variable values you plan to send work correctly on a test number before sending to a large list | |
| |  | | --- | | **Do not reuse rejected or deleted template names** — when recreating a template, always use a new name to avoid potential conflicts with Meta's internal records | |
| |  | | --- | | **Ensure template content does not resemble phishing or spam** — avoid urgent language, suspicious-looking links, requests for personal information, or anything that could trigger Meta's automated detection systems | |

---

|  |
| --- |
| Related Error Codes  Other template-related errors you may encounter |

| Error Code | Title | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 132000 | Template Parameter Count Mismatch | The number of variables in the request does not match the approved template. |
| 132001 | Template Does Not Exist | The template does not exist in the specified language or has not been approved yet. |
| 132007 | Template Content Policy Violation | Template content violates a WhatsApp policy. Review the rejection reasons. |
| 132012 | Template Parameter Format Mismatch | Variable parameter values are not formatted as specified in the approved template. |
| 131037 | Display Name Approval Required | The business phone number does not have an approved display name. |

---

|  |
| --- |
| Frequently Asked Questions  Common questions about error 135000 |

|  |
| --- |
| Q: My template was working fine before and I made no changes — why is it now failing?  This is a known and documented issue. Meta's automated security scanning can incorrectly flag templates that were previously approved and working, causing them to suddenly fail with error 135000. This is a false positive on Meta's end. Deleting and recreating the template with a new name is the most effective fix. |

|  |
| --- |
| Q: Do I need to use a completely different template or can I recreate the same one?  You can recreate the same content, but you must use a **new template name**. Reusing the same name may result in the same issue persisting. Create the new template, wait for approval, and then update your workflows or campaigns to use the new template name. |

|  |
| --- |
| Q: Is this error always caused by something wrong with my template?  No. Meta Support has confirmed that error 135000 can be triggered by false positives in their spam detection system. In these cases, the template and request are correctly formatted — the issue is entirely on Meta's side. If you have reviewed your template and request thoroughly and found no issues, it is likely a Meta-side false positive. |

|  |
| --- |
| Q: Will I be charged for messages that return error 135000?  No. Messages that fail with error 135000 are not delivered and no conversation is opened, so you will not be charged for them. |

|  |
| --- |
| Q: Can I appeal this restriction with Meta?  Meta does not provide an official appeal process specifically for error 135000. The recommended path is to recreate the template and, if the error persists, contact Meta Business Support directly with the `fbtrace_id` from the error response so they can investigate on their end. |

|  |
| --- |
| Quick Summary  Error 135000 is Meta's "Generic User Error" — a vague error that covers template restriction failures. Start by checking your variable values for unsupported content. If the request looks correct, delete and recreate the template with a new name. If that does not work, remove and re-add the phone number. This is a known Meta-side issue and the workarounds above resolve it for most users. Contact support with your `fbtrace_id` if the issue persists. |

title_en: MailGun Setup - HostGator Domain Setup
source_md:
Email Infrastructure

Mailgun + HostGator Domain Setup

Step-by-step DNS configuration for connecting Mailgun to a domain hosted with HostGator's cPanel.

What You'll Learn

This guide walks through signing up for Mailgun, adding your domain, and configuring the five DNS records Mailgun requires — two TXT records, two MX records, and one CNAME — inside HostGator's cPanel Zone Editor.

It also covers how to avoid breaking your existing Google Workspace/Gmail mail delivery while adding Mailgun's records.

## Sign up for Mailgun & add your domain

Step 1

Sign up at [Mailgun.com](https://signup.mailgun.com/new/signup), then check your inbox to verify your email address.

![Mailgun signup confirmation screen](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284378416/original/VewuZVN3oFOFIvBdf4XqMAOX4vtVGv_jNg.png?1677630998)
![Mailgun email verification confirmation](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284378421/original/GU6IL6Y3N81qm6KMH9aTz7l5FV5IEv7ySA.png?1677630999)

Step 2

Log in to Mailgun, then click **Sending → Add New Domain**.

![Sending menu with Add New Domain option in Mailgun](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284378418/original/kxsnymCeuFAsBWkXaOes6QaaWED2_bfASA.png?1677630999)

Step 3

If your domain is **companyname.com**, decide whether to set up the main domain or a subdomain with Mailgun.

- **Main domain:** if you use the main domain, it should not also be used with Google Workspace or any other email provider — see [Mailgun's guidance](https://help.mailgun.com/hc/en-us/articles/203357040-Can-I-Use-the-Same-Domain-Name-for-Mailgun-and-for-Google-Apps-Or-Another-Email-Server-) on sharing a domain with another email server.
- **Subdomain:** type **ANYTHING\_HERE**.companyname.com — for example mg.companyname.com, replies.companyname.com, or support.companyname.com.

Important

Set up the domain or subdomain under the **US** region — not EU.

Click **Add domain**.

![Adding a domain in Mailgun](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284382652/original/woVjMqNw3YY_Zjs20LoBHUb4KrThVvj_Rw.png?1677635102)

Tip

The next screen asks you to add DNS records to your domain. Leave this screen open — you'll need it for the next step.

![Mailgun DNS records screen to keep open for the next step](https://help.mailgun.com/hc/article_attachments/8759612958491/Screen_Shot_2022-09-11_at_6.39.22_PM.png)

## Access DNS records in cPanel

Now log in to your DNS records and add the 5 DNS records Mailgun requires. This guide uses HostGator's cPanel as the example.

Step 1

Log in to [cPanel](https://portal.hostgator.com/hosting/cPanel/sso-redirect?redirect=/frontend/paper_lantern/).

Step 2

Look for the **Domains** section, then click **Zone Editor**.

![cPanel Zone Editor location](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284388376/original/0ObShEaAQ6GXG-G-sSlIwX_9uLXpFUjdCA.png?1677640303)

Step 3

Locate your domain in the Zone Editor section, then click its **Manage** button to view the domain's complete set of DNS records.

![Manage button next to a domain in cPanel Zone Editor](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284388585/original/ZsKY3OvmFHtUBZWXElGKPG31Nl51EuXcFA.png?1677640464)

Step 4

Click the **+Add Record** button and select **Add "TXT" Record**.

![Add TXT Record option in cPanel Zone Editor](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284388748/original/NLKDFwtDUhzgL1MKCSJEt-0sZ8a-ZR0JaA.png?1677640597)

## Add the 1st TXT record (SPF)

![TXT record entry form in cPanel Zone Editor](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284389218/original/uUNVP51P30hs2i_U9O701kVRlGP55HpdDw.png?1677641077)

Fields

**A. Name:** different for everyone — **do not include the root domain.**

- mg.companyname.com → host name is **mg**
- replies.companyname.com → host name is **replies**
- Main domain (companyname.com) → host name is **@**

**B. Record:** the same for everyone — paste v=spf1 include:mailgun.org ~all.

![Mailgun screen showing the SPF TXT record to copy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284389338/original/L_D8amxfS4rLqz8NkwMDjBWCqAuPnFqSiw.png?1677641215)

**C.** Click **Add Record**.

## Add the 2nd TXT record (DKIM)

Click the **+Add Record** button and select **Add "TXT" Record** again.

![Add TXT Record option in cPanel Zone Editor for the second record](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284388748/original/NLKDFwtDUhzgL1MKCSJEt-0sZ8a-ZR0JaA.png?1677640597)
![TXT record entry form for the DKIM record](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284389413/original/bZ319PXDv8_TwakgxeWsjd6r5-6KFjcfAA.png?1677641278)

Fields

**A. Name:** this part is a little tricky. Copy everything from the beginning of the value up until the subdomain part — **do not include the root domain.** Everyone's 2nd TXT record name and record value are different.

| Example | Host name to copy | Highlighted part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Using a subdomain | mx.\_domainkey.helpdesk | Example of the host value to copy when using a subdomain |
| Using the main domain | mailo.\_domainkey | Example of the host value to copy when using the main domain |

**B. Record:** different for everyone. Head back to Mailgun and copy the 2nd, much longer TXT record — highlighted in the screenshot below — and paste it here.

![Mailgun screen highlighting the long DKIM TXT record to copy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284385043/original/UvAhE3LGN5sYkTb4kyEsXNM0GE0Uc8Eq1Q.png?1677637220)

**C.** Click **Add Record**.

## Add the 1st MX record

![MX records section in cPanel Zone Editor](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284385538/original/qHcrrZPnp3g0LC4c75qM1hg_opwYUXgE0w.png?1677637720)

Click the **+Add Record** button and select **Add "MX" Record**.

![Add MX Record form in cPanel Zone Editor](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284389907/original/18xrjivpU7RYPDJqHY2wnce79K3AkwJe0A.png?1677641569)

Heads Up

If you have a Google Workspace account capturing incoming email for your main domain, make sure you're using a subdomain for Mailgun instead. See [Can I Use the Same Domain Name for Mailgun and for Google Apps (Or Another Email Server)?](https://help.mailgun.com/hc/en-us/articles/203357040-Can-I-Use-the-Same-Domain-Name-for-Mailgun-and-for-Google-Apps-Or-Another-Email-Server-)

![MX record fields highlighted in cPanel](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284390505/original/nO1ZhMzBXp4ZqlhfzX1QYLxgGT0_ET-_vg.png?1677642035)

Fields

**A. Name:** different for everyone —

- mg.companyname.com → host name is **mg**
- replies.companyname.com → host name is **replies**
- Main domain → host name is **@**

**B. Priority:** 10 — the same for everyone, no matter what domain you're setting up.

**C. Destination:** the same for everyone — paste mxa.mailgun.org.

Click **Save Record**.

## Add the 2nd MX record

Click the **+Add Record** button and select **Add "MX" Record** again. This time we'll add a second record pointing to mxb.mailgun.org.

![Add second MX Record form in cPanel Zone Editor](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284389907/original/18xrjivpU7RYPDJqHY2wnce79K3AkwJe0A.png?1677641569)
![Second MX record fields highlighted in cPanel](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284390505/original/nO1ZhMzBXp4ZqlhfzX1QYLxgGT0_ET-_vg.png?1677642035)

Fields

**A. Name:** different for everyone —

- mg.companyname.com → host name is **mg**
- replies.companyname.com → host name is **replies**
- Main domain → host name is **@**

**B. Priority:** 10 — the same for everyone.

**C. Destination:** the same for everyone — paste mxb.mailgun.org.

Click **Save Record**.

## Add the CNAME record

![CNAME section in cPanel Zone Editor](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284385721/original/3LyKoigujZ-vEjMFQDflCfmRRfAJra3rYA.png?1677637907)

Click the **+Add Record** button and select **Add "CNAME" Record**.

![Add CNAME Record option in cPanel](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284390884/original/13yHoywGcgf3oSslLKzD03Sj9MAxoJQGfA.png?1677642360)
![CNAME record entry form in cPanel](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284391213/original/QLb8ArxkgSrQsXJzo63PddCcQRhylQBGHw.png?1677642643)

Fields

**A. Name:** different for everyone. Head back to Mailgun to copy the host name — copy everything from the beginning up until the subdomain part, **do not copy the main domain**.

- mg.companyname.com → host name is **email.mg**
- replies.companyname.com → host name is **email.replies**
- Main domain (companyname.com) → host name is **email**

![Mailgun CNAME host name to copy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284385985/original/OtLw_A4zY8FbLbBKqMB9kUKRaQJO3xpp8A.png?1677638165)

**B. Record:** the same for everyone — paste mailgun.org.

**C.** Click **Save Record**.

## Verify DNS & finish setup

Now that you've added all 5 records, go back to Mailgun and click **Verify DNS Settings**. If some records still aren't showing a green checkmark, click the same button again — DNS propagation can take a little time.

![Verify DNS Settings button in Mailgun](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284387965/original/I7T5QQCSjAnBvT1zqQlVgXSuNdgfuNiM3w.png?1677639928)

Next Steps

Once all records are verified, grab your [Mailgun API key and add it to your email service settings](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48000981682).

Then send a test email to confirm everything works — see [how to send a test email in the Conversation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001208887).

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Where do I find the Zone Editor in cPanel?

Log in to cPanel, look for the Domains section, and click Zone Editor. From there, find your domain and click Manage to view and add DNS records.

Q: Should I use my main domain or a subdomain with Mailgun?

If you already use your main domain with Google Workspace or another email provider, use a subdomain (like mg.companyname.com) for Mailgun instead to avoid mail routing conflicts.

Q: What does "do not include the root domain" mean for the Name field?

In cPanel's Zone Editor, the Name field only needs the subdomain portion — the root domain is added automatically. So for mg.companyname.com, you'd enter just "mg", not the full domain.

Q: Will this break my existing Gmail or Google Workspace email?

Not if you use a subdomain for Mailgun rather than your main domain, and leave your existing MX records for Google Workspace untouched on the main domain.

Q: How long does it take for DNS records to verify?

DNS propagation is usually fast, but it can occasionally take a few hours. If a record isn't showing green yet, wait a bit and click Verify DNS Settings again.

Q: What do I do after all 5 records show a green checkmark?

Grab your Mailgun API key, add it to your email service settings, and send a test email in a conversation to confirm delivery is working.

title_en: How to Setup Flow Agents in Agent Studio
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/kffk-zdHGHg?&wmode=opaque)

Agent Studio is HighLevel’s visual environment for building intelligent AI agents. It allows you to design how an agent is triggered, how it processes information, how it makes decisions, and what actions it performs all within a flexible, node-based canvas.

This article is intended for users who are exploring Agent Studio for the first time and want to understand its structure, purpose, and core components before building advanced automations.

```
Note: AI Studio and Agent Studio are two separate AI tools within HighLevel, designed for different use cases.

AI Studio is a conversational, AI-powered builder that helps you quickly create websites, pages, and other web assets using prompts. Agent Studio is a visual builder used to create AI-powered agents that can respond to events, interact with users, and automate tasks.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Agent Studio?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-Agent-Studio?)
- [Key Benefits of Agent Studio](#Key-Benefits-of-Agent-Studio)
- [Understanding the Agent Studio Interface](#Understanding-the-Agent-Studio-Interface)
  - [Agent Studio Dashboard](#Agent-Studio-Dashboard)
  - [Creating a New Agent](#Creating-a-New-Agent)
  - [Agent Template Library](#Agent-Template-Library)
  - [The Builder Canvas](#The-Builder-Canvas)
  - [Start Trigger](#Start-Trigger)
  - [Node Categories](#Node-Categories)
  - [Variables and Global Prompt](#Variables-and-Global-Prompt)
  - [Testing and Publishing](#Testing-and-Publishing)
  - [Getting Started with Agent Studio](#Getting-Started-with-Agent-Studio)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Agent Studio?**

Agent Studio is a visual builder used to create AI-powered agents that can respond to events, interact with users, retrieve information, generate content, and connect with external systems.

Unlike simple rule-based automations, agents built in Agent Studio can interpret input, make contextual decisions, route conversations dynamically, and use tools such as knowledge search or APIs.

Each agent is built using connected nodes on a canvas, allowing you to define how it starts, how it processes information, and how it completes its task.

---

## **Key Benefits of Agent Studio**

- **Visual AI Builder:** Design agent behavior using a drag-and-drop canvas.

- **Event-Based Execution:** Trigger agents using CRM events such as chat messages, form submissions, or lead tags.

- **Flexible Decision Logic:** Route conversations based on AI intent detection or rule-based conditions.

- **Integrated Knowledge & Tools:** Connect your Knowledge Base, search the web, or make API calls.

- **Multi-Modal Output:** Generate text, images, audio, or video within a single flow.

- **Structured Data Collection:** Capture emails, phone numbers, and user selections during interactions.

---

## **Understanding the Agent Studio Interface**

### **Agent Studio Dashboard**

When you navigate to **AI Agents → Agent Studio**, you’ll see a list of all agents in your account.

The dashboard allows you to:

- View existing agents
- Check status (Draft or Published)
- See when they were created or last updated
- Organize agents into folders
- Create a new agent
- Browse available templates

This is the central management area for your AI agents.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065467179/original/gWUu9paUMwlzK6dQPBNaOIeV_5xeMiJ2Lw.png?1771836642)

---

### **Creating a New Agent**

From the dashboard, click **Create Agent**.

You can choose to:

- Start from scratch
- Use a template from the Template Library

Starting from scratch gives you a blank canvas. Using a template provides a pre-built structure that you can customize.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065467329/original/eB2-7EQoCxCCn7M_gSnjbFxwknHLuAGRyA.png?1771836707)

---

### **Agent Template Library**

The Template Library provides ready-made agent blueprints designed for common use cases.

Instead of building from a blank canvas, you can:

- Browse categorized templates
- Preview how the agent is structured
- Install a template into your account
- Modify any part of the flow after installation

Templates typically include predefined triggers, AI nodes, routing logic, and actions. For first-time users, templates are often the fastest way to understand how agents are structured and connected.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065467554/original/Hx0kM4KOVSCbclD-pkhVXECAkt6Y34_8ww.png?1771836848)

---

### **The Builder Canvas**

When you open or**create**an agent, you enter the visual builder canvas.

This is where you:

- Drag and connect nodes
- Define execution logic
- Configure each step of your agent

Agents are built by connecting nodes from left to right, beginning with a trigger and ending with an action or completion point. The connections between nodes define how the agent behaves in real scenarios.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065467643/original/mUl-0JICTLTok7QU4UcJcsOfNe7wSNCLpw.png?1771836930)

---

### **Start Trigger**

Every agent begins with a **Start Trigger**.

The Start Trigger defines when the agent should run. Common examples include:

- Chat Message
- Form Submission
- Lead Tag Added

Without a trigger, the agent will not execute. The trigger ensures the agent responds only when specific conditions are met.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065467704/original/jm98QJcg8ElCvZmjypz51nJYGPYV7OSJSQ.png?1771836978)

---

### **Node Categories**

In Agent Studio, everything on the canvas is built using **nodes**. A node is a building block that performs one specific function, such as starting the agent, generating a response, collecting information, or connecting to another system. By connecting nodes together, you define how your agent behaves from start to finish.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065466013/original/j4oMLxMOzUDEiNY0V7eX1F1IkCKNcPyfeQ.png?1771835869)

#### 

#### **AI Agent:**The AI Agent node is the “brain” of your flow. It reads incoming input, understands the context, and generates intelligent responses based on instructions you provide. For example, if a user asks about pricing, this node can interpret the question and generate a relevant reply.

#### 

#### **Sequential:**The Sequential node allows you to group multiple steps and run them in a fixed order. This is useful when certain actions must happen one after another, such as collecting an email first and then sending a confirmation message.

#### 

#### **End Node:**The End Node marks where the agent’s execution stops. Once the flow reaches this node, the interaction is complete.

#### 

#### **Router:**The Router node helps the agent choose between different paths based on conditions or AI-detected intent. Think of it like a decision point if a user asks about support, go one way; if they ask about sales, go another.

#### 

#### **Search Knowledge Base:**This node allows the agent to look up information stored in your connected Knowledge Base. For example, it can pull answers directly from your company’s documentation.

#### 

#### **Search Web:**The Search Web node enables the agent to gather information from online sources when needed. This is useful when responding to questions that require publicly available or current data.

#### 

#### **MCP Server:**The MCP Server node connects your agent to supported external tool servers. This allows advanced integrations where the agent can use external systems to perform specialized actions.

---

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065466189/original/oilx-pQ2JI0o4w5Q8deexvh1uFZ02VS7Nw.png?1771835998)

#### 

#### **API Call:**The API Call node allows your agent to send or receive information from other applications. For example, it could send lead data to another system or retrieve customer details.

#### 

#### **Audio Generation:**This node allows the agent to generate spoken audio responses based on instructions within the flow.

#### 

#### **Image Generation:**The Image Generation node creates images based on descriptive prompts, useful for dynamic visual content.

#### 

#### **Text Generation:**The Text Generation node produces written content such as messages, summaries, or structured responses.

#### 

#### **Email Address:**This node collects a user’s email address during an interaction in a structured format.

#### 

#### **Phone Number:**The Phone Number node collects a user’s phone number in a standardized format for accurate storage.

#### 

#### **Single Choice:**The Single Choice node presents predefined options for the user to select from, helping guide structured decision-making.

#### 

#### **Text Input:**The Text Input node collects open-ended responses from users, allowing the agent to gather detailed information.

---

### **Variables and Global Prompt**

At the top of the builder, you will find additional configuration tools that control how your agent behaves across the entire flow.

#### 

#### **Variables**

Variables act as reusable placeholders that store information. Instead of repeating the same value in multiple places, you define it once and reference it throughout the agent. For example, you could store a business name and use it consistently across responses.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065466863/original/zD8T9uxFzHxMGtXUqX8eUEOonkdo86vetA.gif?1771836435)

#### 

#### **Global Prompt**

The Global Prompt defines overarching instructions that guide the agent’s behavior. It sets tone, personality, and rules the agent should follow in every interaction.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065467862/original/SyRStCRC4ePrfe8ujj_lisNlSwj4PLcoUw.gif?1771837088)

### 

### **Testing and Publishing**

Before activating an agent, you can:

- Use the **Test** feature to simulate execution
- Save changes as a draft
- Publish the agent when ready

An agent must be published in order to respond to real-world triggers.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do agents run automatically?**

Agents run only when their configured trigger conditions are met.

**Q: How is Agent Studio different from workflows?**

Workflows follow predefined automation rules. Agents can interpret input and make dynamic decisions using AI.

**Q: Do I need to publish an agent for it to work?**

Yes. An agent must be published to respond to real events.

**Q: Can agents integrate with external systems?**

Yes. API Call and MCP Server nodes allow external integrations.

**Q: Can agents generate content beyond text?**

Yes. Agent Studio supports image, audio, and video generation.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Intent-Based Routing in Agent Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006436-intent-based-routing-in-agent-studio-ai-router-node-)
- [How to Set Up Agent Studio Triggers](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007310-how-to-set-up-agent-studio-triggers-for-real-time-starts)
- [Agent Studio Template Library](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007318-agent-studio-template-library-build-ai-agents-faster-with-reusable-templates)

title_en: Creating and Managing LinkedIn Ads in HighLevel Ad Manager
source_md:
The HighLevel Ad Manager allows you to **create, launch, and manage LinkedIn ad campaigns** without leaving your workspace. By connecting your LinkedIn Ad Account, you can design lead-generation or website-traffic ads, monitor campaign performance, and manage budgets all alongside your Google and Meta ads from one unified dashboard.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Overview of LinkedIn Ads in Ad Manager](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BOverview-of-LinkedIn-Ads-in-Ad-Manager)
- [Key Benefits of LinkedIn Ads in HighLevel](#Key-Benefits-of-LinkedIn-Ads-in-HighLevel)
- [Connecting Your LinkedIn Ad Account](#Connecting-Your-LinkedIn-Ad-Account)
- [Campaign Structure in LinkedIn](#Campaign-Structure-in-LinkedIn)
- [Supported Campaign Objectives](#Supported-Campaign-Objectives)
- [Ad Creation & Media Types](#Ad-Creation-&-Media-Types)
- [Audience Targeting](#Audience-Targeting)
- [Budget & Schedule](#Budget-&-Schedule)
- [Managing Campaigns and Performance Dashboard](#Managing-Campaigns-and-Performance-Dashboard)
- [How to Create a LinkedIn Ad Campaign](#How-to-Create-a-LinkedIn-Ad-Campaign)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)

---

# **Overview of LinkedIn Ads in Ad Manager**

LinkedIn Ads in HighLevel Ad Manager bring professional B2B advertising directly into your marketing environment. This integration connects with LinkedIn Campaign Manager so you can build campaigns, sync leads in real time, and analyze performance without switching between tools. HighLevel consolidates your ad workflows, budgets, and reports into a single, easy-to-manage interface.

LinkedIn Ads inside Ad Manager streamline your paid media management by letting you target professional audiences, monitor engagement metrics, and capture leads all from within the same dashboard where you already manage your other ad platforms.

---

## **Key Benefits of LinkedIn Ads in HighLevel**

Running LinkedIn Ads within HighLevel saves time, improves reporting accuracy, and ensures your campaigns reach the right business audiences with minimal effort.

- **Unified Dashboard:** Manage Google, Meta, and LinkedIn ads in one place.

- **Native Lead Gen Sync:** LinkedIn Lead Gen Form submissions automatically flow into HighLevel CRM.

- **Advanced Targeting Filters:** Reach audiences by job title, seniority, company size, industry, skills, and more.

- **Real-Time Previews:** Instantly review desktop and mobile layouts before publishing.

- **Granular Reporting:** Track CPC, CPM, CPL, conversions, and spend per campaign, group, or ad.

---

## **Connecting Your LinkedIn Ad Account**

Connecting your LinkedIn Ad Account to HighLevel Ad Manager allows you to publish, manage, and track ads directly through LinkedIn’s Campaign Manager API. This connection ensures all leads, campaigns, and metrics sync automatically with your CRM.

### **Pre-requisites**

Before connecting, confirm that:

- **LinkedIn Ad Account**  is active in [LinkedIn Campaign Manager](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a426102/create-an-ad-account-in-campaign-manager-as-a-new-advertiser).

- **LinkedIn Company Page**  is linked to your ad account. [Learn how.](https://linkedin.com/help/lms/answer/a427419)

- **Access Permissions** You must have:
  - Campaign Manager access to the Ad Account.
  - Admin access to the LinkedIn Company Page.

### **Steps to Connect Your LinkedIn Ad Account**

**Open Ad Manager Settings**

To begin, navigate to **Marketing › Ad Manager**, then click the **Settings gear icon** in the top right corner of the dashboard.

This opens the Ad Manager Settings page where you can configure or connect ad accounts across supported platforms like Meta, Google, and LinkedIn.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056534519/original/7Qb0nohk-xv3qVF6FLpnJMCob9fk3UJJXA.png?1761117435)

**Select LinkedIn Platform**

On the left side of the Ad Manager Settings page, click **LinkedIn** under the **Platform Settings** section.

Then click **+ Connect Account** on the right-hand panel to start linking your LinkedIn Ad Account.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056534546/original/6vFDw6q8SmP4L9hHj0tsemfbpT9tJsYn_g.png?1761117462)

**Connect Your LinkedIn Account**

A pop-up window will appear prompting you to connect your LinkedIn account.

Click **Connect LinkedIn** to open a secure login window where you can sign in and authorize HighLevel to access your LinkedIn Ad Account.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056534584/original/Ml-htpyl6hYqTdmdDg2_VQYWgtPA4Wb_zw.png?1761117484)

**Confirm Successful Connection**

After signing in and granting permissions, your LinkedIn Ad Account will appear in the **LinkedIn** section under **Ad Manager Settings**.

You’ll see the account name listed with a green **Active** status and the associated currency (e.g., USD), confirming that your LinkedIn account is now successfully connected to HighLevel Ad Manager.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056535335/original/UfOLvPAGOiiHoonVcP8cd4iGjnAQBHCxqw.png?1761117916)

### 

```
Notes & Best Practices

If your ad account doesn’t appear, check your admin permissions.

Each LinkedIn Ad Account must be linked to a Company Page.

To disconnect or reconnect, click the bin icon beside the connected account in settings.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056532769/original/VsN04pwy-OrhiurvjkHI7jtjpFZLKwmAnQ.png?1761115917)
```

---

## **Campaign Structure in LinkedIn**

LinkedIn uses a three-tier campaign hierarchy that HighLevel mirrors inside Ad Manager. Understanding this structure helps organize campaigns efficiently for tracking and budgeting.

- **Campaign Group** – Top-level budget container.

- **Campaign** – Objective, targeting, and spend layer.

- **Ad** – Creative assets and copy.

Multiple campaigns can exist within one group, and each campaign can include multiple ads for A/B testing.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056558985/original/9xMN1BO67fZuNLsjGq8TMLSG_BJvTcxz9w.png?1761127322)

---

## **Supported Campaign Objectives**

Choosing the correct campaign objective ensures that LinkedIn optimizes delivery based on your marketing goal.

| **Objective** | **Purpose** |
| --- | --- |
| Lead Generation | Capture qualified B2B leads through LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms that automatically sync with HighLevel. |
| Website Traffic | Drive verified clicks to your website and validate landing pages before publishing. |

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056535986/original/vMqC49i2xMR9aji9A5gizM6p7gj0WwsZdQ.png?1761118201)

---

## **Ad Creation & Media Types**

HighLevel enables you to build visually engaging ad creatives directly in Ad Manager while previewing how they’ll appear to LinkedIn users.

- Choose an ad format: **Single Image**, **Single Video**, or **Carousel**.

- Add ad components: **Introduction**, **Description**, **Headline**, **CTA**, and **Destination URL**.

- Carousel ads allow unique headlines and URLs for each card.

- Use the **Live Preview Panel** to confirm your ad layout for desktop and mobile before publishing.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056536863/original/uM93JWTmMzJ5vsCpami4QEEV-HUGEVRadQ.png?1761118707)

---

## **Audience Targeting**

LinkedIn targeting options allow precise audience selection, helping you connect with decision-makers and industry professionals relevant to your offer.

- Begin with a **mandatory geographic location**.

- Refine targeting by **Job Title**, **Industry**, **Company Size**, **Education**, **Skills**, **Seniority**, **Interests**, or **Traits**.

- Create up to **three attribute groups** using:

- **OR logic** within each group.
- **AND logic** between groups.
- Include or exclude attributes for advanced targeting control.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056536598/original/Bc9z-gj0MmwiOxnw_dGESEhQ6OQz_LWvJQ.png?1761118577)

---

## **Budget & Schedule**

HighLevel lets you set and adjust budgets and scheduling parameters directly from Ad Manager, ensuring your campaigns align with your financial and time-based goals.

- Set a **Daily** or **Lifetime** budget at the Campaign Group level.

- Choose optimization mode: **Maximum Delivery (default)** or **Cost Cap**.

- Launch campaigns immediately or select specific start and end dates for scheduled promotions.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056536467/original/jfDVQwPr5S_k83YRI2ouvw9QOT4CTyB5VA.png?1761118533)

---

## **Managing Campaigns and Performance Dashboard**

The Performance Dashboard helps you **monitor and manage** all active LinkedIn campaigns from a single screen. You can view key metrics, pause or edit campaigns, and export detailed reports.

- Go to **Ad Manager › Statistics › LinkedIn** tab.

- Track metrics such as **Impressions**, **Clicks**, **CTR**, **CPC**, **CPM**, **CPL**, **Leads**, **Spend**, and **Conversions**.

- Drill down from Campaign Group to Campaign or Ad level for deeper insights.

- Pause, resume, or edit campaigns directly from the dashboard.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056537215/original/Esig7GWbBbZiD3iC3ZeWg6C_OPVnM4dHmw.png?1761118815)

---

## **How to Create a LinkedIn Ad Campaign**

After connecting your LinkedIn account, you can build your first campaign directly from Ad Manager. Follow these steps to create and publish your ad.

1. Go to **Marketing › Ad Manager › Settings › LinkedIn** and click **+ Create Campaign**.
2. Select your campaign **Objective** (Lead Generation or Website Traffic).
3. Add creatives: **image**, **video**, or **carousel**, including headline, description, CTA, and destination URL.
4. Define your **Audience Targeting** parameters.
5. Choose **Daily or Lifetime Budget**, optimization mode, and schedule.
6. Review the campaign summary and check the live preview.
7. Click **Publish** — HighLevel pushes your campaign to LinkedIn Campaign Manager and begins tracking results immediately.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need Admin access on the LinkedIn Page to connect the ad account?**

Yes. You must have “Campaign Manager” or higher access, and the Page must already be linked to the Ad Account.

**Q: Can I connect multiple LinkedIn Ad Accounts to one HighLevel sub-account?**

Yes. You can connect multiple accounts and toggle between them under Ad Manager › Settings › LinkedIn.

**Q: Where do LinkedIn leads appear inside HighLevel?**

Leads from LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms automatically appear under **Contacts** with the source “LinkedIn Ads.”

**Q: My LinkedIn account isn’t appearing—what should I check?**

Verify that you have admin-level permissions on the ad account and that it’s linked to a valid Company Page.

**Q: Can I disconnect and reconnect my LinkedIn account?**

Yes. Click the bin icon under **Settings › LinkedIn** to remove or reconnect an account.

**Q: Are carousel ads supported for all objectives?**

Yes—carousel format is available for both **Lead Generation** and **Website Traffic** campaigns.

**Q: What happens if my LinkedIn ad is disapproved?**

The ad’s status displays as “Rejected” in HighLevel, along with LinkedIn’s feedback for resubmission.

title_en: How to Select Your First Action During HighLevel Onboarding
source_md:
Getting started with HighLevel is easier when you know what to focus on first. The personalized onboarding experience allows new customers to select an initial action based on their business goals and access guidance to complete it. With direct navigation to relevant features, tutorial videos, and guided product tours, you can start using HighLevel more confidently and achieve your first goal faster.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Action Selection During Onboarding?](#What-is-Action-Selection-During-Onboarding?)
- [Key Benefits of Action Selection During Onboarding](#Key-Benefits-of-Action-Selection-During-Onboarding)
- [Suggested Onboarding Actions](#Suggested-Onboarding-Actions)
- [Custom Action Suggestions](#Custom-Action-Suggestions)
- [Personalized Redirection to Your Selected Action](#Personalized-Redirection-to-Your-Selected-Action)
- [Recommended Actions in Launchpad](#Recommended-Actions-in-Launchpad)
- [How to Select Your First Action During Onboarding](#How-to-Select-Your-First-Action-During-Onboarding)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Action Selection During Onboarding?**

Action Selection During Onboarding is a personalized onboarding feature that helps new HighLevel customers identify and complete their first important task. Instead of navigating the platform to determine where to begin, you can choose a suggested action that aligns with your immediate business needs.

Once you select an action, HighLevel directs you to the corresponding product page within your sub-account. Tutorial videos and guided product tours provide assistance to help you complete the task.

Your selected action also appears at the top of your Launchpad with a **Recommended** label, making it easier to return to your initial goal and track your onboarding progress.

---

## **Key Benefits of Action Selection During Onboarding**

Choosing a specific goal during onboarding creates a more focused experience, helping you prioritize essential tasks and become familiar with HighLevel's features without unnecessary navigation.

- **Personalized Onboarding:** Select an initial action based on your business priorities rather than following a generic setup path.
- **Faster Time to Value:** Start working toward a meaningful business outcome immediately after onboarding.
- **Direct Feature Access:** Navigate automatically to the product page associated with your selected action.
- **Guided Learning:** Access tutorial videos and product tours that help you understand how to complete your task.
- **Flexible Feedback:** Suggest an action that better matches your needs when the available options are not relevant.
- **Easy Action Tracking:** Find your selected action at the top of the Launchpad with a Recommended label.
- **Consistent Navigation:** Access the relevant sub-account product page regardless of whether you identify as an Agency User or SaaSpreneur.

---

## **Suggested Onboarding Actions**

Suggested onboarding actions help you identify a useful starting point based on common activities performed by new HighLevel customers. These recommendations are informed by Launchpad engagement trends, making it easier to choose a task that can deliver immediate value.

During onboarding, HighLevel presents a selection of actions that you can choose from. Consider which action best supports your immediate business objective. For example, you may want to begin by configuring a core feature or preparing a tool your business will use regularly.

The suggested actions are intended to simplify decision-making so you can move directly into using the platform.

---

## **Custom Action Suggestions**

Custom Action Suggestions allow you to share an onboarding goal when none of the predefined actions match your needs. This feedback helps HighLevel understand which additional onboarding experiences may be useful to customers in the future.

If you don't find a relevant action among the available suggestions, you can enter your preferred action using the free-text input field.

Describe the task you would like to accomplish as clearly as possible so your feedback accurately represents your goal.

For example, you might describe a specific setup activity or business outcome you want to prioritize.

```
Important: Custom suggestions are currently collected as feedback for future improvements. Submitting a suggestion does not automatically create a new onboarding action or personalized product tour.
```

---

## **Personalized Redirection to Your Selected Action**

Personalized redirection connects your onboarding choice with the relevant HighLevel feature, reducing the steps required to begin your first task. This allows you to move from selecting a goal to working toward completing it without manually searching for the correct product page.

After you select one of the suggested onboarding actions, HighLevel automatically directs you to the corresponding product page within your sub-account.

The destination provides onboarding guidance through resources such as:

- **Tutorial Videos:** Short instructional videos that introduce the relevant feature and help you understand how to use it.
- **Product Tour Guide:** Interactive, on-screen guidance that walks you through supported setup activities.
- **Relevant Feature Access:** Direct access to the HighLevel tools needed to complete your selected task.

This redirection also applies to customers who identify as Agency Users or SaaSpreneurs. Previously, these customers were directed to the agency account by default. With personalized action selection, choosing a supported onboarding action takes you directly to the corresponding sub-account product page instead.

---

## **Recommended Actions in Launchpad**

The Launchpad provides a centralized location for guided onboarding activities and helps you keep track of your progress. By placing your selected action at the top of the list, HighLevel makes it easier to recognize your initial goal and continue working toward completing it.

After selecting an onboarding action, you can find it displayed at the top of the Launchpad with a **Recommended** 

label.

This placement helps you:

- Quickly identify your selected onboarding goal.
- Return to the task when you need additional guidance.
- Access related tutorials and supported guided walkthroughs.
- Review onboarding progress as you complete available actions.

Supported Product Tour Guides can mark an action complete when the guided process finishes successfully.

For additional information about Launchpad navigation and tracking, see [Subaccount Launchpad](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005436-subaccount-launchpad).

---

## **How to Select Your First Action During Onboarding**

Selecting your initial onboarding action helps HighLevel connect you with the features and guidance most relevant to your immediate goals. Completing this process gives you a clear starting point and reduces the effort required to locate your first setup task.

Follow these steps to choose an action and begin your onboarding journey.

**Step 1: Begin Your HighLevel Onboarding**

Sign in to your new HighLevel account and follow the onboarding process until you reach the step asking you to select your first action.

**Step 2: Review the Suggested Actions**

Review the list of suggested actions and identify the option that best matches what you want to accomplish first. Choose an action that aligns with your immediate business needs.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082848776/original/EeErYxsY2T28ATNXK6yviROIbiwJ_4U5JQ.png?1791462408)

**Step 3: Select Your Preferred Action**

Choose your preferred action and follow the on-screen prompt to continue. If none of the suggested actions are relevant, use the custom suggestion field to submit feedback about your preferred goal.

**Step 4: Access the Corresponding Product Page**

After you proceed with a suggested action, HighLevel redirects you to its corresponding product page within your sub-account. The page provides access to relevant features and supporting onboarding guidance.

**Step 5: Follow the Tutorial or Product Tour**

Use the available instructional resources to understand and complete your selected action. Depending on the supported experience, you may be able to:

1. Watch a tutorial video explaining the feature.
2. Follow on-screen prompts in the Product Tour Guide.
3. Complete the required configuration or setup activity.

**Step 6: Return to Launchpad to Review Your Progress**

Navigate to **Launchpad** in the sub-account's left navigation menu. Your selected onboarding action should appear at the top of the Launchpad with the **Recommended** label. Review its progress and continue completing other relevant onboarding actions as needed.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082848815/original/l5FLxltObc-0OkQUezx8n4ln1-juwIW6iQ.png?1791462452)**

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Is action selection available to existing HighLevel customers?**

A: The original release introduced action selection for new customers. The newer Subaccount Launchpad also has rollout and eligibility requirements. Existing accounts should not assume they will receive the new onboarding selection screen.

**Q: Is the onboarding action selection feature available on every HighLevel plan?**

A: The initial release confirmed availability for new customers on the $97 plan, with expansion to the $297 and $497 plans planned. The broader Subaccount Launchpad now supports eligible customers on these plans, but availability of the specific first-action selection step has not been independently confirmed for every tier.

**Q: Can I change my selected onboarding action later?**

A: Launchpad allows you to access other supported onboarding actions. However, whether you can modify the original action selected during onboarding has not been confirmed.

**Q: What happens if I cannot complete an action because of missing permissions?**

A: Some onboarding tasks require specific user permissions. If you cannot complete an action, ask your agency administrator to verify your access to the relevant feature. Product tours may prevent progress when required permissions are unavailable.

**Q: What should I do if I cannot find Launchpad in my account?**

A: Confirm that your account is eligible for the current Launchpad experience and that your user role has the required permissions. Availability may also depend on your agency's signup date and rollout group.

**Q: Can I access onboarding guidance again after leaving the product page?**

A: Yes, supported Launchpad actions can be reopened from the Launchpad. Available Product Tour Guides may also allow you to replay the guided experience.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Sub account Launchpad](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005436-subaccount-launchpad)
- [Agency Launchpad](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005494-getting-started-agency-launchpad-overview)
- [Launchpad Contextual In-App Nudges](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006435-launchpad-contextual-in-app-nudges)
- [What Is an Agency Sub-Account in HighLevel?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007979-what-is-an-agency-sub-account-in-highlevel-)

title_en: Understanding the 5% Markup on Phone System Pass-Through Charges
source_md:
HighLevel Phone System billing separates standard usage costs, selected pass-through charges, and any agency-configured rebilling. A fixed 5% location-level markup currently applies to specific Phone System pass-through categories, while other wallet-billed services follow their applicable rates. Understanding these differences makes it easier to review wallet deductions, reconcile client usage, and verify charges directly inside HighLevel.

---

# **What is the 5% Phone System Pass-Through Markup?**

The 5% Phone System markup is an additional location-level charge applied to specific pass-through billing categories. It is separate from any rebilling or reselling amount an agency chooses to configure for its sub-accounts.

Current HighLevel Phone System pricing documentation identifies these categories as receiving the fixed 5% markup:

- **A2P Registration Fees:** Applicable brand, campaign registration, and recurring campaign fees.
- **SMS Carrier Fees:** Applicable carrier surcharges for SMS messaging.
- **MMS Carrier Fees:** Applicable carrier surcharges for MMS messaging.
- **Verified Caller ID:** Applicable charges associated with Verified Caller ID.
- **RCS Messaging Carrier Fees:** Applicable carrier charges for RCS messaging.

The 5% markup applies at the location level regardless of whether agency rebilling is enabled.

---

## **Key Benefits of Understanding Phone System Billing**

Knowing how underlying usage, pass-through charges, and agency rebilling are separated helps you verify wallet activity and explain costs more accurately to your clients.

- **Clearer billing:** Understand which charges include the location-level markup and which follow their standard wallet rate.

- **Better reconciliation:** Match individual wallet transactions with the corresponding HighLevel pricing information.

- **Accurate client pricing:** Keep HighLevel Phone System charges separate from the rebilling or reselling amount your agency chooses to apply.

- **Centralized verification:** Review transaction details and current wallet pricing directly inside HighLevel.

- **Improved visibility:** Filter wallet transactions by sub-account, billing period, product, transaction type, and other available criteria.

---

## **Phone System Charges and Agency Rebilling**

Agency rebilling is separate from the underlying Phone System charge. This distinction matters because an agency-configured markup does not replace the location-level 5% markup applied to the documented pass-through categories.

When the 5% markup applies and agency rebilling is enabled, the billing sequence is:

**Base pass-through cost → 5% location-level markup → agency-configured rebilling**

When agency rebilling is disabled, the applicable 5% location-level markup still applies to the documented categories.

Agency rebilling and reselling settings remain under the agency's control and should be reviewed separately from the underlying Phone System charge.

---

## **Current Pricing in Wallet & Transactions**

Wallet & Transactions provides a centralized place to review wallet usage, individual charges, pricing, invoices, recharge activity, and exports. This makes it easier to trace a transaction and compare it with the applicable current HighLevel wallet rate.

Go to:

**Agency View → Settings → Billing → Wallet & Transactions**

The current Wallet & Transactions experience includes:

- **Usage Overview:** Review wallet usage by sub-account or activity.

- **Wallet & Recharge:** Manage wallet balance and recharge settings.

- **Transactions:** Review individual wallet charges.

- **Invoices:** Access applicable billing records.

- **Pricing:** Review current wallet-billed product rates.

- **Export Center:** Create and manage transaction exports.

HighLevel's Wallet Pricing page is designed as the centralized source of truth for wallet-billed product rates and keeps displayed rates updated automatically.

---

## **Using the Transactions Page**

The Transactions page helps you investigate a specific wallet deduction without reviewing all account activity manually. Filtering the transaction list is especially useful when reconciling Phone System costs for a particular sub-account or billing period.

Go to:

**Agency View → Settings → Billing → Wallet & Transactions → Transactions**

The available transaction controls can be used to narrow results by applicable criteria such as:

- Sub-account
- Billing period
- Product
- Transaction Type
- Transaction ID

The transaction table provides information such as:

- ID and Location Name
- Billing Date
- Activity Date
- Description
- Amount
- Total Balance

Use the **Description** and **Amount** fields to identify the service responsible for the wallet deduction before comparing it with the applicable current rate.

---

## **Using the Pricing Page**

The Pricing page gives agencies a HighLevel-native reference for wallet-billed product costs. Using this page is more reliable than comparing a HighLevel wallet charge with an external provider's public pricing because wallet charges can involve different products, billing units, providers, and country-specific rates.

Go to:

**Agency View → Settings → Billing → Wallet & Transactions → Pricing**

The Wallet Pricing experience allows you to:

- Search for a product or category.
- Browse wallet-billed products by category.
- Review unit costs and billing units.
- Expand a product for additional pricing details.
- Review supported country-specific rates.

Prices shown on the Wallet Pricing page are maintained automatically by HighLevel.

---

## **What Did Not Change?**

Separating the Phone System markup from other billing functions helps prevent unnecessary configuration changes. The 5% location-level markup does not replace the agency's own pricing controls or change unrelated wallet-management settings.

Your agency can continue using applicable:

- Rebilling and reselling configurations
- Wallet funding
- Auto-Recharge settings
- Subscription and add-on billing
- Other wallet-billed HighLevel products

Historical transactions remain records of the amounts charged when those transactions occurred. Use the current Pricing page when you need to confirm the rate that applies to new usage.

---

## **How To Verify a Phone System Charge**

Reviewing both the transaction and its current pricing reference helps you understand what generated a wallet deduction and how that service is billed.

### **Step 1: Open Wallet & Transactions**

1. Go to **Agency View**.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Open **Billing**.
4. Select **Wallet & Transactions**.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080481002/original/IIEN7Ubr2gXKm5Tetei0GfYg_2JI6NHz5w.png?1788954174)**

### **Step 2: Open Transactions**

1. Select **Transactions** from Wallet & Transactions.
2. Review the transaction table.
3. Select the applicable sub-account when you are investigating usage for a specific location.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080481046/original/fxRS3XR3eThCauskCTT8kcX1606dhLByUQ.png?1788954199)

### **Step 3: Filter the Transaction List**

Use the available filters to narrow the transaction list.

Depending on the charge you are investigating, filter by:

- Sub-account
- Billing period
- Product
- Transaction Type
- Transaction ID

Locate the applicable Phone System transaction.

### 

### **Step 4: Review the Transaction Details**

Review the transaction's:

- **Billing Date**
- **Activity Date**
- **Description**
- **Amount**
- **Total Balance**

Use the transaction description to identify the product or Phone System activity responsible for the charge.

### 

### **Step 5: Compare the Charge With Current Pricing**

1. Open **Wallet & Transactions → Pricing**.
2. Search for the corresponding product or service.
3. Review its current pricing and billing unit.
4. Select the applicable country where country-specific pricing is available.
5. Compare the pricing information with the transaction you are reviewing.

The Pricing page provides the current HighLevel reference for wallet-billed product rates.

---

## **How To Export Wallet Transactions**

Export Center gives agencies a dedicated location for preparing transaction exports when a larger billing reconciliation needs to be completed outside HighLevel.

1. Go to **Agency View → Settings → Billing → Wallet & Transactions**.
2. Open **Transactions**.
3. Apply the filters needed for the transactions you want to investigate.
4. Select **Go to Export Center**, or open **Export Center** directly from the Wallet & Transactions navigation.
5. Configure the applicable export from Export Center.
6. Complete the export process using the options available in the current interface.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080481941/original/0fNH3zPBNHUdqY_ECy4d8Vu3f3ZdBZzC9A.png?1788954387)**

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does every Phone System charge receive the 5% markup?**  
No. Current HighLevel Phone System documentation identifies specific pass-through categories that receive the fixed 5% location-level markup. Other services follow their applicable documented rates.

**Q: Does agency rebilling replace the 5% Phone System markup?**  
No. Agency rebilling is separate. For categories where the 5% location-level markup applies, an agency-configured rebilling amount can be applied afterward when rebilling is enabled.

**Q: Do I need to change my agency's resale pricing?**  
Not solely because of the Phone System markup. Rebilling and reselling are configured separately from the underlying wallet charge.

**Q: Where can I see the current rate for a wallet-billed product?**  
Go to **Billing → Wallet & Transactions → Pricing**. The Wallet Pricing page provides centralized, automatically updated pricing for wallet-billed products.

**Q: Can I filter transactions for one sub-account?**  
Yes. Use the sub-account selector on the Transactions page to isolate applicable wallet activity for a specific location.

**Q: Does Auto-Recharge change because of the Phone System markup?**  
No. Auto-Recharge is a separate wallet-management setting and continues to follow the wallet configuration selected by the agency.

**Q: Are previous wallet transactions recalculated when pricing changes?**  
No. Historical transactions remain records of the charges that occurred at that time.

**Q: Where do I export wallet transactions?**  
Use **Wallet & Transactions → Export Center**. You can also access the Export Center from the Transactions page using **Go to Export Center**.

---
