- [How to Calculate SMS and MMS Costs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001203458)

title_en: Manage AI Employee & Email IP Billing
source_md:
Stay on top of AI Employee and Email IP subscription billing with a centralized view of subscribed sub-accounts in HighLevel. The enhanced billing card makes it easier to review subscription details such as purchase type, status, billing cycle, and purchase date without checking accounts individually. Use the billing card to understand how relevant subscriptions are associated with your sub-accounts and quickly review important billing information.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Billing Card for AI Employee & Email IP?](#What-is-the-Billing-Card-for-AI-Employee-&-Email-IP?)
- [Key Benefits of the Billing Card for AI Employee & Email IP](#Key-Benefits-of-the-Billing-Card-for-AI-Employee-&-Email-IP)
- [Understanding Purchase Types](#Understanding-Purchase-Types)
- [Understanding Subscription Details](#Understanding-Subscription-Details)
- [Navigating Multiple Sub-Accounts](#Navigating-Multiple-Sub-Accounts)
- [Agency Billing vs. Sub-Account Billing](#[H2]-Agency-Billing-vs.-Sub-Account-Billing)
- [How To Setup the Billing Card for AI Employee & Email IP](#[H2]-How-To-Setup-the-Billing-Card-for-AI-Employee-&-Email-IP)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#[H2]-Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#[H3]-Related-Articles)

---

# **What is the Billing Card for AI Employee & Email IP?**

The Billing Card for AI Employee & Email IP gives agencies a centralized way to review sub-account subscriptions associated with these services. Bringing subscription information together on the Agency Billing page makes it easier to understand which sub-accounts have relevant subscriptions and how those subscriptions are billed.

From the applicable billing card, you can select **Show Subaccounts** to open a tabular view of subscription information for the selected product.

For Email IP, the billing card relates to **Dedicated IP subscriptions used with LC Email**. Dedicated IPs give eligible agencies and sub-accounts access to an exclusive sending IP rather than relying solely on shared IP infrastructure. 

For more information about Dedicated IPs, see [LC Email – Complete Guide to Dedicated IP](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001152-what-is-a-dedicated-ip-in-lc-email-?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

---

## **Key Benefits of the Billing Card for AI Employee & Email IP**

Centralizing subscription details helps agencies understand billing relationships across sub-accounts without navigating into each account separately. The billing card provides an easier way to review relevant subscription 

information and identify how products were purchased.

- **Centralized Subscription Visibility:** Review relevant AI Employee or Email IP sub-account subscriptions from the Agency Billing page.
- **Purchase Source Visibility:** Identify how a subscription was purchased using the purchase-type information displayed in the billing table.
- **Billing Details at a Glance:** Review important subscription information such as billing cycle and purchase date from one view.
- **Subscription Status Visibility:** Check the displayed status of subscriptions while reviewing your sub-accounts.
- **Simplified Account Review:** Browse multiple subscription records without opening each sub-account individually.
- **Scalable Navigation:** Use pagination when available to move through larger subscription lists.

---

## **Understanding Purchase Types**

Purchase types help explain how a subscription originated, which can make it easier to understand the billing relationship between an agency, its SaaS offering, and the individual sub-account. Because available purchase methods can vary by product and account configuration, use the value displayed in the billing card as the source of truth for each subscription.

The billing card can identify subscription origins such as applicable:

- **SaaS Bundle:** The product is associated with an add-on included as part of a SaaS plan.
- **Agency Purchase:** The subscription originated from an agency-level purchase.
- **Location Purchase:** The subscription originated from the applicable sub-account or location.

AI Employee can also be offered through supported SaaS plan add-ons. HighLevel bills the agency for products bundled directly into a SaaS plan, so agencies should account for those costs when pricing their SaaS packages.

For details about bundling supported products with SaaS plans, see [SaaS: Reselling Add-Ons with SaaS Plans](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004175/?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

---

## **Understanding Subscription Details**

Each row in the billing table provides information about a subscription associated with a sub-account. Reviewing these details together can help agencies distinguish subscriptions, understand their billing schedules, and confirm when purchases were created.

Depending on the selected product and subscription, the billing card can display details such as:

- **Plan:** The applicable subscription plan or offering.
- **Purchase Type:** How the subscription originated.
- **Status:** The current status displayed for the subscription.
- **Billing Cycle:** The billing frequency associated with the subscription.
- **Purchase Date:** The date associated with the subscription purchase.

Use the information displayed in HighLevel when reviewing a specific account, as available plans and subscription configurations can vary.

---

## **Navigating Multiple Sub-Accounts**

Agencies managing many subscribed sub-accounts may have more records than can be conveniently displayed at once. Pagination keeps the billing table easier to review by dividing larger subscription lists into manageable groups.

When pagination controls appear at the bottom of the billing table, use them to move through the available subscription records.

---

## **Agency Billing vs. Sub-Account Billing**

Understanding which billing area you are viewing helps prevent confusion when investigating subscription charges. The Agency Billing page provides agency-level visibility into services and subscriptions, while the Billing Dashboard inside an individual sub-account focuses on that sub-account's own subscriptions, payment methods, invoices, transactions, and Wallet information.

Use the **AI Employee or Email IP billing card in Agency Billing** when you want to review applicable subscriptions across sub-accounts.

Use the individual **Sub-Account Billing Dashboard** when you need to review billing information belonging specifically to one sub-account.

For more information about billing within a sub-account, see [Account Billing Dashboard](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004182-account-billing-dashboard?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

---

## **How To Setup the Billing Card for AI Employee & Email IP**

The billing card does not require a separate configuration before you can review applicable subscription records. Accessing it from Agency Settings gives you a consolidated view of the subscriptions associated with the selected product.

**Step 1: Open Agency Settings**

1. From **Agency View**, click **Settings**.
2. Select **Billing**.

**Step 2: Locate the Subscription Card**

1. Find the applicable **AI Employee** or **Email IP** subscription card in the Billing area.
2. Click **Show Subaccounts**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082656078/original/uBWQ-5EPc2gcIdny9uA7ig9FOv79jhOY8Q.png?1791297923)

HighLevel uses the **Show Subaccounts** control on supported agency billing subscription views to display location-level subscription information.

**Step 3: Review Sub-Account Subscription Details**

1. Review the sub-accounts displayed in the table.
2. Use the available columns to check subscription details such as:

   - Plan
   - Purchase Type
   - Status
   - Billing Cycle
   - Purchase Date  
       
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082656247/original/8HhsrXBwZ28SfheJXnhVTvjMs62oyVDmsA.png?1791298022)
3. Compare the displayed information when you need to identify how a particular subscription was purchased or billed.

**Step 4: Navigate Additional Records**

1. Scroll to the bottom of the subscription list when more records are available.
2. Use the displayed pagination controls to review additional records.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083333408/original/8dDE8WsxP5hm1JqFTdtFegdd9RH9XjIfrg.gif?1791991366)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Is Email IP the same as a Dedicated IP in LC Email?**

A: The Email IP billing context refers to Dedicated IP subscriptions associated with LC Email. A Dedicated IP gives an eligible agency or sub-account an exclusive sending IP that can be associated with dedicated sending domains.

**Q: Why might different sub-accounts show different purchase types?**

A: Subscriptions can originate through different purchasing workflows, such as an agency purchase, a location-level purchase, or an applicable SaaS bundle. Review the Purchase Type displayed for the specific subscription to determine how it originated.

**Q: Does a SaaS Bundle mean the sub-account is billed separately for the add-on?**

A: Not necessarily. For products bundled directly into supported SaaS plans, HighLevel documentation states that the agency is responsible for the bundled add-on cost. The agency can account for that cost when determining the customer-facing price of the SaaS plan.

**Q: Where can I learn more about AI Employee plans and rebilling?**

A: Review the **AI Employee: Access, Rebilling and Reselling** article for information about AI Employee plans, sub-account access, usage, rebilling, and reselling options.

**Q: Where should I look if I need billing information for only one sub-account?**

A: Open the applicable sub-account and go to **Settings > Billing**. The Sub-Account Billing Dashboard contains that account's subscriptions, payment methods, billing information, invoices, transaction history, and Wallet details.

**Q: Can an agency manage eligible location subscriptions from Agency Billing?**

A: HighLevel supports agency-side management and cancellation for eligible location-level reselling subscriptions. Available actions depend on the subscription. Review the available controls for the applicable subscription before making changes.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [AI Employee: Access, Rebilling and Reselling](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003906?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [LC Email – Complete Guide to Dedicated IP](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001152-what-is-a-dedicated-ip-in-lc-email-?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [HighLevel Pricing Guide](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001156-highlevel-pricing-guide?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [SaaS: Reselling Add-Ons with SaaS Plans](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004175/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Billing Related Questions for Agencies](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001208376-common-billing-related-questions-for-agencies?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Account Billing Dashboard](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004182-account-billing-dashboard?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: Workflow Trigger - Pipeline Stage Changed
source_md:
Tracking and managing opportunities efficiently is key to maintaining a streamlined sales process. The Pipeline Stage Changed Workflow Trigger automates actions when an opportunity moves from one stage to another, ensuring timely follow-ups, notifications, and updates. This guide will walk you through what this trigger does, its benefits, and how to configure it for optimized pipeline management.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Pipeline Stage Changed Workflow Trigger?](#What-is-the-Pipeline-Stage-Changed-Workflow-Trigger?)
- [Key Benefits of the Pipeline Stage Changed Workflow Trigger](#Key-Benefits-of-the-Pipeline-Stage-Changed-Workflow-Trigger)
- [Configuring the Pipeline Stage Changed Workflow Trigger](#Configuring-the-Pipeline-Stage-Changed-Workflow-Trigger)
  - [Access Workflow Builder](#Access-Workflow-Builder%C2%A0)
  - [Choosing the Workflow Trigger](#Choosing-the-Workflow-Trigger)
  - [Name your Trigger](#Name-your-Trigger)
  - [Setting Up Filters](#Setting-Up-Filters)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions%C2%A0)

---

# **What is the Pipeline Stage Changed Workflow Trigger?**

The Pipeline Stage Changed Workflow Trigger activates when an opportunity moves from one stage to another within a sales pipeline. It helps businesses automate workflows based on stage transitions, ensuring that no lead falls through the cracks. This trigger allows users to define actions that should occur when an opportunity progresses, regresses, or is reassigned to a new pipeline stage.

---

## **Key Benefits of the Pipeline Stage Changed Workflow Trigger**

- **Automates Follow-Ups:**Ensures that each stage change prompts timely notifications, keeping sales reps engaged with prospects.

- **Reduces Manual Work:**Eliminates the need for manually tracking pipeline movements, freeing up time for strategic sales activities.

- **Enhances Pipeline Visibility:**Provides real-time insights into opportunity progress, allowing better forecasting and decision-making.

- **Customizable Filtering:**Allows users to set up workflows based on specific conditions such as pipeline, stage, assigned user, or lead value.

- **Improves Response Time:**Automates outreach and internal communication, ensuring quick action at crucial sales stages.

---

## **Configuring the Pipeline Stage Changed Workflow Trigger**

### **Access Workflow Builder**

Navigate to Automation > Workflows in your CRM dashboard. Click Create New Workflow or edit an existing one.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042344919/original/Z7YdmZWW7YgF69trLKngBYbP9khNZlzM7Q.jpeg?1740653065)

### **Choosing the Workflow Trigger**

Click + Add New Trigger and search for Pipeline Stage Changed in the list. Select Pipeline Stage Changed as the trigger.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042344941/original/kfZD3Kxp2NTZ21LG1l8qVDolI6EWELeE-Q.jpeg?1740653081)

### **Name your Trigger**

Give your workflow trigger a clear and descriptive name that reflects its purpose. This helps you quickly identify the trigger’s function when managing multiple workflows.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042345055/original/dXHpPUsrNAiJDuS17dtyEYvBnHSGw1O1DA.jpeg?1740653162)

### **Setting Up Filters**

Filters help you control when and how a workflow is triggered by setting specific conditions that must be met. Instead of triggering the workflow for every opportunity change, filters allow you to target only the ones that matter most to your business. Whether you want to automate actions for opportunities in a specific pipeline, those assigned to a certain team member, or only when a deal is marked as lost for a particular reason, filters give you the flexibility to refine and customize your automation. This ensures that workflows are more precise, relevant, and aligned with your sales process.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065763970/original/xa_HvOOR8vPFm_8fQBtF4lMuOsVb_tAy5g.png?1772101325)

#### **Assigned To Filter**

The Assigned To filter ensures that workflows are triggered based on the user assigned to an opportunity. This filter is particularly useful for directing follow-ups, assigning tasks, or notifying specific team members when an opportunity moves through the pipeline.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042363650/original/j4BOkGGKQ7xDL_xBkrZXtqgtrryqMg8biQ.png?1740664257)

#### **Tag filter (formerly “Has Tag”)**

Use Tag filters to trigger workflows only for opportunities that match specific tag conditions. The Tag filter allows you to trigger workflows only when an opportunity contains a specific tag, making it particularly useful for segmenting opportunities, prioritizing leads, and automating targeted actions. Tags serve as labels to categorize opportunities based on attributes such as lead type, priority, source, or other relevant classifications. When setting up the Tag filter, you can specify which tag(s) must be present for the workflow to activate, ensuring automation is applied to the right opportunities.

**Example:** If an opportunity is tagged as “High Priority,” the workflow activates when it moves to the next stage.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155065763802/original/vDBNog5lhciogk9I3LPoOK0x7CzN_XOshg.png?1772101275)

#### **In Pipeline Filter**

#### 

The In Pipeline filter limits the workflow trigger to a specific pipeline, ensuring that automation is only activated for opportunities within the selected pipeline. This filter is particularly useful for businesses managing multiple pipelines for different sales processes, client types, or service offerings. By specifying a pipeline, users can ensure that workflows are applied only to relevant opportunities, preventing unnecessary automation across unrelated pipelines.

**Example:** The workflow only activates when an opportunity moves within the “Enterprise Sales” pipeline.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042363876/original/oAKEstTXufxn_LLmvtnYhsr8_NdH6YWYfA.png?1740664390)

#### **Lead Value Filter**

The Lead Value filter triggers workflows based on the monetary value assigned to an opportunity. This allows businesses to automate actions depending on the financial significance of a lead, ensuring that high-value deals receive appropriate follow-ups while lower-value opportunities are handled differently.

**Example:**If an opportunity’s value exceeds $10,000, notify the sales manager.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042363981/original/ih30kq-4ZMDpZHus1Oh3AXUEyk7BrYyQtw.png?1740664432)

#### **Lost Reason Filter**

The Lost Reason filter triggers workflows when an opportunity is marked as Lost and a specific reason is assigned, allowing businesses to track why deals are being lost, automate follow-up actions, and implement strategies to recover potential customers or prevent similar losses in the future. When an opportunity moves to the Lost stage in the pipeline, users can assign a reason (e.g., “Price Too High,” “Competitor Chosen,” “No Response”), ensuring that workflows activate only when a particular lost reason is selected.

**Example:** If the lost reason is “Budget Constraints,” send an automated follow-up email offering a flexible pricing plan.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042364228/original/kki_iWGEv2YLSlewo_PlI4yixV68EY5vVQ.png?1740664590)

#### **Pipeline Stage Filter**

The Pipeline Stage filter triggers workflows when an opportunity moves to a specific stage within a pipeline. This allows businesses to automate actions based on stage transitions, ensuring timely follow-ups, task assignments, or notifications as opportunities progress. Users can define which stage transition should activate the workflow, making it easier to manage leads and track sales pipeline movements efficiently.

**Example:** When an opportunity moves from “Negotiation” to “Closed Won,” notify the finance team.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042364328/original/JHzyQQFJyOxBYMLPCT2PKB8tlFggH5aVCQ.png?1740664628)

#### **Status Filter**

The Status filter triggers workflows based on the current status of an opportunity. This ensures that automation is executed when an opportunity reaches a specific stage in the sales process, helping teams track and manage their pipeline effectively. Users can select from the following status options:

- **Open:**The opportunity is still active and in progress.
- **Won:**The deal has been successfully closed.
- **Lost:**The opportunity was not converted into a sale.
- **Abandoned:**The opportunity is no longer being pursued.

**Example:** If an opportunity is marked as “Won,” trigger a welcome email sequence.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155042364875/original/g0iRsRHN_JARCYsJozticR4tVJUgZ-7hIQ.png?1740664959)

### **Defining Workflow Actions**

Once the trigger is set, define the actions that should follow when an opportunity changes stages.

- **Send a Notification:** Notify the assigned sales rep about the stage change.
- **Update Opportunity Details:**Modify fields such as status, priority, or tags automatically.
- **Create a Follow-Up Task:**Assign a task to the sales team to reach out to the prospect.
- **Trigger Another Workflow:**Activate additional workflows based on opportunity progression.
- **Send an Email to the Contact:**Automate customer communication based on pipeline movement.

### **Saving and Publishing the Workflow**

1. After configuring filters and actions, click **Save Trigger** to apply changes.
2. Ensure all necessary workflow steps are in place, then click **Publish**to activate automation.
3. **Test**the workflow by manually moving an opportunity through stages to confirm expected behavior.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q1: What happens if an opportunity is moved manually?**

If an opportunity is manually moved to another stage, the workflow still triggers, provided it meets the configured filter conditions.

**Q2: Can I use multiple filters within the same workflow?**

Yes, you can combine multiple filters to create highly specific automation rules, such as triggering actions only when an opportunity in a particular pipeline and stage is assigned to a specific user.

**Q3: How does this trigger interact with other opportunity-based triggers?**

The Pipeline Stage Changed trigger is independent of other triggers like Opportunity Status Changed or Opportunity Created. If needed, you can configure workflows using multiple triggers to cover different automation needs.

**Q4: What if an opportunity moves back to a previous stage?**

If an opportunity regresses to a prior stage, the workflow will trigger again, provided the conditions match.

**Q5: Can I track historical stage movements using this trigger?**

No, this trigger only activates upon real-time stage transitions. However, you can review historical changes in the opportunity’s activity log.

title_en: Service Area Businesses in Prospecting: Search, Audit, and Generate Heatmaps
source_md:
Service Area Business support in HighLevel helps you find, add, and audit businesses that do not operate from a public storefront. This expands Prospecting to include more real-world local businesses, such as home service providers and consultants, while keeping audit scoring accurate for their business type. You can also generate Marketing Audit Reports and Local SEO Heatmaps for these businesses without relying on older workaround-heavy processes.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Service Area Business (SAB) Support in Prospecting?](#What-is-Service-Area-Business-(SAB)-Support-in-Prospecting?)
- [Key Benefits of Service Area Business (SAB) Support](#Key-Benefits-of-Service-Area-Business-(SAB)-Support)
- [Search and Discover Service Area Businesses](#Search-and-Discover-Service-Area-Businesses)
- [Add and Audit Service Area Business Prospects](#Add-and-Audit-Service-Area-Business-Prospects)
- [Google Business Profile Scoring for Service Area Businesses](#Google-Business-Profile-Scoring-for-Service-Area-Businesses)
- [Local SEO Heatmaps for Service Area Businesses](#Local-SEO-Heatmaps-for-Service-Area-Businesses)
- [How To Setup Service Area Business (SAB) Prospecting](#How-To-Setup-Service-Area-Business-(SAB)-Prospecting)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Service Area Business (SAB) Support in Prospecting?**

Service Area Business support allows HighLevel to include businesses that serve customers in a region without displaying a public business address. This matters because many local businesses operate from service areas instead of storefronts, and they still need accurate prospecting, reporting, and local SEO analysis. With this update, Prospecting supports these businesses across the full workflow, from discovery to audit reporting and heatmap generation.

A Service Area Business, or SAB, is a business that serves customers at their location or across a service region rather than at a public storefront. In HighLevel, SAB support means these businesses can now be surfaced in Prospecting search results, added as prospects, audited through Marketing Audit Reports, and analyzed with Local SEO Heatmaps.

---

## **Key Benefits of Service Area Business (SAB) Support**

Supporting Service Area Businesses makes Prospecting more useful for agencies and teams that work with real local service markets. It also improves reporting accuracy by adjusting expectations based on business type rather than forcing storefront-based requirements onto every business.

- **Broader prospecting reach**: Discover service-based businesses that may not have appeared in older storefront-focused search experiences.
- **Accurate Google Business Profile scoring**: Businesses without a storefront are not incorrectly penalized for lacking a public address.
- **Full audit support**: Generate complete Marketing Audit Reports for SABs just like other eligible prospects.
- **Heatmap access for service businesses**: Create Local SEO Heatmaps for service-area businesses to evaluate local search visibility.
- **Better fit for local agencies**: Prospect more relevant business types, including providers that serve customers across a city or region.

---

## **Search and Discover Service Area Businesses**

Finding Service Area Businesses directly in Prospecting helps reduce missed opportunities and makes it easier to prospect in industries where many businesses do not have storefronts. This is especially valuable for users targeting local service markets instead of retail-style locations.

You can now search for Service Area Businesses directly in the Prospecting Tool. These businesses appear in search results as part of the normal prospecting experience, so there is no separate workflow required just to discover them.

- Search for prospects using your normal business category and location terms.
- Review the search results as you normally would.
- Include service-based businesses in your prospect list when they match your targeting criteria.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069614114/original/0b1VQuPbwo2az2TPDYB03aA_Fdhfce2TLA.png?1776777317)

---

## **Add and Audit Service Area Business Prospects**

Being able to add and audit SABs without a visible storefront address removes a major barrier for service-based businesses. This allows you to evaluate more prospects using the same audit-driven sales workflow used for other local businesses.

Service Area Business prospects can now be added and audited in HighLevel even when they do not display a public business address. Once added, you can generate a full Marketing Audit Report for the prospect.

- Open the Prospecting Tool and locate the business you want to review.
- Add the business as a prospect.
- Generate a Marketing Audit Report for that prospect.
- Review the report sections to evaluate the prospect’s digital presence, listings, reputation, SEO, and website performance.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069615414/original/YqjltdsgcUf4E49N5qLTuDI8vThJk3siFQ.png?1776778020)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069615551/original/xLpRNT0OAgdV23Kz5GDrXtRBHcg60TdWsg.png?1776778113)

---

## **Google Business Profile Scoring for Service Area Businesses**

Accurate scoring matters because service-area businesses should not be measured against storefront-only requirements. HighLevel adjusts the audit experience to reflect the business type, helping users avoid misleading score interpretations.

For Service Area Businesses, the business address field is excluded from Google Business Profile evaluation when a storefront address does not apply. Instead of showing a misleading pass or fail indicator, the report displays a neutral status to show that the field is not relevant for that business type.

**What to expect in the Marketing Audit Report:**

- The Business Address field may display: **Not applicable (service-based business)**
- The report does not use misleading red or green address indicators for SABs
- Scoring is adjusted based on business type

**Recommended note for the article:**

- Scores are adjusted based on business type. Businesses without a storefront are not evaluated on Business Address.

Proper setup helps ensure that service-based businesses move smoothly through the full Prospecting workflow. Following the correct process makes it easier to search for eligible businesses, generate accurate reports, and understand business-type-specific scoring.

1. Go to **Reporting** and open the **Prospecting Tool**.
2. Enter your target keyword and location to search for local businesses.
3. Review the search results and select a Service Area Business that matches your targeting criteria.
4. Add the business as a prospect.
5. Generate a **Marketing Audit Report** for the prospect.
6. Review the **Google Business Profile** section and confirm whether the Business Address field displays **Not applicable (service-based business)** when relevant.

title_en: How to View Snapshot Load History in a Subaccount
source_md:
Snapshot Load History gives agencies a clear record of the Snapshots loaded into a HighLevel subaccount. Users can see which Snapshot was loaded, when it was loaded, which version was used, and who completed the load. They can also review each load and inspect the assets included, making account reviews and troubleshooting faster.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Snapshot Load History Columns](#Snapshot-Load-History-Columns)
- [Load History Columns](#Load-History-Columns)
- [Asset Details](#Asset-Details)
- [Open Snapshot Load History](#Open-Snapshot-Load-History)
- [Review All Snapshots Loaded into the Subaccount](#Review-All-Snapshots-Loaded-into-the-Subaccount)
- [Review a Specific Snapshot’s Load History](#Review-a-Specific-Snapshot%E2%80%99s-Load-History)
- [Review the Assets Included in a Load](#Review-the-Assets-Included-in-a-Load)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Is Subaccount Snapshot Load History?**

Subaccount Snapshot Load History is an activity record for Snapshots loaded into a specific subaccount. It provides a clear path from a summary of all loaded Snapshots to the history of one Snapshot and then to the assets included in a particular load.

The feature contains three levels of information:

1. **Snapshot Load History:** Lists all Snapshots loaded into the subaccount.
2. **Load History:** Lists each time a selected Snapshot was loaded.
3. **Asset Details:** Shows the asset categories included in a selected load and their statuses.

Snapshot Load History is different from Snapshot Push Update History. Snapshot Load History starts from one subaccount and shows the Snapshots loaded into it. Snapshot Push Update History starts from an agency Snapshot and shows how an update was sent across subaccounts.

---

## **Key Benefits of Snapshot Load History**

Snapshot Load History gives agencies a reliable record of previous Snapshot activity, helping teams understand account changes without relying on notes, support tickets, or information from other users.

- **Faster troubleshooting:** Identify which Snapshot and version may have introduced a particular account setup.
- **Clear accountability:** See who completed the most recent load and who completed each earlier load.
- **Better visibility:** Review the complete Snapshot setup history of a subaccount from one place.
- **Version tracking:** Confirm which version of a Snapshot was used for each load.
- **Detailed asset review:** Open a load to review the asset categories included and their current status.
- **Easier team handoffs:** Give support and implementation teams a shared record of previous Snapshot activity.

---

## **Information Available in Snapshot Load History**

Each history view answers a different question about the Snapshot activity in the selected subaccount. Understanding the available columns helps users locate the right Snapshot, load, or asset details quickly.

### 

### **Snapshot Load History Columns**

The first screen lists the Snapshots that have been loaded into the subaccount.

- **Snapshot name:** The name of the Snapshot loaded into the subaccount.
- **Last loaded version:** The most recent version of that Snapshot loaded into the subaccount.
- **Type:** The source or ownership type assigned to the Snapshot.
- **Last loaded on:** The date and time of the most recent load.
- **Last loaded by:** The user who completed the most recent load.

The interface may display a dash when user information is unavailable.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076490674/original/wtywvJGa8w3pXelNAy8S-gFIr1BXEm6iPA.png?1784636290)**

---

### **Load History Columns**

Selecting a Snapshot opens a list of each time that Snapshot was loaded into the subaccount.

- **Version:** The Snapshot version used for the load.
- **Assets:** The number of assets associated with the load.
- **Status:** The result or current state of the load.
- **Loaded on:** The date and time the load occurred.
- **Loaded by:** The user who started the load.

Snapshot versions help users identify the exact version loaded into the subaccount. Snapshot Version Management separately shows what changed between versions after a Snapshot was refreshed.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076490937/original/DonXQ9rlTRQ-Jjm0EqN5y-mXK8wKk-yKDw.png?1784636445)**

---

### **Asset Details**

Selecting a load opens its Asset Details screen. Assets are grouped by category so users can review what was included and check the status of each category.

Visible examples may include:

- Custom Values
- Membership Products
- Workflows
- Custom Objects
- Funnels & Websites
- Custom Metrics
- Forms
- Membership Offers
- Tags

The visible status labels may include **Success** and **Processing**. A processing status means HighLevel is still working on that asset category.

The Asset Details screen shows assets associated with a historical load. It is different from the Snapshot Asset Viewer, which shows the assets currently stored in a Snapshot.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076491307/original/LihaEqEGWbVtESLF8miBU2NIofXSuRxdjg.png?1784636581)**

---

## **Searching Snapshot Load History**

Search helps users find a Snapshot quickly when a subaccount has a long load history. The search field checks Snapshot names and updates the table to show matching results.

To search the history:

1. Click the **Search by snapshot name** field.
2. Enter all or part of the Snapshot name.
3. Review the matching records.
4. Click **Clear search** when no results appear or when you want to return to the complete list.

The table also includes page navigation and a rows-per-page selector for reviewing longer histories.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076491754/original/bpFogwBbGXkR9iTKHhSR9nJ2z3iatIOs9w.png?1784636714)**

---

## **Snapshot Load History Compared with Other Snapshot Records**

HighLevel provides different history and review tools for different Snapshot tasks. Choosing the correct view helps users avoid confusing a Snapshot’s contents, versions, pushes, and subaccount load history.

- **Subaccount Snapshot Load History:** Shows every Snapshot loaded into one subaccount.
- **Snapshot Push Update History:** Shows the results of a Snapshot update pushed across subaccounts.
- **Snapshot Version Management:** Shows assets added, removed, or synchronized when a Snapshot was refreshed.
- **Snapshot Asset Viewer:** Shows the assets currently contained in a Snapshot.
- **Snapshot Load Retry:** Provides recovery options for eligible failed Snapshot loads.

---

## **How To View Snapshot Load History**

Opening Snapshot Load History from the correct subaccount ensures that the records apply to the account you are reviewing. From there, users can move from the full Snapshot list to a specific load and its asset details.

### 

### **Open Snapshot Load History**

1. Go to **Agency View**.
2. Open **Sub-Accounts**.
3. Select the subaccount you want to review.  
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076489897/original/1uGZfNSZoZ6ZnKhkzyuifDQVOOQUqDDazg.png?1784635987)
4. Click **Actions**.
5. Open **Snapshot actions**.
6. Click **View snapshot history**.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076490321/original/sYHIsel6Nt1EH1iLfYP1c9ntS5RpdYsN7g.png?1784636134)**

### 

### **Review All Snapshots Loaded into the Subaccount**

1. Review the **Snapshot Load History** table.
2. Locate the required Snapshot by name.
3. Check its last loaded version, type, date, and user.
4. Use the search field when the list contains many Snapshots.
5. Click the Snapshot row to open its detailed history.

### 

### **Review a Specific Snapshot’s Load History**

1. Select a Snapshot from the main history table.
2. Review every recorded load for that Snapshot.
3. Use the **Version** column to identify the version used.
4. Check the asset count and load status.
5. Review when the load occurred and who started it.
6. Select a load to open its Asset Details.

### 

### **Review the Assets Included in a Load**

1. Open the required Snapshot.
2. Select the load you want to inspect.
3. Review the asset categories on the **Asset Details** screen.
4. Expand a category when additional details are available.
5. Check the status shown beside each category.
6. Use the asset search field to find a particular asset or category.

Snapshot loading and Snapshot history serve different purposes. Loading applies selected Snapshot assets to a subaccount, while history provides a record of the loads that already occurred.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does Snapshot Load History show every Snapshot loaded into the subaccount?**  
It lists the Snapshot records available for the selected subaccount and shows the most recent load information for each one.

**Q: Can I see every time the same Snapshot was loaded?**  
Yes. Select the Snapshot from the main history table to open its individual Load History.

**Q: What does Last loaded version mean?**  
It identifies the most recent version of that Snapshot loaded into the selected subaccount.

**Q: Why does the Last loaded by field show a dash?**  
A dash indicates that user information is not available for that history record.

**Q: What does Processing mean in Asset Details?**  
Processing indicates that HighLevel is still working on that asset category. Check the history again after the load has had time to finish.

**Q: Does the Asset Details screen show what is currently inside the Snapshot?**  
No. It shows the assets associated with a particular historical load. Use the Snapshot Asset Viewer to inspect what the Snapshot currently contains.

**Q: Can I load a Snapshot from the history screen?**  
Snapshot loading is a separate action. Use the subaccount’s Snapshot actions to start a new load.

**Q: Is Snapshot Load History the same as Push Update History?**  
No. Subaccount Snapshot Load History shows the Snapshots loaded into one subaccount. Push Update History shows the results of sending an update from one Snapshot to multiple subaccounts.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Snapshots – Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982511-snapshots-overview)
- [Load Snapshots Into Existing Sub-Account](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982582-load-snapshots-into-existing-sub-account)
- [Snapshot Push Update History](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004171-snapshot-push-update-history)
- [Snapshot Version Management](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006497-snapshot-version-management)

title_en: LC Email: Email Service Provider Block Notification - Email Sending Temporarily Restricted (Action Required)
source_md:
Email Deliverability

New ESP Block Policy — Action Required

A full walkthrough of the new ESP Block System, the steps to take right now, and how to keep your sub-account out of permanent suspension.

Implementation Timeline

**Effective Date: 12th Feb 2026.** This new ESP Block Policy will be implemented on 12th Feb 2026. Current users will receive advance notification and have time to review their email practices before enforcement begins.

**What you should do now:** review your current bounce classification data, implement recommended email authentication and best practices, clean your email lists and improve content quality, and monitor your ESP block rates closely.

Urgent — Action Required Within 24-48 Hours

**Your sub-account has been temporarily restricted from sending emails due to ESP (Email Service Provider) blocks.** This is part of our Anti-Spam Policy designed to protect your sender reputation and ensure high deliverability rates.

## What Are ESP Blocks?

ESP blocks occur when major email providers (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook, etc.) reject your emails due to:

- Authentication failures (DMARC, SPF, DKIM issues)
- Poor sender reputation
- Content that appears spam-like
- Policy violations
- Technical configuration problems

Why This Matters

Unlike regular bounces, ESP blocks are calculated separately and trigger immediate restrictions to protect your long-term email deliverability.

## New ESP Block System

The block system escalates through three temporary blocks, with warning emails sent before each one. Here is the full progression:

| ESP Block Rate | Action | Duration | Block Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3% | Warning Email Sent | Immediate notification | Pre-Block Warning |
| 5% | Email sending suspended | 12 hours | 1st Block |
| 3% (after 1st block) | Critical Warning Email Sent | Immediate notification | Pre-2nd Block Warning |
| 5% (after 1st block) | Email sending suspended | 24 hours | 2nd Block |
| 3% (after 2nd block) | Final Warning Email Sent | Immediate notification | Pre-3rd Block Final Warning |
| 5% (after 2nd block) | PERMANENT SUSPENSION | Permanent | 3rd Block — FINAL |

Critical

All blocks are reset after 7 consecutive days of maintaining ESP block rates below 1%.

Good to Know

In this release, email sending will not be permanently disabled. Each block will be temporary and limited to a 24-hour duration only.

If your email service is **blocked** due to **ESP Block Detected**, you will see the following error message displayed as a **top banner** inside the affected subaccount:

Email sending is blocked due to a high number of spam blocks from email providers.

![ESP block error banner displayed inside the subaccount](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064792608/original/5TW75eQ0t8kTt0vQOwFX3kr_-mcIEgdcDQ.png?1770907247)

This block is enforced to protect email deliverability and prevent further reputation damage with Email Service Providers (ESPs).

Related Reading

Refer to [*ESP Block Detected — Immediate Action Required to Restore Email Sending*](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007341-lc-email-email-service-provider-block-detected-immediate-action-required-to-restore-email-sending) for the recovery walkthrough.

Setup Guide

Take Action Now

Three immediate steps, then a three-phase preparation plan.

## Immediate Steps Required

Step 1

Access the Bounce Classification feature

1. Log into your sub-account.
2. Navigate to **Sub-account Settings → Email Services → Bounce Classification**.
3. Review your ESP block categories and error details.
4. Identify the highest volume ESP blocks affecting your sub-account.

Step 2

Identify your primary issues

The Bounce Classification feature will show you:

- **Specific ESP block categories** (DMARC failures, reputation issues, etc.)
- **Error volumes** by provider (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook)
- **Detailed error messages** with exact reasons for blocks
- **Recommended actions** for each block type

Step 3

Implement fixes

Based on your bounce classification results, you'll need to address:

- Email authentication setup (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)
- Content and template improvements
- List hygiene and engagement issues
- Technical configuration problems

## Prepare for the New Policy

Phase 1

Audit your current performance

Check Bounce Classification Dashboard

- Navigate to Sub-account Settings → Email Services → Bounce Classification
- Identify current ESP block rates and categories
- Review recent email campaign performance
- Document problem areas that need attention

Analyze Historical Data

- Review bounce rates over the past 30 days
- Identify patterns in ESP blocks
- Check which email providers are blocking you most

Phase 2

Implement email best practices

Email Authentication Setup

- Configure SPF records to include the platform's sending IPs
- Set up DKIM signing for your domain
- Implement DMARC policy (start with p=none for monitoring)
- Verify all DNS records are properly configured

List Hygiene and Quality

- Remove all bounced and invalid email addresses
- Implement double opt-in for new subscribers
- Segment lists based on engagement levels
- Remove inactive subscribers (6+ months no engagement)

Content Optimization

- Avoid spam trigger words and excessive promotional language
- Maintain proper text-to-image ratio (60:40)
- Include clear unsubscribe links
- Use professional, branded email templates
- Test content with spam checking tools

Phase 3

Monitor and test

Pre-Implementation Testing

- Send test emails to major providers (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook)
- Monitor delivery rates and engagement metrics
- Use email testing tools to check spam scores
- Verify email authentication is working correctly

Ongoing Monitoring

- Check bounce classification dashboard daily
- Monitor ESP block rates closely
- Track engagement metrics (opens, clicks, unsubscribes)
- Set up alerts for unusual bounce patterns

## Why This Matters

Protecting Your Business

- ESP blocks damage your sender reputation permanently
- Poor reputation leads to emails landing in spam folders
- Reduced deliverability impacts your business revenue
- Recovery can take weeks or months without proper action

Industry Standards

- Major ESPs are increasingly strict about email quality
- Authentication requirements are now mandatory
- Content filtering has become more sophisticated
- Sender reputation affects all future campaigns

## Next Steps

Step 1 — Analyze

Use the Bounce Classification feature to understand your specific ESP blocks.

Step 2 — Fix

Address the identified issues using our detailed support articles.

Step 3 — Monitor

Track your improvements through the bounce classification dashboard.

Step 4 — Verify

Ensure fixes are working before resuming normal sending.

## Support Resources

Bounce Classification Feature

- Access detailed ESP block analysis
- View error categories and volumes
- Get specific recommendations for your sub-account
- Monitor improvement progress

**Category-Specific Support Articles.** Each ESP block category in your bounce classification links to detailed fix guides:

**DMARC Authentication Failures**

**Domain / IP Reputation Issues**

**Content and Spam Filtering**

**Technical Configuration Problems**

**And more...**

## Time-Sensitive Actions

Before Policy Implementation

- Complete email authentication setup
- Clean all email lists thoroughly
- Optimize email content and templates
- Test email delivery across major providers
- Monitor bounce classification dashboard daily

Within 24 Hours of Warning

- Review bounce classification data immediately
- Identify top 3 ESP block categories
- Begin implementing critical fixes (authentication, major content issues)

Within 48 Hours of Block

- Complete all technical fixes
- Clean email lists and remove problematic content
- Test email delivery to major providers

Ongoing

- Monitor bounce classification dashboard daily
- Maintain email best practices
- Regular list hygiene and engagement monitoring

## Need Help?

Self-Service Options

- Use the Bounce Classification feature for detailed analysis
- Follow category-specific support articles for step-by-step fixes
- Access our email best practices documentation

Contact Support

If you need assistance interpreting your bounce classification data or implementing fixes, contact our support team with:

- Your sub-account details
- Screenshots from the Bounce Classification feature
- Specific error messages you're seeing

## Important Reminders

- **ESP blocks are separate from regular bounces** — they require immediate attention.
- **Each provider has different requirements** — use bounce classification to see provider-specific issues.
- **Prevention is better than cure** — implement proper email practices from the start.
- **Time is critical** — delays in fixing issues can lead to permanent restrictions.
- **You have 30 days to prepare** — use this time wisely to optimize your email practices.

Take Action Now

Your email deliverability and business success depend on taking action now. Start with the Bounce Classification feature and begin preparing for the new policy implementation.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: When does this new policy take effect?

The ESP Block System will be implemented on **12 Feb 2026**, giving all users 30 days to prepare and optimize their email practices.

Q: What happens to my current ESP blocks?

Your ESP block history will reset on the implementation date. However, we strongly recommend addressing any current issues before the policy goes live to ensure smooth operations.

Q: How do blocks reset?

Blocks reset after **7 consecutive days** of maintaining ESP block rates below 1%. However, if you receive 3 blocks within any 7-day period, permanent suspension will occur.

Q: Can permanent suspensions be reversed?

Permanent unblocking **cannot be done automatically**. A manual review by the Support team is required, and unblocking is not guaranteed — it depends on compliance with email best practices. This is why we provide multiple warnings and temporary suspensions before taking final action.

Q: Will I receive notifications before each block?

Yes — you will receive warning emails when your ESP block rate reaches 3%, giving you time to take corrective action before the 5% threshold triggers a block.

Q: What if I'm currently above 3% ESP block rate?

Use the preparation period before **12th Feb 2026** to address these issues. The block system will not be enforced until the implementation date, giving you time to fix problems.

Q: How is this different from regular bounce management?

ESP blocks are calculated separately from regular bounces and have their own block system. Regular bounces (invalid addresses, full mailboxes) are handled differently than ESP blocks (reputation, authentication, policy issues).

We're Here to Help

This policy is designed to protect your sender reputation and ensure long-term email deliverability success. We're here to help you prepare and succeed with these new requirements.

# **For the privacy policy page:**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155026164330/original/mBeoYVqSjfwYMj9ZcZm1FGjthVGYaR4BHg.jpeg?1715892982)

# 

**A compliant Privacy Policy must state:**

**"No mobile information will be shared with third parties/affiliates for marketing/promotional purposes. Information sharing to subcontractors in support services, such as customer service is permitted. All other use case categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties."**

# Your Twilio subaccounts will be suspended due to non-compliant activities:

- High Error Rate
- High Opt-Out rates

## **High Error Rate**

A high error rate can be driven by one error code or by the sum of several collectively. ([see the Error and Warning Dictionary for a full list of all possible Twilio REST API error codes](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors)).

## **High Opt-Out Rate**

A high opt-out rate is an indication of unwanted/unsolicited messaging.

Your targeted audience must be aware of what they are signing up for and your website/form must clearly state how their information will be used and they have to provide consent to it accordingly. For example, you can't obtain the consent of message recipients by purchasing a phone list from another party.

**Consent / Opt-in:**

Prior to sending the first message, you must obtain agreement from the message recipient to communicate with them - this is referred to as "consent", you must make clear to the individual they are agreeing to receive messages of the type you're going to send. You need to keep a record of the consent, such as a copy of the document or form that the message recipient signed, or a timestamp of when the customer completed a sign-up flow. Consent can't be bought, sold, or exchanged. For example, you can't obtain the consent of message recipients by purchasing a phone list from another party.

## **Lack of Sender Identification**

Every message you send must clearly identify you (the party that obtained the opt-in from the recipient) as the sender, except in follow-up messages of an ongoing conversation. Such that the message recipient can immediately associate where/whom they have given consent to.

**Lack of Opt-Out Language**

The initial message that you send to an individual needs to include the following language: "Reply STOP to unsubscribe," or the equivalent using another standard opt-out keyword, such as STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, and QUIT.

Same or similar message sent across a large number of phone numbers

We do not permit spreading similar or identical messages across many phone numbers without appropriate business justification.

As a result,  we have restricted your ability to provision additional phone numbers. If you attempt to recycle phone numbers and further provision additional phone numbers, you will see an error message due to this restriction.

To appeal this decision, please respond to this email with the justification of your business use case requiring the same or similar messages across additional phone numbers.

### **Your Key Messaging Metrics**

Your messaging activity reflects consumer impacting and/or policy-violating content being sent.  Your opt-out and error rates have reached higher than acceptable levels.    

A good opt-out rate is typically in the range of 0—1%

A good error rate is typically in the range of 0—6%

title_en: A2P 10DLC Campaign Use Cases
source_md:
SMS Compliance

# A2P 10DLC Campaign Use Cases

This article explains the A2P 10DLC Campaign use cases available through HighLevel and how to choose the option that best matches your messaging purpose. 

You'll learn about standard, special, and low-volume use cases, as well as important restrictions that may affect eligibility. Choosing the correct use case helps keep your Campaign details, sample messages, and actual messaging aligned.

What You'll Learn

When registering an A2P 10DLC campaign, selecting the appropriate use case is critical for compliance and message deliverability. Your use case defines the type of messaging your campaign will send and determines throughput limits and carrier approval requirements.

This guide explains each available use case, provides examples of qualifying message content, and helps you select the right classification for your business communications.

## What is an A2P 10DLC Campaign Use Case?

An A2P 10DLC campaign use case categorizes the type of business messaging you send through your registered phone numbers. When you register a 10DLC campaign with mobile carriers, you must declare a primary use case that accurately describes your messaging intent and content.

Mobile carriers use your declared use case to:

- Evaluate and approve your campaign registration
- Determine message throughput limits (messages per minute)
- Apply appropriate filtering and spam protection rules
- Verify compliance with carrier messaging policies

Key Benefits

- **Compliance Assurance:** Reduces the risk of Campaign rejection by The Campaign Registry.
- **Carrier Understanding:** Helps carriers understand message intent and apply filtering appropriately.
- **Legal Alignment:** Supports alignment with applicable messaging and compliance requirements.
- **Faster Approval:** Helps reduce avoidable review delays caused by an incorrect use case.
- **Improved Deliverability:** Helps keep registered messaging intent aligned with the traffic actually being sent.

## Standard A2P 10DLC Campaign Use Cases

Standard Campaign use cases describe the primary purpose of the messages your business plans to send. Choose the option that most accurately represents your actual messaging, because your Campaign Description, sample messages, opt-in flow, website, and live traffic should support the same use case.

Use Case

2FA (Two-Factor Authentication)

Authentication messages sent to verify user identity or provide secure access codes. These messages are transactional and time-sensitive.

Example Messages:

- Login verification codes
- Password reset PINs
- Multi-factor authentication tokens
- Account security alerts requiring user action

Note: 2FA messages must not include marketing content or promotional language.

Use Case

Account Notifications

Informational messages about changes to a customer's account status, settings, or activity. These are transactional updates triggered by account events.

Example Messages:

- Account creation confirmations
- Profile update notifications
- Payment method changes
- Subscription status changes
- Security setting modifications

Use Case

Customer Care

Messages related to customer support interactions, service inquiries, and problem resolution. This covers two-way conversational support.

Example Messages:

- Support ticket updates
- Customer service responses
- Technical support conversations
- Issue resolution status updates
- Service request confirmations

Use Case

Delivery Notifications

Updates about the status and progress of product or service deliveries. These are transactional messages tied to fulfillment events.

Example Messages:

- Shipping confirmations
- Package tracking updates
- Delivery arrival notifications
- Order status changes
- Delivery attempt alerts

Use Case

Fraud Alert Messaging

Time-sensitive security alerts about potentially fraudulent account activity or suspicious transactions. These messages require immediate user attention.

Example Messages:

- Suspicious transaction alerts
- Unusual login attempt notifications
- Payment decline fraud warnings
- Account compromise alerts
- Identity verification requests

Use Case

Higher Education

Messages from colleges, universities, and higher education institutions to students, staff, or prospective students. This covers academic and administrative communications.

Example Messages:

- Class schedule notifications
- Campus event announcements
- Registration reminders
- Grade postings
- Administrative updates
- Admissions communications

Use Case

Marketing

Promotional messages and marketing communications sent to customers who have provided explicit consent. This includes sales offers, promotions, and advertising content.

Example Messages:

- Sales promotions and discounts
- Product launch announcements
- Limited-time offers
- Newsletter content
- Event invitations
- Abandoned cart reminders

Note: Marketing messages require documented opt-in consent from recipients.

Use Case

Mixed

Combines multiple standard messaging purposes within one messaging program, such as marketing and account notifications.

Example Messages:

- Promotional offers plus account or appointment notifications sent under the same messaging program.

Use Case

Polling and Voting

Messages that solicit feedback, conduct surveys, or facilitate voting processes. This includes opinion collection and interactive polling.

Example Messages:

- Customer satisfaction surveys
- Product feedback requests
- Opinion polls
- Voting instructions
- Interactive questionnaires

Use Case

Public Service Announcement

Non-commercial messages from government agencies, non-profits, or organizations sending information in the public interest. This covers emergency alerts and community notifications.

Example Messages:

- Emergency weather alerts
- Community safety warnings
- Public health notifications
- Service outage announcements
- Government updates

Use Case

Security Alert

Critical security notifications that inform users of threats, vulnerabilities, or required security actions. Similar to fraud alerts but broader in scope.

Example Messages:

- Data breach notifications
- Password compromise warnings
- Unauthorized access alerts
- Security policy changes
- Required security updates

Use Case

Conversational Messaging

Two-way conversational interactions between businesses and customers, including live agent chats and bot conversations. This supports ongoing dialogue rather than one-way notifications.

Example Messages:

- Live agent conversations
- Chatbot interactions
- Two-way customer communications
- Interactive service requests
- Real-time customer engagement

## How to Choose the Right Campaign Use Case

The best use case is the one that most accurately reflects the messages recipients will actually receive. Choosing based on your primary messaging purpose helps prevent mismatches between your Campaign registration, sample messages, and live traffic.

Decision Guidance

- **Marketing:** Use when promotional offers, sales, discounts, or similar marketing content are the primary purpose.
- **Customer Care:** Use when messaging primarily supports customer-initiated service or support interactions.
- **Account Notifications:** Use for non-promotional updates about a customer's account, status, or activity.
- **Delivery Notifications:** Use when messages primarily communicate fulfillment or delivery status.
- **2FA:** Use for authentication or verification codes.
- **Mixed:** Use when one messaging program genuinely combines multiple standard messaging purposes.

Important

Do not select Mixed simply because you are unsure which use case applies. Your selected use case should accurately represent your real messaging program.

### Mixed vs. Separate Campaigns

A Mixed Campaign may be appropriate when multiple message types are part of the same messaging program. However, materially different messaging purposes may be better represented by separate Campaigns.

For example, a business sending authentication codes and unrelated promotional messages may need separate Campaigns so each type of traffic is accurately represented.

When in doubt, register according to the actual purpose and consent experience associated with each messaging program rather than grouping unrelated traffic together.

Important

Choose your Campaign use case carefully before submitting. If the selected use case is incorrect, it may not be editable during resubmission and you may need to create a new Campaign.

## Special Campaign Use Cases

Special use cases require additional verification, documentation, or pre-qualification during the registration process. These use cases serve specific industries or regulated purposes.

Special Use Case

Charity

For registered 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations and charitable entities. Requires tax-exempt status documentation during registration.

Special Use Case

Emergency

For organizations that send emergency alerts or critical public safety notifications. Requires documentation of emergency notification authority and approval from carrier partners.

Special Use Case

Political

Used for political messaging, including campaigns, parties, and PACs. Political Campaigns may require additional verification or pre-qualification during registration.

Special Use Case

Low Volume Mixed

Low Volume Mixed may be appropriate for businesses with lighter messaging needs that do not require higher throughput. It supports the same general categories of messaging as standard Mixed but has a lower monthly Campaign fee and is limited to the lowest available throughput tier regardless of Brand Trust Score.

If sending speed or scale is important, review the Message Throughput (MPS) guidance before selecting Low Volume Mixed.

Note

Special use cases may have different approval timelines, documentation requirements, or carrier restrictions. Contact HighLevel support if you have questions about eligibility or requirements for a special use case.

## Restricted and Forbidden Use Cases

A Campaign use case describes messaging purpose; it does not override carrier or platform restrictions. A Campaign may still be rejected, filtered, suspended, or subject to enforcement when the business type or message content is prohibited or restricted.

Examples of Restricted or Prohibited Categories

- Cannabis (including legal jurisdictions)
- Debt collection and consolidation
- Payday loans and high-risk financial services
- Gambling and sweepstakes (subject to restrictions)
- Adult content and services
- Cryptocurrency and unregulated investments
- Third-party lead generation (S.H.A.F.T.)
- Stock alerts and pump-and-dump schemes
- Other categories defined by carrier policy

Important

Review the [Forbidden Message Categories for SMS and MMS in the US and Canada](#) article for current policy details before registering any Campaign. Selecting an available use case does not make prohibited business types or message content eligible for messaging.
