title_en: Workflow Action - Instagram DM
source_md:
The Instagram DM workflow action in HighLevel allows you to automatically send personalized Instagram direct messages to contacts through workflows. This article explains how to configure the action, use it with Instagram triggers, add message templates and attachments, and understand the 24-hour messaging requirements for successful delivery.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Instagram DM Workflow Action?](#What-is-the-Instagram-DM-Workflow-Action?)
- [How to Set Up and Use the Instagram DM Workflow Action](#How-to-Set-Up-and-Use-the-Instagram-DM-Workflow-Action)
- [Instagram DM Action Fields and Settings](#Instagram-DM-Action-Fields-and-Settings)
- [Instagram DM Delivery Rules and Recommendations](#Instagram-DM-Delivery-Rules-and-Recommendations)
- [Recommended Alternative: Instagram Interactive Messenger](#Recommended-Alternative%3A-Instagram-Interactive-Messenger)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is the Instagram DM Workflow Action?**

The Instagram DM workflow action allows you to send automated direct messages to contacts who have recently interacted with your connected Instagram account. It helps businesses manage Instagram conversations, respond to inquiries, and share relevant information without manually sending each message.

You can customize messages using templates, custom values, trigger links, and attachments. However, successful delivery depends on Instagram's messaging restrictions, including whether the contact has sent your business a DM within the previous 24 hours.

---

## **How to Set Up and Use the Instagram DM Workflow Action**

Setting up the Instagram DM action requires a connected Instagram account, a workflow trigger, and a configured message. Choosing the appropriate trigger and understanding Instagram's messaging requirements helps ensure that messages reach the intended contacts.

### **Step 1:** Create or Open a Workflow

1. Navigate to **Automations > Workflows**.
2. Click **Create Workflow** to create a new workflow, or open an existing workflow.
3. Open the workflow in the Workflow Builder. You can use either the Standard Builder or Advanced Builder.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/V7fhgryQHgwasuG8dyHy+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-09+at+18.26.09.png)

### **Step 2:** Add a Workflow Trigger

A workflow trigger determines when a contact enters the automation. For Instagram DM responses, the **Customer Replied** trigger with the reply channel set to **Instagram DM** is a recommended option.

1. Click **+ Add New Trigger**.
2. Search for and select **Customer Replied**.
3. Click **+ Add Filters**.
4. Select **Reply Channel** and choose **Instagram DM**.
5. Add other filters if needed to narrow down the incoming messages.
6. Click **Save Trigger**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/qZkHrrnpLPgdNDPkLNDl+/GIF+Recording+2026-10-09+at+18.27.49.gif)

### **Step 3:** Add & Configure the Instagram DM Action

Once the trigger is configured, add the Instagram DM action to define the message contacts will receive.

1. Click the **+** icon below the workflow trigger.
2. Search for **Instagram DM** in the workflow actions.
3. Select **Instagram DM** to open the action configuration panel.
4. Enter an **Action Name** to identify the action within the workflow.

1. **Select a Template (Optional):** Choose an existing message template if you want to reuse previously created content.
2. **Enter Your Message:** Type the message you want to send to the contact.
3. **Personalize the Message:** Use Custom Values or Trigger Links to include contact-specific information or clickable resources.
4. **Write with AI (Optional):** Use the Write with AI option to help draft message content.
5. **Add an Attachment (Optional):** Click **Add Attachment** to upload a file from your device or select an existing file from Media Storage.
6. **Add Files Through URL (Optional):** Use the file URL option to attach a resource hosted online.
7. Click **Save Action**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/wnWkRStgCJu8g4TeyUda+/GIF+Recording+2026-10-09+at+18.34.44.gif)

---

## **Instagram DM Action Fields and Settings**

Each field in the Instagram DM action controls a different part of the outgoing message. Understanding which fields are required helps you configure messages correctly and avoid unnecessary setup errors.

| Field | Description | Mandatory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Action Name** | Specifies the name used to identify the action within the workflow. | Yes |
| **Templates** | Allows you to select a preconfigured message template for consistent communication. | No |
| **Message** | Defines the content sent to the contact. Supports custom values for personalization. | Yes |
| **Add Attachment** | Allows you to attach files or media, such as images or documents, to the message. | No |
| **Add Files Through URL** | Allows you to add externally hosted files using their URLs. | No |

---

## **Instagram DM Delivery Rules and Recommendations**

Instagram applies messaging restrictions to automated direct messages. Understanding these rules helps you choose the appropriate workflow action and avoid delivery failures.

### **24-Hour Messaging Requirement**

The Instagram DM workflow action should only be used to send messages to contacts who have sent a direct message to your connected Instagram business account within the previous 24 hours.

If a contact has not sent a DM within this period, the Instagram DM action cannot be relied upon to deliver a new direct message.

**Important:** A contact commenting on an Instagram post does not automatically establish the 24-hour direct messaging window required for a standard Instagram DM.

### **Behavior with Instagram Comment Triggers**

When the Instagram DM action is used with the **Instagram Comment(s) On A Post** workflow trigger, its behavior depends on the contact's recent interactions.

- **Recent Instagram Comment:** If the contact has a recent comment on your Instagram post, the message is sent as a reply to that comment through DM.
- **No Recent Instagram Comment:** If there is no recent comment, the action attempts to send a direct DM. This requires the contact to have sent your business a DM within the previous 24 hours.

---

## **Recommended Alternative: Instagram Interactive Messenger**

For Instagram comment-based automation and interactive conversations, HighLevel recommends the **Instagram Interactive Messenger** workflow action.

Select the appropriate **Reply Type** based on the interaction:

- **Reply to Comment via DM:** Use when you want to send a private message in response to an Instagram post comment.
- **Reply to DM:** Use when you want to respond to a contact's Instagram direct message.

Instagram Interactive Messenger also supports interactive elements such as buttons and quick replies, making it useful for more advanced conversation workflows.

For additional details, refer to [Workflow Action - Instagram Interactive Messenger](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004662-workflow-action-instagram-interactive-messenger).

**Note:** Instagram messaging behavior was updated following a Meta-side issue resolved on August 31, 2024. Workflows should not assume that a post comment alone authorizes unrestricted direct messaging through the standard Instagram DM action.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why is my Instagram DM workflow running but the message is not being delivered?**

The contact may not meet Instagram's messaging requirements, or the Instagram account connection may need attention. Verify that the contact has sent a DM within the previous 24 hours, check your connected account, and review the workflow execution details.

**Q: Can I send an Instagram DM to a contact who submitted an Instagram lead form?**

You can configure workflows based on lead form submissions, but submitting a form does not automatically satisfy the Instagram DM action's messaging requirements. The contact must also have an eligible recent Instagram DM interaction for standard direct message delivery.

**Q: Does commenting on an Instagram post automatically open a 24-hour DM window?**

No. A comment alone does not establish the standard 24-hour DM window. For comment-based private replies, use Instagram Interactive Messenger with the appropriate Reply Type.

**Q: Can I use the same Instagram DM message across multiple workflows?**

Yes. You can select an existing message template in different Instagram DM actions to maintain consistent messaging across workflows.

**Q: Can I personalize Instagram messages using contact information?**

Yes. The Message field supports Custom Values, allowing you to insert available contact or workflow information into your messages.

**Q: What is the difference between Instagram DM and Instagram Interactive Messenger?**

Instagram DM is primarily used to send a configured direct message with optional attachments. Instagram Interactive Messenger supports comment-to-DM reply types and interactive conversation elements such as buttons and quick replies.

**Q: Can I use a keyword to send different Instagram messages to different contacts?**

Yes. You can configure trigger filters such as Contains Phrase or Exact Match to identify specific incoming messages or comments. For more complex scenarios, use separate workflow paths or conditions to send the appropriate message.

**Q: Can I use an online file instead of uploading an attachment?**

Yes. The **Add Files Through URL** option allows you to provide a URL for a hosted file instead of uploading it directly from your device or Media Storage.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Workflow Action - Instagram Interactive Messenger](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004662-workflow-action-instagram-interactive-messenger)
- [Workflow Trigger - Instagram Comment(s) On A Post](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004646)
- [Workflow Trigger - Customer Replied](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002677)
- [Guide to Facebook & Instagram Comment Automation & AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002055-guide-to-facebook-instagram-comment-automation-ai)
- [Workflow Recipes - Instagram Comment Automation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004658-workflow-recipes-instagram-comment-automation)

title_en: Using Page Context with Ask AI
source_md:
Ask AI can use information from the HighLevel page you are currently viewing to better understand your questions and instructions. Page context helps you ask natural questions about what is on screen, point Ask AI to specific elements, and receive visual guidance directly on the page.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Page Context in Ask AI?](#What-is-Page-Context-in-Ask-AI?)
- [Key Benefits of Page Context](#Key-Benefits-of-Page-Context)
- [How to Select Page Elements](#How-to-Select-Page-Elements)
- [Follow Guided Highlight Walkthroughs](#Follow-Guided-Highlight-Walkthroughs%C2%A0)
- [Page Context and Voice Mode](#Page-Context-and-Voice-Mode)
- [Approval Before Ask AI Makes Changes](#Approval-Before-Ask-AI-Makes-Changes)
- [Privacy](#Privacy-and-Page-Context)
- [Use Cases](#Use-Cases-for-using-Page-Context-with-Ask-AI)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Page Context in Ask AI?**

Page context allows Ask AI to understand information from the HighLevel page you are currently working on. When Ask AI is open alongside a HighLevel page, it can use relevant information from that page when your request depends on what you are viewing. You do not need to turn page context on.

Instead of manually describing every card, field, row, setting, or section, you can ask questions that depend on what is already visible on the page. Ask AI will use the current page to understand what your question refers to before responding.

For example:

- *“What is this?”*
- *“Why are these in the list?”*
- *“What does this mean?”*
- *“Help me here.”*
- *“Explain this section.”*

When you need Ask AI to focus on something specific, you can even select individual page elements and attach them directly to your message.

```
Note: Page context can work whether Ask AI is open as a floating panel or in Split View. Since it requires a HighLevel host page, it is unavailable from the full-page Ask AI experience.
```

---

## **Key Benefits of Page Context**

- **Ask more naturally:** Ask questions about what you are viewing without describing every detail manually.
- **Point instead of describing:** Select the exact card, row, field, setting, or section you want Ask AI to consider.
- **Get more precise assistance:** Give Ask AI direct context when a page contains several similar elements.
- **Follow visual guidance:** Ask AI can highlight relevant areas of the page during supported walkthroughs.
- **Keep page context with voice requests:** Select something on the page and then explain what you want using Voice Mode.
- **Protect sensitive information:** Credentials and sensitive fields are masked before page content is sent to Ask AI.

---

## **How to Select Specific Page Elements**

Page element selection lets you point Ask AI to the exact part of the page you want it to consider. This is useful when a page contains several cards, rows, fields, settings, or other elements that could make a general request unclear.

Select Page Element is unavailable on the full-page Ask AI screen and the sidebar expanded to full screen as there's no host page to point at.

To select a page element:

1. Click **Select page element** in the Ask AI composer, or press **Ctrl + Shift + E** on Windows or **Command + Shift + E** on Mac.  
     
   Hold Shift to temporarily interact with the page while selection mode is active, such as opening a dropdown, scrolling through a list, or entering a modal.
2. Move your pointer across the page to highlight and click selectable areas that you want Ask AI to consider.
3. Continue selecting additional elements when needed. You can attach up to 20 page sections per message.
4. Review the page-context cards displayed above the composer.
5. Type your question or request and send it to Ask AI.

Each selected item appears as a page-context card above the composer. Click a card to highlight its location on the page again. You can remove individual selections or use **Clear all** to remove all attached page context.

```
Note: Attached selections stay pending until the transcript lands, so you can point at something and simply say what you want. For more information about Ask AI voice controls, see How to Use Ask AI Voice Mode.
```

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080750469/original/PLEQDpHiUCQxFtYvNMZF8gg694z-ntg08A.gif?1789151853)**

---

## **Follow Guided Highlight Walkthroughs**

Ask AI can show you where to go on the page instead of only describing it. When visual guidance is available, Ask AI can highlight the relevant location directly on the current HighLevel page.

Multi-step walkthroughs can include:

- A step counter
- **Previous** and **Next** controls
- Arrow-key navigation
- A draggable hint bar

You can move the hint bar if it covers content you need to see. If the page changes and Ask AI can no longer reliably identify a previously referenced location, it identifies that highlight as stale instead of directing you to outdated page content. Ask AI may then prompt you to select the relevant area again.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080910048/original/rCWY8zNxpe73gJgv_xaz_p-l46fdOZzcFw.gif?1789415219)

---

## **Page Context and Voice Mode**

You can combine page element selection with Ask AI Voice Mode. After selecting an element, start Voice Mode and explain what you want Ask AI to do. The attached page selection remains pending while your spoken request is transcribed, allowing the selected information to accompany your voice request.

For example, you can select a field or section and then simply ask:

*“What does this do?”*

For more information about voice controls, see [How to Use Ask AI Voice Mode.](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008022)

---

## **Approval Before Ask AI Makes Changes**

Ask AI can use page context to understand what you mean, but it will not automatically perform a supported write action based on that context. Any request that would create, update, delete, cancel, reschedule, send, publish, or perform a supported bulk action must stop for explicit approval before execution.

When a request results in a write action, Ask AI shows the exact operation it plans to perform. You can then **Approve** the action to continue, **Edit** the proposed plan before execution or **Reject** the action and return it to Ask AI.

If the page leaves more than one reasonable interpretation, Ask AI can first ask you to select the intended option before presenting the approval request.

Questions, explanations, and guided walkthroughs do not require approval.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080909865/original/s3rVNq-_u3JAgtuQicpKqKdwSHC_AP1GbQ.gif?1789414796)**

---

## **Privacy and Page Context**

HighLevel applies safeguards before page information is used as Ask AI context.

- **Sensitive-Field Redaction:** Credentials and sensitive fields are masked before page content is sent to Ask AI.
- **Masking disclosure:** Ask AI indicates when sensitive information has been redacted.
- **Large Page Content:**If the amount of page content exceeds the supported context limit, Ask AI can truncate the extracted information. Ask AI indicates when truncation occurs.

---

## **Use Cases for Page Context with Ask AI**

#### **Analyze Dashboard Metrics**

Ask AI makes it easy to ask questions about the dashboard metrics you are currently reviewing.

You can rely on page context for general questions or select a specific metric when you want Ask AI to focus on one part of the dashboard.

For example, you can prompt:

- *“Explain how I can improve my business.”*
- *“What does this metric mean?”*

[동영상](https://jumpshare.com/embed/bpl7GCNcgukzmyfDxbVq?disableDownload=true)

#### **Manage Calendars and Booking Assignments**

Calendar workflows often involve several appointments, filters, settings, or booking details at once. Ask AI can understand the information you are viewing while you ask for assistance. You can select a specific appointment, filter, setting, or section when you want Ask AI to focus on one part of the page

For example, you can prompt:

- *“Block my calendar from 2pm - 4 pm.”*
- *“Create a new meeting with John Smith”*

[동영상](https://jumpshare.com/embed/hAxTzbyudBxbw9T3rVYq?disableDownload=true)

#### **Accelerate Platform Setup**

Ask AI can help you move through setup and configuration tasks by explaining the settings and options you are currently working with.

For example, you can prompt:

- *“What does this setting do?”*
- *“Help me here.”*
- *“Explain the selected element on this page."*
- *“Explain this option before I change it.”*

You can also select a specific field when you need a more precise explanation or follow a guided highlight walkthrough when visual guidance is available.

[동영상](https://jumpshare.com/embed/C3jtnlF83LoPTTTBfEtD?disableDownload=true)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need to turn page context on?**  
No. When Ask AI is open alongside a supported HighLevel host page, it can use page information when your request depends on what you are viewing.

**Q: Does Ask AI need to be in Split View to use page context?**  
No. Page context can also work when Ask AI is open as a floating panel. Split View changes the panel layout but is not required for page context. Page context does not apply when in a full-screen Ask AI mode as there is no page to draw context from.

**Q: When should I select a page element manually?**  
Use page element selection when you want Ask AI to focus on a specific card, row, field, setting, or section instead of relying on the broader page context.

**Q: How many page elements can I select?**  
You can attach up to 20 page sections to one message.

**Q: Can I use page context from the full-page Ask AI experience?**  
No. Page context requires a HighLevel host page. It is unavailable from the full-page Ask AI experience and when Ask AI is expanded to full screen.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Ask AI Assistant](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005327)
- [Ask AI Split View](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008730)
- [How to Use Ask AI Voice Mode](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008022)

title_en: How to Create and Manage Tags for Sub-Accounts
source_md:
Tags for Sub-Accounts in HighLevel help agencies organize client accounts using custom labels. You can assign multiple tags to an account, filter or group accounts by tag, and save filtered views as Smart Lists. Tags are useful for tracking onboarding stages, industries, service levels, and internal account categories. This article explains how to create, apply, and manage tags from Agency View.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Tags for Sub-Accounts?](#What-Are-Tags-for-Sub-Accounts?)
- [Key Benefits of Sub-Account Tags](#Key-Benefits-of-Sub-Account-Tags)
- [How to Create and Manage Tags for Sub-Accounts](#How-to-Create-and-Manage-Tags-for-Sub-Accounts)
- [Creating and Assigning Tags](#Creating-and-Assigning-Tags)
- [Managing Tags](#Managing-Tags)
- [Filtering and Grouping Sub-Accounts](#Filtering-and-Grouping-Sub-Accounts)
- [Saving Tag-Based Smart Lists](#Saving-Tag-Based-Smart-Lists)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Tags for Sub-Accounts?**

Sub-Account Tags are customizable labels that help agencies categorize the client accounts they manage.

For example, one sub-account can have **Dental**, **Onboarding**, and **VIP** tags. You can then use those labels to find and organize related accounts.

**Sub-Account Tags are different from Contact tags.** Sub-Account Tags organize accounts in Agency View, while Contact tags organize individual Contacts inside a sub-account.

**Availability:** Access to Tags for Sub-Accounts may depend on your agency plan and user permissions. The exact plan eligibility and tag-management permissions require confirmation.

---

## **Key Benefits of Sub-Account Tags**

Tags provide a flexible way to organize client portfolios without relying on a single category.

- **Custom Organization:** Categorize accounts by industry, service level, lifecycle stage, or team.
- **Multiple Tags:** Apply several labels to the same account.
- **Quick Filtering:** Find accounts that match selected tags.
- **Grouped Views:** Review tag-based groups with account counts.
- **Reusable Smart Lists:** Save filtered account views for future use.
- **Simpler Management:** Edit, reassign, delete, or apply tags in bulk using supported controls.

---

## **How to Create and Manage Tags for Sub-Accounts**

A consistent tagging workflow makes it easier to organize accounts and reuse filtered views. The following steps demonstrate the main operations.

### **Step 1: Open Sub-Accounts**

The Sub-Accounts list contains the controls used to organize and manage agency client accounts.

1. Switch to **Agency View**.
2. Open **Sub-Accounts**.
3. Locate **Tags** in the toolbar.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084508360/original/fFpx8pC0LAK12QGgcuVdCKk5oZmEIqB0iw.png?1793279015)

### 

### **Step 2: Create a Tag**

Creating a tag establishes a reusable label for your client accounts.

1. Click **Tags**.
2. Search for the tag name.
3. Select the available option to create a new tag.
4. Enter a name, such as **Onboarding**.
5. Choose a color if prompted.
6. Complete the creation action.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084528446/original/c9ETOSgJKFlueX_V4FapTSHUeCiKYDVWEA.png?1793288516)

### 

### **Step 3: Assign Tags to an Account**

Assigning multiple tags lets you describe a client account using several categories.

1. Find the sub-account in the list.
2. Hover over its name and select **Add tags**, or use the applicable Tags control.
3. Select **Onboarding**.
4. Add another tag, such as **Dental**.
5. Confirm both tags appear beside the account.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084529118/original/im2KRlUF7I8RFo1I_CBrFdns9vfy1GMkrw.png?1793288854)

### **Step 4: Apply Tags in Bulk**

Bulk tagging helps when multiple accounts need the same label.

1. Select the checkboxes beside the relevant sub-accounts.
2. Open the available bulk-action controls.
3. Choose the tag-assignment option.
4. Select the tag.
5. Review and apply the change.

```
Note: The exact bulk controls, supported removal actions, and required permissions should be verified.
```

### **Step 5: Filter Sub-Accounts by Tag**

Tag filters help you locate a specific group of client accounts.

1. Click **Tags**.
2. Select the tag you want to use, such as **Onboarding**.
3. Review the matching accounts.
4. Apply other supported filters if needed.

### **Step 6: Group Sub-Accounts by Tag**

Grouping provides an organized view of account categories and their counts.

1. Click **Group by**.
2. Select **Tags**.
3. Review the resulting groups.
4. Expand or collapse groups as needed.

### **Step 7: Save a Smart List**

Saving a filtered view makes it easier to return to the same account segment.

1. Apply the required tag and account filters.
2. Click **Add Smart List** or the applicable save control.
3. Enter a descriptive name.
4. Save the Smart List.
5. Reopen it from the Smart List tabs.

### **Step 8: Edit, Reassign, or Delete a Tag**

Managing existing tags helps keep account categories accurate and consistent.

1. Open **Tags**.
2. Find the tag you want to manage.
3. Open its management options.
4. Change its name or color, or choose **Reassign to...** or **Delete tag**.
5. Review any confirmation before completing the action.

```
Important: Review reassignment and deletion carefully, particularly for tags used by many accounts.
```

---

## **Creating and Assigning Tags**

Tags help you identify accounts according to the categories your agency uses.

Common examples include:

| Category | Example Tags |
| --- | --- |
| Lifecycle | Onboarding, Active, At-risk |
| Industry | Dental, Roofing, Real Estate |
| Service level | DIY, Done-for-you |
| Account type | VIP, Test, Internal |
| Account management | Sarah, Dev, Priya |

A sub-account can have multiple tags, and the same tag can be used across different sub-accounts.

```
Note: Tags are organizational labels. Adding an account manager's name as a tag does not assign the account to that user or grant access.
```

---

## **Managing Tags**

Keeping tag names and categories consistent makes filtering and grouping more useful.

The **Tags** menu includes controls for searching for tags and managing existing labels.

Available management options shown in the release include:

- **Edit name:** Update an existing tag's name.
- **Change color:** Make categories easier to recognize.
- **Reassign to...:** Reassign an existing tag to another tag.
- **Delete tag:** Remove a tag that is no longer needed.

```
Important: Confirm how reassignment and deletion affect existing sub-account assignments before making changes. These actions may affect multiple accounts.
```

---

## **Filtering and Grouping Sub-Accounts**

Filtering and grouping are two different ways to work with tagged accounts.

**Filtering** narrows the list to accounts matching selected criteria. **Grouping** organizes the displayed accounts into sections.

| Option | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Tags** | Filter sub-accounts by selected tags |
| **Filter / Advanced filters** | Refine results using other supported account criteria |
| **Group by → Tags** | Organize accounts into collapsible tag-based groups |
| **Untagged** | Find accounts without tags, where available |

For example, filter by **Onboarding** to review clients in that stage, or group by Tags to compare different client categories.

```
Note: Multiple-tag matching rules and the way accounts with several tags appear in grouped results require verification.
```

---

## **Saving Tag-Based Smart Lists**

Smart Lists let you save frequently used Sub-Account views so you can return to them without rebuilding the same filters.

For example, an agency could save a view named **Dental Onboarding Clients** to review that group regularly.

Use **Add Smart List** or the applicable save control in the Sub-Accounts interface.

```
Important: Agency-level Sub-Account Smart Lists are separate from Contact Smart Lists inside individual sub-accounts. The exact behavior of saved grouping, sorting, and updates when tag assignments change should be confirmed.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can one sub-account have multiple tags?**

A: Yes. You can assign several tags to the same account.

**Q: Are Sub-Account Tags the same as Contact tags?**

A: No. Sub-Account Tags organize agency client accounts. Contact tags organize Contacts within an individual sub-account.

**Q: Can I change a tag's name or color?**

A: Yes. The tag-management menu includes editing and color-selection options.

**Q: Can I apply tags to multiple sub-accounts at once?**

A: Yes. Bulk tag application is included in the release. The exact controls and permissions require confirmation.

**Q: What is the difference between filtering and grouping?**

A: Filtering narrows the account list. Grouping organizes visible accounts into tag-based sections.

**Q: Can I find sub-accounts without tags?**

A: The Tags menu includes an **Untagged** option to help identify accounts without tags.

**Q: Can I save a tag-filtered view?**

A: Yes. Tag-filtered Sub-Account views can be saved as agency-level Smart Lists.

**Q: What happens when I reassign or delete a tag?**

A: The interface provides both actions, but their exact effects on existing assignments should be verified before use.

**Q: Does adding a team member's name as a tag assign them to the account?**

A: No. Tags do not replace actual account assignments or user permissions.

---

### **Related Articles**

title_en: Google Analytics Widgets in Dashboard and Custom Reports
source_md:
Bring your Google Analytics 4 (GA4) insights straight into HighLevel. With ready‑made widgets you can track users, engagement, traffic sources, and top pages without leaving the platform—ideal for agencies that want website analytics and CRM outcomes in one place. Build always‑on dashboards for daily monitoring and schedule client‑ready reports with zero spreadsheets.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Google Analytics Widgets?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-Google-Analytics-Widgets?)
- [Key Benefits of Google Analytics Widgets](#Key-Benefits-of-Google-Analytics-Widgets)
- [Prerequisites & Access](#Prerequisites-&-Access)
- [Available Google Analytics Widgets](#Available-Google-Analytics-Widgets)
- [Dashboards vs Custom Reports](#Dashboards-vs-Custom-Reports)
- [Filtering & Customizing Widgets](#Filtering-&-Customizing-Widgets)
- [How To Setup Google Analytics Widgets](#How-To-Setup-Google-Analytics-Widgets)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Google Analytics Widgets?**

Google Analytics Widgets are pre‑built visual blocks that surface GA4 metrics inside a HighLevel sub‑account. After connecting a GA4 property, you can place widgets—such as Total Users, Engagement Rate, or Sessions by Channel—on dashboards and custom reports to evaluate website behavior alongside pipeline, attribution, and revenue data. This centralizes insights for faster, data‑driven decisions.

---

## **Key Benefits of Google Analytics Widgets**

Understanding the value of each widget helps you assemble dashboards that answer real business questions. Use the benefits below to align GA data with goals like acquisition efficiency, content performance, and conversion health.

- **Single source of truth:** Marry GA4 web analytics with CRM, ad, and sales metrics in one workspace.
- **Faster decisions:** Spot traffic spikes, engagement dips, or top‑performing pages at a glance.
- **Audience insights:** Compare new vs. returning users, devices, and channels to optimize campaigns.
- **Time savings:** Skip CSV exports and tab‑switching; dashboards and reports pull data automatically.
- **Client transparency:** Share live web reports with stakeholders without granting GA access.

---

## **Prerequisites & Access**

Confirm access and connections before adding widgets to ensure data loads correctly the first time.

- A connected GA4 property and data stream in **Settings → Integrations → Google Analytics**.
- User permissions: ability to **Edit** dashboards to add widgets (or **View** to consume), and access to **Create/Schedule**reports where applicable.
- Recommended: verify you have the right Google account and GA4 property permissions (view access to the property and stream).

---

## **Available Google Analytics Widgets**

These widgets focus on the most useful GA4 KPIs for acquisition, engagement, and content analysis. Mix trend, breakdown, and leaderboard styles to create an at‑a‑glance story.

| Metric | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Total Users | Total number of unique users who visited your website during the selected time period. |
| Active Users | Number of users who had an engaged session or were active on your site. |
| New Users | First‑time visitors to your website in the selected period. |
| Sessions Over Time | A time‑series view of total sessions across the selected date range. |
| Engagement Rate | Percentage of engaged sessions, indicating how actively users interact with content. |
| Bounce Rate | Percentage of sessions with no further engagement after a single page view. |
| Average Engagement Time | Average time users actively spend engaging with your website content. |
| Sessions by Channel | Sessions grouped by default acquisition channels (e.g., Organic Search, Paid Social). |
| Sessions by Source/Medium | Sessions grouped by traffic source and medium pairs (e.g., google/organic, facebook/social). |
| Top Pages by Views | Most‑viewed pages ranked by total views. |
| Top Events | Most frequently triggered GA4 events (key interactions and behaviors). |
| New vs. Returning Users | Comparison of first‑time vs. returning visitors in the selected period. |
| Device Category Breakdown | Sessions by device type (desktop, mobile, tablet). |

---

## **Dashboards vs Custom Reports**

Use dashboards for continuous monitoring and use custom reports to package insights for routine sharing. Both surfaces use the same GA widget library, so you can start with one and reuse layouts in the other.

- **Dashboards:** Always‑on visual snapshot for daily checks and quick comparisons.
- **Custom Reports:** Designed for scheduled email delivery and polished hand‑offs to clients or leaders.

---

## **Filtering & Customizing Widgets**

Tailor each widget so stakeholders see only what matters. Filters, chart types, and layout controls turn raw data into focused, scannable visuals.

- **Date range controls:** Use the dashboard/report picker to set the time window for all widgets on the page.
- **Chart types:** Choose from **Numeric, Donut, Line, Bar,** or **Table** where available for the selected widget.
- **Filters & conditions:** Narrow results (e.g., **Source/Medium = google / organic**, include/exclude channels, pages, or events).
- **Layout controls:** Drag to reposition, resize for readability, duplicate widgets you want to compare with different filters, or remove unneeded ones.
- **Theming:** Optional theme choices let you present data consistently across dashboards and reports.

---

## **How To Setup Google Analytics Widgets**

A short one‑time connection enables you to add GA4 widgets to dashboards and reports. Follow the step‑by‑step process below to visualize performance and share it with stakeholders.

### **Add Widgets to a Dashboard**

1. In your **Sub‑Account**, open **Dashboard** and click the blue button in the top‑left to open the desired dashboard.  
     
   *![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155059266775/original/eh0QG2easYSJgc_Wnm6VkYXdMajBuTQOsQ.png?1764157499)*
2. Click **Edit Dashboard → Add Widget**.  
     
   *![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155059266822/original/0Mx5zJn_N-jjy7Ni2A0g23XxC4f83nfCFg.gif?1764157543)*
3. Choose a chart type (**Numeric, Donut, Line, Bar,** or **Table**), then scroll to the **Google Analytics** category and select the metric or “Top” widget you want to add.  
     
   *![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155059267010/original/2DpoezShTl5HSRswM9hiZ9NtdG4mmd87Jw.gif?1764157637)*
4. Apply filters (e.g., channel, source/medium, page, date range) or adjust theme/colors if needed.  
     
   *![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155059267244/original/ZiuA7lLmWMTPJdl-NZn3bOHHQWyzfL3muQ.png?1764157778)*
5. Click **Save**. The widget begins pulling GA4 data.

### **Add Widgets to a Custom Report**

1. In your **Sub‑Account**, go to **Reporting → Custom Reports**, then open an existing report or click **New Report**.  
   *![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155059267621/original/XMriTqN4Ov_Mtm_yuIO_VGEPcPI2XmsyFA.png?1764157947)*
2. Start from a blank canvas, use a template, or import an existing dashboard layout.  
     
   *![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155059267656/original/U4pbI68KZN-47u1U6OSqalRR4JUjQPx3hg.png?1764157967)*
3. Click **Add Widget/Element** (top‑left). In the widget list, locate **Google Analytics** and drag the widgets you want into the layout.  
     
   *![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155059267780/original/WxVJsikndxalX_FGy4Tns7VbVX1_aLPrsw.gif?1764157995)*
4. Configure each widget: select chart type, set filters, choose theme, and click **Save**.  
     
   *![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155059267942/original/DtVbHOWLwz5vAQFN0NDMZVkDLQE_dw82cQ.png?1764158044)*
5. Click **Send** or **Schedule** to configure email delivery so recipients receive the report automatically.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Which version of Google Analytics is supported?**  
Google Analytics 4 (GA4). Universal Analytics (UA) is not supported for these widgets.

**Q: Why does a widget show “No Data”?**  
Check that the GA4 property is connected, widen the date range, and review filters (for example, a restrictive Source/Medium or a page path that has no traffic).

**Q: Can I duplicate and tweak a Google Analytics widget?**  
Yes. Use duplicate to create a copy, then adjust filters or chart type to compare variants side by side.

**Q: Do dashboards and custom reports use different GA data?**  
No. Both surfaces read from your connected GA4 property; choose the surface based on monitoring vs. scheduling needs.

**Q: Can I mix GA widgets with ads and CRM metrics?**  
Yes. Combine GA4 widgets with Meta Ads, Google Ads, and CRM widgets to tell a complete acquisition‑to‑revenue story.

**Q: What permissions are required to add GA widgets?**  
Users need the ability to connect integrations (as applicable) and to **Edit** dashboards or **Create/Schedule** reports. View‑only users can see shared dashboards and received reports.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Create & Add Dashboard Widgets](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006363-how-to-create-add-dashboard-widgets)
- [How to Create and Schedule Reports](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003965-how-to-create-and-schedule-reports)
- [How To Manage Dashboard Permissions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006500-how-to-manage-dashboard-permissions)
- [Customizing Dashboard Widgets](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006406-customizing-dashboard-widgets)
- [Google Analytics 4 Tracking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001234199-google-analytics-4-tracking)
- [Record Pageviews into Google Analytics for Funnels/Websites (GA4)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001219725-how-to-record-pageviews-into-google-analytics-for-funnels-websites-ga4-)

title_en: Customize AI-Generated WordPress Pages Directly in HighLevel
source_md:
Universal Content Customization makes it easier to update AI-generated WordPress pages without opening Elementor for routine content changes. This gives you a faster way to refine page content while keeping Elementor available for deeper design changes.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Universal Content Customization for AI Pages?](#What-is-Universal-Content-Customization-for-AI-Pages?)
- [Requirements](#Requirements)
- [Supported Content Elements](#Supported-Content-Elements)
- [Editing Text Directly from the Page Preview](#Editing-Text-Directly-from-the-Page-Preview)
- [Using AI-Assisted Text Editing](#Using-AI-Assisted-Text-Editing)
- [Changing the Tone of Page Content](#Changing-the-Tone-of-Page-Content)
- [How To Customize an AI-Generated WordPress Page](#How-To-Customize-an-AI-Generated-WordPress-Page)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Universal Content Customization for AI Pages?**

Universal Content Customization lets you edit supported content on AI-generated WordPress pages directly from the HighLevel preview. Instead of switching to Elementor whenever you need to change copy or replace an image, you can make many common updates from the **Customizations** panel.

Supported editable elements include:

- Headings
- Paragraphs
- Buttons
- Icon Box titles
- Icon Box descriptions
- Images

You can select a supported element, change the content manually, use AI-assisted editing options, and save the result. Saved updates are reflected on the WordPress page.

```
Important: Universal Content Customization requires LeadConnector WordPress Plugin v4.0.4 or later.
```

---

## **Requirements**

The correct WordPress integration version is required for Universal Content Customization to work as expected. Checking the plugin version first can help prevent missing editing controls or unsupported behavior.

You need:

- An AI-generated WordPress page in HighLevel.
- **LeadConnector WordPress Plugin v4.0.4 or later**.

For newly provisioned WordPress sites hosted through HighLevel, the LeadConnector plugin is installed automatically. You can also review the plugin connection status from the WordPress area in HighLevel.

If you need to download or update the plugin manually, the latest versions are available through the LeadConnector WordPress Plugin Hub. 

---

## **Supported Content Elements**

Universal Content Customization expands editing beyond a small number of predefined page sections. Selecting supported content directly from the preview makes it easier to update copy wherever it appears on the AI-generated page.

Supported elements include:

- **Headings:** Change titles and section headings.
- **Paragraphs:** Update longer descriptions and body copy.
- **Buttons:** Change supported button content.
- **Icon Box titles:** Edit the heading associated with an Icon Box.
- **Icon Box descriptions:** Update the descriptive text below an Icon Box.
- **Images:** Regenerate supported AI-generated images or replace them with uploaded images.

Not every Elementor element should be assumed to support direct customization. If an element cannot be selected from the HighLevel preview, use Elementor for additional editing.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079992204/original/FA46BcGuxRUbrE9M-J4_XvjG0plZHNxYiA.png?1788430229)**

---

## **Editing Text Directly from the Page Preview**

Direct text editing lets you correct wording, update business information, or refine generated copy without leaving the page preview. Selecting the text opens its current content in the **Customizations** panel so you can make the change in context.

To edit supported text:

1. Open the AI-generated WordPress page preview.
2. Hover over the text you want to change.
3. Click the supported element.
4. Review the selected text in the **Customizations** panel.
5. Replace or edit the text.
6. Preview the change if needed.
7. Click **Save Changes** when you are satisfied.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079992646/original/Re_VTta_mIgryuGYGWwKf9cmogt14KF08g.jpeg?1788430422)**

---

## **Using AI-Assisted Text Editing**

AI-assisted editing can help you improve existing copy without writing a replacement from scratch. The available tools let you adjust the length, wording, or style of selected content while keeping the original page structure.

Available options include:

- **Rephrase:** Rewrite the selected content using different wording.
- **Shorten:** Create a more concise version.
- **Elaborate:** Add more detail to the existing text.
- **Change Tone:** Rewrite the content with a different communication style.

You can review the generated result before saving it to the page.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080002864/original/pfL8spCQ5XcZrNV02KvGg4WPLlT_FW7FKQ.png?1788435404)**

---

## **Changing the Tone of Page Content**

Changing the tone helps you keep page copy aligned with how your business communicates. Instead of manually rewriting the selected text, you can choose a predefined tone and generate a version that better matches the style you want.

Available tone options include:

- **Professional**
- **Friendly**
- **Compelling**
- **Confident**

Choose the tone that best matches the page and review the generated copy before saving it.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080003423/original/p6R_KYkyFGrKbs3zGok9ykWrRkAYn5SbmA.png?1788435665)**

---

## **How To Customize an AI-Generated WordPress Page**

Following the customization workflow helps ensure that you select a supported element, review the result, and save the change correctly. You can repeat the process for different text and image elements across the page.

### 

### **Step 1: Open the AI-Generated Page**

1. Go to **Sites > WordPress > All Sites**.
2. Open the appropriate WordPress site.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/NOJVS6j7u7CmuYxRCc2Y+/1+%283%29+%281%29.png)
3. Go to **Pages**.
4. Open the AI-generated page you want to customize.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/RBGYgCtLBjdkbOYLGFXg+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-13+at+17.41.58.png)

### **Step 2: Select a Supported Element**

1. Move your cursor over the page preview.
2. Hover over the text or image you want to change.
3. Click the supported element.
4. The **Customizations** panel opens on the right.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080004243/original/w6eVcdzdgegD7jzjP8PF_TFa1xZNTiUHPA.jpeg?1788436126)**

### 

### **Step 3: Edit the Content**

For text:

1. Update the content manually, or select an AI-assisted option.
2. Use **Rephrase**, **Shorten**, or **Elaborate** if you want HighLevel to generate a revised version.
3. Use **Change Tone** when you want to adjust how the content sounds.
4. Review the result.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080003791/original/5CTyuUvyDkPSkqIYS4O2RbihMA51PYvgDA.png?1788435859)**

### 

### **Step 4: Customize Images if Needed**

To replace a supported image:

1. Hover over the image in the page preview.
2. Click **Regenerate Image**.
3. Select **Generate with AI** to create a new image or **Upload image** to use an existing file.
4. Generate or upload the replacement image.
5. Review the result in **Live preview**.
6. Click **Insert image**.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/6ErmsL5E3n9XlglCdGLL+/GIF+Recording+2026-10-13+at+16.46.17.gif)

### **Step 5: Save the Changes**

Click **Save Changes** when the page looks correct.

Your saved updates are applied to the WordPress page.

### **Step 6: Use Elementor for Additional Changes**

If you need editing options that are not available in the HighLevel preview, click **Edit on Elementor** and continue customizing the page there.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/YSEA5cS1wHmCTLNJ1nWV+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-13+at+17.36.30.png)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I edit every element on an AI-generated WordPress page?**  
No. Universal Content Customization applies to supported elements. If an element cannot be selected or customized from the HighLevel preview, use Elementor for additional editing.

**Q: Do I still need Elementor?**  
Not for many routine content changes. You can update supported text and images directly in HighLevel, but Elementor remains available for advanced layout, styling, and unsupported elements.

**Q: What plugin version do I need?**  
Universal Content Customization requires **LeadConnector WordPress Plugin v4.0.4 or later**.

**Q: Why do I not see the customization controls?**

Confirm that you are working with a supported AI-generated WordPress page and that the LeadConnector WordPress Plugin is on the required version or later.

**Q: Can I change the tone of generated content?**  
Yes. Supported text can use tone options such as Professional, Friendly, Compelling, and Confident.

**Q: Can I regenerate only one image?**

Yes. Supported AI-generated images can be regenerated individually without rebuilding the entire page.

**Q: What is the difference between Preview Changes and Save Changes?**  
Preview lets you review the updated page before finalizing your edits, while Save Changes applies your customization.

**Q: Can I continue editing the page in Elementor afterward?**  
Yes. The generated WordPress page can still be opened and edited in Elementor.

**Q: Can I upload my own images instead of using AI-generated images?**

Yes. Select a supported image, click **Regenerate Image**, and choose **Upload image**. You can upload JPEG, PNG, WebP, or GIF files up to 10 MB. Review the uploaded image before inserting it into the page.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [WordPress - AI-Powered Page Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007585)
- [How to Setup WordPress for Clients](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001199648-getting-started-with-wordpress-client-side-setup-guide)
- [WordPress - LeadConnector Plugin Hub](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008424-wordpress-leadconnector-plugin-hub)

title_en: Voice AI Performance Reports
source_md:
Voice AI Performance Reports give you an automated email summary of how each Voice AI agent is performing over time. Instead of checking dashboards manually, you can receive scheduled reports with key call metrics, caller sentiment, actions taken, after-hours activity, and flagged calls that may need review. Reports are configured per agent, giving teams flexibility to choose different frequencies and recipients for each Voice AI agent.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Voice AI Performance Reports?](#What-is-Voice-AI-Performance-Reports?)
- [Key Benefits of Voice AI Performance Reports](#Key-Benefits-of-Voice-AI-Performance-Reports)
- [What’s Included in a Voice AI Performance Report?](#What%E2%80%99s-Included-in-a-Voice-AI-Performance-Report?)
- [Report Frequency Options](#Report-Frequency-Options)
- [Report Recipient Options](#Report-Recipient-Options)
- [Call Anomalies and Deep Links](#Call-Anomalies-and-Deep-Links)
- [How To Setup Voice AI Performance Reports](#How-To-Setup-Voice-AI-Performance-Reports)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Voice AI Performance Reports?**

Voice AI Performance Reports are scheduled email summaries that help you monitor Voice AI agent performance without needing to manually review reporting dashboards. Each report provides a periodic snapshot of call activity, quality signals, caller outcomes, and automation activity for a specific Voice AI agent.

Voice AI agents can already be reviewed through in-app dashboards, logs, and call records in HighLevel. Performance Reports add an email-based layer for teams that want recurring visibility into agent performance, call trends, and calls that may need follow-up review. The Voice AI Agents Dashboard article covers in-app analytics for call performance, sentiment, and triggered actions, while Agent Logs and Call Logs provide deeper call-level review options.

---

## **Key Benefits of Voice AI Performance Reports**

Performance Reports help teams stay informed about Voice AI activity by sending important metrics directly to the right people. This makes it easier to identify trends, review customer experience signals, and monitor automation outcomes without manually checking each agent.

- **Automated Visibility:** Receive recurring performance summaries by email for each Voice AI agent.
- **Flexible Reporting Cadence:**Choose Weekly, Fortnightly, or Monthly reports based on how often each agent needs to be reviewed.
- **Agent Level Control:**Configure report frequency and recipients independently for each Voice AI agent.
- **Caller Experience Tracking:**Review positive, neutral, and negative caller sentiment trends over time.
- **Operational Insights:**See after-hours calls, action counts, and period-over-period changes in one summary.
- **Faster Call Review:** Use flagged call links to quickly investigate negative sentiment or unexpectedly short calls.
- **Cleaner Inboxes:**Reports are skipped automatically for periods with zero calls.

---

## **What’s Included in a Voice AI Performance Report?**

Each Voice AI Performance Report gives you a clear summary of activity for the selected reporting period. These metrics help you understand call volume, call quality, customer sentiment, and how often the agent completed important actions.

A report may include the following information:

- **Total Calls:**The number of calls handled by the Voice AI agent during the reporting period.
- **Total Call Duration:**The combined duration of all calls included in the report.
- **Average Call Duration:** The average length of calls during the reporting period.
- **Success Rate:** A summary indicator showing how successfully the agent handled calls during the period.
- **Caller Sentiment:** A positive, neutral, and negative breakdown to help track caller experience.
- **After Hours Calls:**The number of calls received outside business hours, based on the agent’s configured timezone.
- **Action Breakdown:**Counts for key actions such as SMS sent, call transfers, workflows triggered, appointments booked, and custom actions executed.
- **Period Over Period Comparison:**Percentage changes compared with the previous reporting period.
- **Call Anomalies:**Up to three flagged calls, such as calls with negative sentiment or unexpectedly short duration, with deep links back into HighLevel for review.

---

## **Report Frequency Options**

Choosing the right frequency helps your team receive performance insights at the right pace. High-volume agents may need weekly review, while lower-volume or stable agents may only need monthly summaries.

Voice AI Performance Reports can be sent on one of the following cadences:

- Weekly
- Fortnightly
- Monthly

Each Voice AI agent can have its own reporting frequency. For example, one agent can send a weekly report to operations managers, while another agent sends a monthly report to business stakeholders.

---

## **Report Recipient Options**

Recipient settings let you decide who should receive each agent’s report. This is useful when different teams, managers, clients, or external stakeholders need visibility into specific Voice AI agents.

You can send reports to:

- All Admins of the location
- All Users of the location
- A list of specific users
- Custom email addresses

Custom email addresses are useful for stakeholders who need report visibility but may not be standard users inside the sub-account.

```
Receiving an email report does not always mean the recipient can access linked in-app call details. Access to Voice AI settings, dashboards, logs, or call records may depend on the user’s HighLevel permissions. HighLevel’s Voice AI permission controls are covered in the Managing Granular Permissions for Voice AI Agents article.
```

---

## **Call Anomalies and Deep Links**

Call anomalies help teams quickly identify conversations that may need closer review. Instead of reading through every call, you can start with flagged calls that may indicate a poor caller experience, an incomplete interaction, or a call that ended earlier than expected.

Each report can include up to three flagged calls. These may include:

- Calls with negative caller sentiment
- Calls that were unexpectedly short

Use the deep links in the report to open the related call details in HighLevel and review what happened. For deeper troubleshooting, use Voice AI Agent Logs or Call Logs to inspect call details, transcripts, summaries, actions, transfers, and other interaction history.

---

## **How To Setup Voice AI Performance Reports**

Proper setup ensures the right people receive the right report at the right time. Because Performance Reports are configured per agent, each Voice AI agent must be updated individually with its own frequency and recipient settings.

1. Go to Agency View in HighLevel. Open Labs. Turn on Voice AI Performance Reports.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071657050/original/iYbLmclfFJQIVAcB0q30tkaG5g9OJQpfRw.png?1779185680)
2. Open the sub-account where the Voice AI agent is configured.
3. Go to Voice AI.
4. Open the Voice AI agent you want to configure.
5. Select Performance Report Settings.
6. Choose the report frequency:  
     
   - Weekly
   - Fortnightly
   - Monthly  
       
       
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071657241/original/Z8MOvuNPNbDUBPhH41X3zMKDruog56d0Lg.png?1779185783)
7. Choose who should receive the report:  
     
   - All Admins of the location
   - All Users of the location
   - Specific users
   - Custom email addresses  
       
       
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071657334/original/VDRvvF7cziL0Bg8BrXOn9OoO1chwcU0ofA.png?1779185818)
8. Save the report settings.

```
The first report will arrive at the start of the next reporting period. Reports are skipped automatically for periods where the agent has zero calls.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Is Voice AI Performance Reports available for all accounts?**  
A: Voice AI Performance Reports is currently available through Labs. The feature must be enabled from Labs in Agency View before it can be configured for Voice AI agents.

**Q: Why did I not receive a report for my Voice AI agent?**  
A: Reports are skipped automatically for periods with zero calls. If the agent did not handle any calls during the reporting period, no report is sent.

**Q: Can different Voice AI agents have different report settings?**  
A: Yes. Each Voice AI agent is configured independently, so you can use different frequencies and recipient lists for each agent.

**Q: Can I send reports to people who are not HighLevel users?**  
A: Yes. You can add custom email addresses as recipients, which is useful for external stakeholders.

**Q: Can custom email recipients open the deep links in the report?**A: They may receive the email, but access to linked call details in HighLevel may require the correct user access and permissions.

**Q: What timezone is used in the report?**A: Report times respect the Voice AI agent’s configured timezone.

**Q: What types of calls can be flagged as anomalies?**A: Reports can flag calls with negative sentiment or unexpectedly short duration, helping your team quickly review conversations that may need attention.

**Q: Can I change report recipients after saving the settings?**A: Yes. Open the agent’s Performance Report Settings, update the recipients, and save the changes.

---

title_en: Overview of Ad Manager
source_md:
Ad Manager in HighLevel is a centralized tool that allows agencies and sub-accounts to create, manage, and track advertising campaigns across multiple platforms in one place.

It simplifies digital advertising by consolidating workflows, providing actionable insights, and helping agencies deliver measurable results to their clients.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Ad Manager?](#What-is-Ad-Manager?)
- [Supported Platforms and Campaign Types](#Supported-Platforms-and-Campaign-Types)
- [What You Can Do with Ad Manager](#What-You-Can-Do-with-Ad-Manager)
- [Key Benefits of Ad Manager](#Key-Benefits-of-Ad-Manager)
- [Pricing & Access](#Pricing-&-Access)
- [How to Set Up Ad Manager](#How-to-Set-Up-Ad-Manager)
- [How to Create a Meta Business Portfolio](#How-to-Create-a-Meta-Business-Portfolio)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Ad Manager?**

Ad Manager brings **Facebook, Instagram, Google, and LinkedIn** Ads together into one easy-to-use dashboard.

Instead of switching between different ad platforms, users can create campaigns, track performance, and optimize results — directly within HighLevel. This saves time, reduces complexity, and makes professional advertising accessible for businesses of all sizes.

Ad Manager enables both agencies and sub-accounts to run high-performing campaigns and analyze performance without leaving the HighLevel platform.

---

## **Supported Platforms and Campaign Types**

Ad Manager supports multiple platforms and ad types. The table below outlines what objectives and formats are available on each platform.

| **Platform** | **Campaign Objectives** | **Ad Formats Supported** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Meta (Facebook & Instagram)** | Lead Generation, Website Traffic, Engagement, Sales | Single Image, Video, Carousel (up to 10), Lead Forms, Conversation Forms |
| **Google Ads** | Search Campaigns, Demand Generation *(coming soon)* | Search Ads, Image, Video, Carousel (Demand Gen) |
| **LinkedIn Ads** | Lead Generation, Website Visits | Single Image, Video, Carousel, Lead Forms |

---

## **What You Can Do with Ad Manager**

Ad Manager brings campaign creation, management, and reporting tools into HighLevel. The table below provides an overview of its key capabilities.

| **Capability** | **What You Can Do** |
| --- | --- |
| **Multi-Platform Ad Management** | Create and manage supported advertising campaigns across Meta (Facebook and Instagram), Google, and LinkedIn from within HighLevel. |
| **Campaign Creation** | Build campaigns using supported objectives and configure campaign settings such as audience targeting, budget, schedule, and ad creatives. |
| **Audience Targeting** | Configure supported targeting options to reach relevant audiences based on the selected advertising platform and campaign type. |
| **Campaign Templates** | Use reusable campaign templates to streamline campaign creation and reduce repetitive setup. |
| **Campaign Management** | Manage supported campaigns from HighLevel and make changes without having to handle every campaign task directly within each advertising platform. |
| **Performance Reporting** | Monitor campaign metrics such as impressions, clicks, conversions, and spend from the Ad Manager dashboard. |
| **Campaign Review and Optimization** | Review campaign performance and use available insights and recommendations to identify opportunities for improvement. |
| **AskAI for Ad Manager** | Use conversational AI for supported advertising workflows, including campaign creation, management, and performance analysis. |
| **Ad Manager APIs** | Use available APIs to build automated campaign management, integration, and reporting workflows. |
| **Agency and Sub-Account Management** | Enable agencies and sub-accounts to manage advertising workflows within HighLevel while agencies oversee access across client accounts. |

---

## **Key Benefits of Ad Manager**

Ad Manager provides powerful advantages for both agencies and sub-accounts by simplifying campaign execution, improving transparency, and enabling measurable results.

- **All-in-One Advertising:** Manage campaigns across Facebook, Instagram, Google, and LinkedIn from a single dashboard.

- **Time-Saving Workflows:** Guided setup helps users launch ads quickly and efficiently.

- **Simplified Targeting:** Reach the right audience through goal-based campaign objectives.

- **Clear ROI:** Gain instant visibility into ad performance, spend, and conversion metrics.

- **Outcome-Focused:** Run lead generation, traffic, or conversion campaigns that drive tangible business results.

- **Operational Efficiency for Agencies:** Manage multiple clients’ campaigns seamlessly.

- **Resell Opportunity:** Agencies can monetize Ad Manager access by offering it to sub-accounts as a value-added service.

---

## **Pricing & Access**

Ad Manager is available **free for agencies**, giving them flexibility to **resell access** to sub-accounts and create new revenue opportunities.

### **Key Details**

- **Agencies:** Ad Manager access is included at no cost.

- **Sub-Accounts:** Agencies can choose to resell access and set their own pricing.

- **Profit Control:** Whatever price the agency sets becomes its profit — HighLevel’s base cost is always $0.

Agencies can manage Ad Manager availability and pricing in three places:

- **Agency → Reselling Tab** – Define default pricing for all sub-accounts.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056046834/original/CyBFXGqxbxRq0qYqbhElmZwnG1ZJTUdfeQ.png?1760529160)

- **Sub-Account → Reselling Tab** – Set or override pricing individually.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056046255/original/6-3sO3HsNugtOa3A5Otms4MDQ_q75qY5Xg.png?1760528884)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056046315/original/bZ6sbiCBPgXqv3XE5PQ2dVnLbkdON5SCFw.png?1760528919)

- **SaaS Configurator → Features Tab** – Include Ad Manager as part of a SaaS plan.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056046350/original/hMjcLn5k7DfdcknJzvpl3C1qFt5AhMPlXg.png?1760528939)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056046371/original/ZKhSUujB6XYpKK_iQ8LoH0HcNQIF_jJjCw.png?1760528964)

---

## **How to Set Up Ad Manager**

Follow these steps to set up Ad Manager and start running campaigns:

**Access Ad Manager:**

From your HighLevel dashboard, navigate to **Marketing → Ad Manager**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056046202/original/eEM9a6YJnB7QmmkWTKKstaj2q3xRvVPjWQ.png?1760528861)

### **Connect Ad Accounts:**

Click **Connect Accounts** and follow the prompts to link your Facebook, Instagram, Google, or LinkedIn Ads account.

### **Set Permissions**

Ensure correct permissions are granted for creating and managing campaigns.

### **Create a Campaign**

Choose the platform (Facebook, Instagram, Google, or LinkedIn). Define your campaign objective (e.g., Awareness, Traffic, Conversions, or Lead Generation). Set audience targeting, budget, and schedule.

### **Monitor Results**

Track performance metrics such as impressions, clicks, conversions, and spend in the Ad Manager dashboard.

## 

### **Get Started with Ad Manager**

Ready to start using Ad Manager? Learn how to enable Ad Manager for sub-accounts, configure access, and set up reselling options with our step-by-step guide [How to Enable and Resell Ad Manager.](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004261-how-to-enable-and-resell-ad-manager)

---

## **How to Create a Meta Business Portfolio**

To connect Facebook to HighLevel Ad Manager, you need access to a Meta Business Portfolio (formerly Business Manager), a Meta ads account, and a Facebook Page.

If you do not have a Meta Business Portfolio, follow Meta’s official guide to create one. Meta manages the Business Portfolio creation process, and the setup experience may change over time. For the latest steps, refer to[Create a business portfolio in Meta Business Suite.](https://business.facebook.com/business/help/1710077379203657?id=180505742745347&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Once created, make sure the required Facebook Page and ads account are added and that you have the appropriate access.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do agencies pay for Ad Manager?**

No. Agencies get free access to Ad Manager. They may choose to resell it to sub-accounts.

**Q: What platforms are supported in Ad Manager?**

Currently supported platforms are **Facebook, Instagram, Google, and LinkedIn Ads**.

**Q: Can agencies set their own pricing for sub-accounts?**

Yes. Agencies can define pricing in the Reselling tab, Sub-Account Reselling tab, or SaaS Configurator.

**Q: Where can sub-accounts see their reports?**

All performance reports are available within the Ad Manager dashboard in real-time.

**Q: Do sub-accounts provide their own ad budgets?**

Yes. Each sub-account is responsible for its own ad spend budget.

---

## **Related Articles**
